His box is like a mobile intelligence station of the city: the orders record the tastes of the district, and the notes hide the daily rhythms of countless families. That day he ran from ten in the morning to nine at night, forty orders in all. First, he remembered each building's "shortcut": the fire stairs of Building Three were two minutes faster than the lift. Second, the most touching thing was a sheet of paper pasted inside the lid with the special notes for six orders: the old man in 301 should be answered by knocking, not the bell; the order at the kindergarten gate should be left with the gatekeeper. Master Wang calls these "addresses more important than addresses". On the day of the presentation, someone asked what my conclusion was. I said: the city writes efficiency into its algorithms, and writes human warmth on the inside of a box lid — and what decides the temperature of a city is usually the part written inside the lid.

lessons.chinese: 高考结束那天，我把三年的错题本搬去晒太阳。五本，七百多页，从三角函数到文言虚词，从第一次月考到最后一次模拟。翻着翻着，我发现错题本其实是另一种日记。第三本的空白处还留着一行批语，是数学老师的字：“这道题我再讲一遍，收你一颗糖。”第五本的第43页有一大片水渍——那是高三一个失利的下午，我掉了几滴不争气的眼泪。物理老师说过：错题不是你的敌人清单，而是你的私人地图——它标出的，全是你曾经到不了的地方。晒完太阳，我把本子装进箱子，写上“大学再翻”，因为我肯定还会在新地方摔跤。旧地图的价值在于提醒我：所有走不通的路，当时都走通过一次——用错误的方式。
lessons.english: On the day the college entrance examination ended, I carried my three years of mistake notebooks out into the sun. Five volumes, more than seven hundred pages in all — from trigonometry to classical Chinese particles, from the first monthly test to the last mock examination. Turning the pages, I found that a mistake book is another kind of diary. On the blank page of the third volume there is a note in the maths teacher's hand: "I will explain it once more, and charge you one candy." On page 43 of the fifth volume there is a large water stain — from an afternoon in Senior Three when I failed a test and shed a few unwise tears. Our physics teacher once said that a mistake book is not a list of your enemies but your private map — everything it marks is a place where you once could not arrive. I packed the notebooks into a box and wrote on it, "to be reopened at university", for I shall surely stumble in new places, and the value of an old map is its reminder: every road that could not be walked was once walked through — in the wrong way.

lessons.chinese: 填志愿的那个夏天，我把自己关在房间里三天。桌上摊着两份材料：计算机专业的录取概率，和我偷偷画了六年的素描册。所有人都说，选稳的。第三天傍晚，爷爷来敲门。他没讲大道理，只讲了一件事：退休后，他办了平生第一次画展。他说：“我这辈子没敢换路，所以我特别想知道，走另一条路的人后来怎么样了。”那天晚上，我把两份材料并排摆着看了很久，最后在素描册的最后一页写下一行字：计算机我照学，素描我照画，两条路的中间站着一个活人，别把他挤没了。后来我如愿读了计算机，画笔也没停。那条“中间的路”不好走，但走到今天，我可以回答爷爷了：走两条路的人后来怎么样了？——他们累，但他们没把自己弄丢。
lessons.english: In the summer of my university choices, I shut myself in my room for three days. On the desk lay two sets of papers: the admission odds for a computer-science major, and a sketchbook kept in secret for six years. Everyone said, choose the safe one. On the third evening, Grandpa knocked at my door. He preached no big principles; he told one story. After retiring he held the first exhibition of his life. He said: "I never dared change roads in my whole life. That is why I am so curious about those who took the other one. " That night I laid the two sets of papers side by side, and at last wrote on the last page of the sketchbook: I will study computers as planned, and I will keep drawing as planned; between the two roads stands a living person — do not squeeze him out of existence. Later I was admitted to computer science, and the brush never stopped. That middle road is not easy; but having walked this far, I can answer Grandpa's question: the person who walks two roads is tired — but he has not lost himself.

lessons.chinese: 家里最旧的一本书，是一本1998年版的袖珍英汉词典。它属于爸爸，封面用牛皮纸包着，边角磨出了毛絮。爸爸说，那是他大学时用三个月家教钱买的，全班只有三个人有词典。书里到处是他的笔迹：生词画着圈，旁边注着土办法，“danger”旁边还画了个小骷髅。我上高二时开始用它。起初我把它当老古董；后来发现它比任何新版都好用——爸爸画圈的地方，是他当年没记住的词，而他没记住的，多半也是难点。于是一圈圈笔迹成了路标。妈妈说该换本新的了。我没换，因为旧书里住着一个二十岁的年轻人，他正隔着二十多年，陪他女儿背同一个单词——这种陪读，新版给不了。
lessons.english: The oldest book in our home is a small English-Chinese dictionary of the 1998 edition. It belonged to Dad, and its cover, wrapped in kraft paper, has worn into fuzzy tufts at the corners. Dad said he bought it with three months of tutoring money in his university years, when only three people in the class owned a dictionary. His handwriting is everywhere in the book: new words are circled, and beside them stand notes in his homemade style — next to "danger" he drew a tiny skull. I began using this dictionary in Senior Two. At first I treated it as a relic; later I found it more useful than any new edition — wherever Dad had drawn a circle was a word he had failed to remember then, and the words he failed to remember are mostly the hard ones too. So his circles of ink became signposts. Mum said it was time to buy a new dictionary. I did not change it, for in the old one lives a twenty-year-old young man who, across more than twenty years, is keeping his daughter company over the very same words — a kind of company no new edition can offer.

lessons.title_en: A Spring Festival Guide for My Pen Pal
lessons.chinese:
亲爱的艾玛：你说你二月要来中国过春节，还问我该准备什么。你最关心的问题的答案是：会冷，请带上你最厚的外套。再给你三条“生存指南”。第一，年夜饭不要吃太饱；春节是一部从除夕播到元宵的连续剧，你得为第二集留着胃口。第二，红包当面拆是失礼的，回家再拆，惊喜和礼貌都保住了。第三，如果有人劝你喝酒，你可以说医生不许可；这句话是中国餐桌上的万能钥匙。最后，除夕夜记得抬头看烟花。我们小镇还允许放，我会带你去河堤，在那里能看见三个镇的烟花同时升起。期待二月。
你的朋友
小雨
lessons.english: Dear Emma, You wrote that you are coming to China in February for the Spring Festival and asked what you should prepare. The answer to the question you care about most: it will be cold, so bring your thickest coat. Now let me give you three rules of survival. First, do not eat too much at the New Year's Eve dinner; the Spring Festival is a television series that runs from New Year's Eve to the Lantern Festival, and you will need your appetite for the second episode. Second, opening a red envelope in front of the giver is bad manners; open it at home, and you keep both the surprise and the courtesy. Third, if someone urges you to drink, you may say that your doctor does not allow it; this sentence is a master key on the Chinese dinner table. Finally, on New Year's Eve remember to look up at the fireworks. Our little town still allows them, and I will take you to the river bank, from where you can see the fireworks of three towns rising at the same time. Looking forward to February.

lessons.title_en: A Lesson in Economics at the School Flea Market
lessons.chinese: 上周六，学校办了第一届跳蚤市场，规则只有一条：不许定价高于原价的一半。我摆摊卖掉了四年的漫画和一批贴纸，净赚八十七元，但比赚钱更有意思的是观察定价。下午两点，我的漫画无人问津，隔壁摊位的钢琴谱却卖疯了。后来我看到他们的招牌：“全部五元，买三送一。”真正的高潮发生在收摊前一小时。有位初一学弟看中我一套绝版漫画，问能不能便宜点。我心中暗喜，正要讨价还价，他忽然从书包里掏出一本我初一丢的笔记。“我知道这是你的，”他说。“我一直想还你，今天特地带来的。”结果你猜怎么着：全套漫画我送了他，一分没收。价格可以计算，但市场上流动的东西，从来不止是价格：那本笔记回来的一刻，跳蚤市场变成了一场重逢。
lessons.english: Last Saturday our school held its first flea market, where nothing could be priced above half the original cost. I sold the comic books of four years and a batch of stickers, earning eighty-seven yuan — but more interesting than the money was the observation of pricing. At two in the afternoon not a soul looked at my comics, while the piano scores at the next stall were selling like crazy. Then I saw their signboard: "Everything five yuan; buy three, get one free." The real climax came in the final hour. A Junior One boy took a fancy to a set of out-of-print comics of mine and asked whether the price could come down. Secretly delighted, I was about to bargain, when he suddenly drew from his schoolbag a notebook that I had lost in Junior One. "I knew it was yours," he said. "I have always wanted to return it, and today I brought it on purpose." Guess what: I gave him the whole set and took not a cent. Prices can be calculated, but what flows through a market has never been prices alone: at the moment that notebook came home, the flea market turned into a reunion.

lessons.chinese: 历史社团这学期的课题是三星堆。去省博看展前，老师让我们先回答一个问题：面对一个没有文字、没有史料支持的文明，我们能知道什么？展厅里，青铜大立人双手环握，手里原本握着什么，无人知晓——这个空白，竟让三千年后的人争论不休。带队老师却说：“空白也是一种表达。”她的意思是，铜尊的纹路、玉璋的刻痕、祭祀坑的层位，都是表达——只是需要另一种阅读。后来我们写了八千字的报告，结论只有一页：关于三星堆，我们能确定的是它有多么不确定。老师给我们的评语是：“这是考古学最诚实的答案。”那学期的活动让我养成了一个习惯：遇到言之凿凿的说法，先问一句——证据的坑挖到哪一层了？
lessons.english: This term the history club took Sanxingdui as its project. Before we visited the exhibition at the provincial museum, the teacher asked us to answer a question first: facing a civilisation with no writing and no written records, what can we actually know? In the hall, the great bronze standing figure holds its hands in a ring; what they once held nobody knows, and this blank has kept people arguing for three thousand years. Our teacher, however, said: "A blank is also a form of expression." Her meaning was that the patterns on the bronze vessels, the carvings on the jade tablets, and the layers of the sacrifice pits are all expressions too — only they need to be read in another way. In the end we wrote a report of eight thousand words, and the conclusion filled a single page: about Sanxingdui, the one thing we can be sure of is how unsure it is. Our teacher's comment read: "This is the most honest answer that archaeology can give." The club left me with a habit: whenever I meet an assertion made with complete confidence, I ask first — to which layer of the evidence has the digging reached?

lessons.title_en: Ten Thousand Metres under the Stars
lessons.chinese: 科技馆的深海展厅里，有一台一万米级载人潜水器的模型。讲解员说，人类登月的次数比下潜到马里亚纳海沟底的次数还多。我将信将疑，回家查了资料，竟然是真的：迄今只有寥寥数人到过那片一万多米深的海底，而在月球上留下脚印的已有十二人。为什么下潜比登天难？第一，压强：万米深处的压强约是一千一百个大气压，相当于每平方厘米压着一辆小轿车。第二，黑暗与低温：阳光在一百米以下就基本消失了，那里的水温常年两度左右。展厅尽头有一面屏幕，循环播放深海的实景：探照灯之外是一片绝对的黑暗，偶尔有发光的生物漂过，像流动的星星。原来这颗星球上真的还有仰望不到的星空——它不在头顶，而在我们脚下，安安静静，从未被打扰。
lessons.english: In the deep-sea hall of the science museum stands a model of a manned submersible rated for ten thousand metres. The guide said that human beings have landed on the moon more often than they have descended to the bottom of the Mariana Trench. I half doubted the claim and checked at home — it is true: only a handful of people have ever reached that seabed eleven thousand metres down, while twelve have left footprints on the moon. Why is diving harder than flying to the sky? First, pressure: at ten thousand metres it is about eleven hundred atmospheres — as if a small car were standing on every square centimetre. Second, darkness and cold: sunlight nearly vanishes below one hundred metres, and the water there stays at about two degrees all year. At the end of the hall a screen plays real footage of the deep sea: beyond the searchlights lies absolute darkness, with a glowing creature drifting past now and then, like a moving star. It turns out that on this very planet there is a sky of stars that no night lets us see — it is not above our heads, but below our feet, quiet and never disturbed.

lessons.chinese: 航天科普讲座上，工程师放过一段视频：火箭点火后四十秒偏离轨道，随后自毁。真正让他记一辈子的，是事后开会时总工程师的那句开场话：“数据都在，人都在，我们重新来。”他没有责怪任何人——因为事后查明，问题出在一个批次密封圈的材料上，而验收记录完全合规。“合规不等于正确，”工程师说。“那一刻所有人都按规矩办事，可规矩里有一个我们当时看不见的坑。”他想了想，说：“看不见的坑没法避免，能避免的是掉进去之后爬不出来。所以我们的数据库里，失败记录比成功记录详细十倍。”一个只庆祝成功的团队，等于把最贵的老师傅关在门外；而肯给失败立传的组织，才养得出真正的工程师。
lessons.english: At a lecture on space science, an engineer played a video: forty seconds after ignition, a rocket deviated from its trajectory and then destroyed itself. What he will remember all his life, however, was the chief engineer's first sentence at the meeting afterwards: "The data are all here, the people are all here — we will start again." He blamed nobody, for the investigation later showed that the problem lay in the material of one batch of seal rings, while every acceptance record was in perfect order. "Being compliant is not the same as being right," the engineer said. "At that moment everyone followed the rules, yet there was a pit in the rules that we could not see at the time." He thought for a moment and said: "Invisible pits cannot be avoided; what can be avoided is the failure to climb out after falling in. That is why in our database the records of failure are ten times more detailed than the records of success." A team that celebrates only success shuts its most expensive old master outside the door; and it is organisations willing to write biographies for their failures that raise real engineers.

lessons.chinese: 高三教学楼有个传统：高考倒计时牌翻到一百天那天，全校高三学生会在操场上走一圈“成人路”。今年轮到我们。一百天，说长不长。数学老师算了笔账：每天弄懂一道错题，一百天就是一百道，足够覆盖近五年的高频考点。他顿了顿，又补了一句：“这一百道题，就是一百级台阶。”仪式本身很简单：走一圈，喊一次年级口号，然后回教室继续刷题。走到第三圈的时候，我听见旁边同学在小声背古文，另一边有人在讨论压轴题的解法。那一刻我忽然觉得，一百天不是倒计时，而是正着数的：一天，多一点确定。路的尽头不叫奇迹，叫水到渠成。
lessons.english: There is a tradition in the building of Senior Three: on the day when the college-entrance countdown board is turned to one hundred days, all Senior Three students walk one circle around the playground on a "road of adulthood". This year it is our turn. A hundred days is not long. Our maths teacher worked out one account: if you truly understand one wrong problem every day, a hundred days give you a hundred problems — enough to cover the high-frequency exam topics of the past five years. He paused, and added one line: "Those hundred problems are a hundred steps." The ceremony itself was simple: one circle, one grade slogan, and then back to the classroom to keep solving problems. As I walked the third circle, I heard a classmate quietly reciting classical prose nearby, while on the other side two students were discussing how to attack the hardest final problem. In that moment I suddenly felt that the hundred days are not a countdown but a count upward: one day, one grain more of certainty. The end of the road is not called a miracle; it is called water finding its channel.

lessons.title_en: The Old Blackboard in the Office
lessons.chinese: 高三最后一个学期，班主任换了间办公室。搬东西那天，我们在角落里发现一块小黑板，边框锈了，板面只擦了一半。他本来要扔，被我们拦下了。后来我们才知道它的来历：十几年前，班上有个学生家境困难，晚上要帮家里看摊，跟不上进度。那个学生后来考上了师范大学，如今也成了老师。我们追问：那个人在哪儿？他笑而不答。他只是把黑板擦干净，挂在新办公室最显眼的墙上，旁边贴了一张便利贴，写着这块小黑板的“使用说明”：不讲新课，只讲卡住的那一步。直到那时，我们才明白——那块黑板从来不是教具，它是一张随时有效的课堂门票。
lessons.english: In the last term of Senior Three, our head teacher moved to a new office. On the day he carried his things, we found a small blackboard in a corner: its frame rusted and its face half wiped. He meant to throw it out, but we stopped him. Later we learned its story. More than a decade ago there was a student in his class whose family was in hardship: at night he had to mind the family's street stall and fell behind in his studies. That student later entered a normal university and is now a teacher himself. We pressed further: where is that student now? He smiled and answered nothing. He simply wiped the board clean and hung it on the most prominent wall of his new office, pasting a sticky note beside it — the "instructions for use" of one small blackboard: it teaches no new lessons, only the step at which you are stuck. Only then did we understand — that blackboard was never a teaching aid; it was a ticket to the classroom, valid at any time.

lessons.title_en: After Walking out of the Exam Hall
lessons.chinese: 最后一科结束的铃声响起时，我的手还悬在半空，笔尖离纸一厘米。然后人群涌动，我随着人流走出考场，站在校门口，忽然不知道该往哪儿走。三年来，一切都替我安排得明明白白：上课的时间、考试的时间、考试的范围。我掏出手机，给妈妈发消息：考完了。过了一会儿，她回了四个字：“回家吃饭。”就在这四个字里，鼻子忽然一酸。走出考场之后我明白的第一件事是：高考不是终点线，它是一条换气管——把三年的憋气呼出去，把往后自己的路吸进来。第二件事是：晚自习传过的纸条、跑操时喊哑的嗓子、办公室门口的欲言又止——它们不参加考试，却组成了全部。路还长，但今晚，先回家吃饭。
lessons.english: When the bell of the final subject rang, my hand was still hanging in the air, the tip of my pen one centimetre from the paper. Then the crowd surged, and I flowed out of the exam hall with the stream of people, stood at the school gate, and suddenly did not know where to go. For three years everything had been arranged for me: class times, exam times, and their ranges. I took out my phone and texted Mum: done. After a while she replied with four words: "Come home for dinner." In those four words my nose suddenly stung. The first thing I understood after walking out of the exam hall was this: the examination is not a finishing line; it is a change of air — breathing out three years of held breath, and breathing in the road that belongs to me from now on. The second thing was this: the notes passed during evening study, the voices shouted hoarse at morning exercises, the half-spoken words at the office door — they never sat for an examination, yet they make up the whole of it. The road is still long; but tonight, first, home for dinner.

lessons.chinese: 过去十年，移动支付深刻改变了中国人的日常生活。支付宝、微信支付等平台让用户用一部智能手机就能支付几乎所有消费，从菜市场的蔬菜到高铁票。据官方报告，中国移动支付的交易规模已居世界第一。在大城市，许多商店不再收取现金，连街头艺人的琴盒上也贴着二维码。移动支付的普及很大程度上得益于智能手机的普及和网络条件的改善。它让消费更加快捷，降低了交易成本，也推动传统商户走向数字化。与此同时，它也带来了新的挑战，例如个人信息保护和老年用户的需求。许多社区现在开设了专门的课程，帮助老年人学会在线支付。移动支付不只是一样新工具，它是一扇窗，世界透过它观察中国的数字生活。
lessons.english: Over the past decade, mobile payment has transformed the daily life of Chinese people. Platforms such as Alipay and WeChat Pay allow users to pay for almost everything with a smartphone, from vegetables at a market to high-speed rail tickets. According to official reports, the transaction volume of mobile payment in China now ranks first in the world. In large cities, many shops no longer accept cash, and even street performers display QR codes on their boxes. The popularity of mobile payment owes much to the spread of smartphones and the improvement of networks. It has made consumption faster, reduced the cost of transactions, and pushed traditional businesses to go digital. At the same time, it has raised new challenges, such as the protection of personal information and the needs of elderly users. Many communities now offer special courses to help older people learn to pay online. Mobile payment is more than a new tool; it is a window through which the world can observe the digital life of China.

lessons.chinese: 中国的高速铁路网络是世界上规模最大的。截至目前，高铁运营里程已超过四万公里，连接了全国大部分大中城市。乘坐高铁从北京到上海只需四个半小时，而过去乘普通火车需要近十个小时。高铁不仅缩短了城市之间的距离，也改变了许多人的生活方式。人们可以在另一座城市工作，周末再回家与家人团聚。高铁还带动了沿线地区的经济发展，许多小城市因为通高铁而迎来了游客和投资。当然，建设和维护这样一张网络需要巨额资金和先进技术。工程师们克服了地质复杂、气候多变等困难，才让列车以每小时三百五十公里的速度安全行驶。如今，高铁已经成为中国制造的一张名片，也成为许多外国游客体验现代中国的第一站。
lessons.english: China operates the largest high-speed rail network in the world. So far, the total length of lines in service has exceeded forty thousand kilometres, connecting most large and medium-sized cities across the country. The journey from Beijing to Shanghai by high-speed train takes only four and a half hours, while the ordinary train used to take nearly ten. High-speed rail has not only shortened the distance between cities but also changed the way many people live. People can work in one city and return home to their families at weekends. The network has also promoted the economic development of areas along the lines; many small cities have welcomed tourists and investment since the trains arrived. Of course, building and maintaining such a network requires enormous funds and advanced technology. Engineers overcame difficulties such as complex geology and changeable weather before trains could run safely at 350 kilometres per hour. Today, high-speed rail has become a calling card of Chinese manufacturing, and for many foreign visitors it is the first stop for experiencing a modern China.

lessons.chinese: 傍晚时分，中国城市的广场和公园里常常响起音乐，成群的中老年人随着节拍起舞，这就是有名的“广场舞”。广场舞的动作简单，不需要专业基础，参与成本几乎为零，因此深受欢迎。对许多退休人员来说，跳舞不只是锻炼身体，更是重要的社交活动。研究显示，经常参加广场舞的中老年人，身体机能和心理状态都明显更好。不过，广场舞也曾因音量过大引发过矛盾，一些居民抱怨舞蹈音乐影响休息。为此，不少城市采取了措施，例如划定专门场地、限制音量和使用无线耳机。如今，“静音广场舞”在一些地区逐渐推广，舞者戴上耳机接收信号，既保留了运动的乐趣，也还给了城市一份安静。广场舞的故事说明：群众文化生活的需求，可以通过协商和管理得到更好的满足。
lessons.english: In the evening, music often fills the squares and parks of Chinese cities, where crowds of middle-aged and elderly people dance to the beat. This is the famous "square dancing". The steps are simple, no professional training is needed, and the cost of joining is almost zero, so the activity has won great popularity. For many retired people, dancing is not only exercise but also an important form of social life. Studies show that those who dance regularly enjoy better physical fitness and a healthier state of mind. However, square dancing once caused conflicts because of loud music, and some residents complained that it disturbed their rest. In response, many cities have taken measures, such as setting aside special sites, limiting volume, and introducing wireless headsets. Nowadays "silent square dancing" is spreading in some areas: dancers receive the music through headsets, keeping the fun of exercise while returning a measure of quiet to the city. The story of square dancing shows that the cultural needs of ordinary people can be better met through negotiation and management.

lessons.title_cn: 外卖骑手与半小时经济
lessons.title_en: Food Delivery and the Half-Hour Economy
lessons.chinese: 如今，在中国城市里，一份热饭半小时内送到家门口早已不是新鲜事。外卖行业的兴起，改变了数以亿计人的用餐方式。用户在手机上下单，骑手接单后前往餐厅取餐，再送往指定地点，全过程通常不超过一个小时。外卖平台还提供了海量就业岗位，其中骑手数量已达上千万。这个行业的发展得益于移动互联网、移动支付和智能调度系统的结合。同时，它也带来了新的社会问题，例如交通安全和骑手的劳动保障。近年来，政府和平台陆续出台措施，要求为骑手提供保险、合理设定配送时限。对外卖用户来说，便利的背后是无数劳动者的奔波；理解这一点，或许会让每一次“准时送达”都多一分温度。
lessons.english: Nowadays in Chinese cities, it is nothing new for a hot meal to arrive at your door within half an hour. The rise of the food delivery industry has changed the way hundreds of millions of people eat. Users place orders on their phones; riders accept the orders, collect the food from restaurants and deliver it to the given addresses, usually within an hour in all. The industry has also created a huge number of jobs, and the number of riders has reached tens of millions. Its development owes much to the combination of the mobile internet, mobile payment and intelligent scheduling systems. At the same time, it has brought new social problems, such as traffic safety and the labour protection of riders. In recent years, the government and the platforms have introduced measures one after another, requiring insurance for riders and reasonable delivery time limits. For users, the convenience on the surface depends on the hard work of countless workers; understanding this may add a little warmth to every "delivered on time".

lessons.title_en: The Rise and Fall of Shared Bikes
lessons.chinese: 几年前，共享单车出现在中国的大街小巷。用户用手机扫码解锁，按骑行时间付费，用完停放在路边即可。共享单车解决了出行中的“最后一公里”难题，一度成为绿色出行的标志。然而，快速扩张也带来了问题：一些企业为抢占市场投放过量车辆，人行道被堵塞，报废单车堆积如山。随后，行业经历了大规模洗牌，小企业退出，市场向少数几家集中。如今，城市管理者与企业建立了总量控制和电子围栏制度，单车数量回归合理，停放也更加有序。共享单车的经历说明，新技术要真正改善城市生活，光有好的创意还不够，还需要科学的管理和理性的竞争。这段起伏也提醒人们：分享经济的未来，取决于创新与规则能否同行。
lessons.english: A few years ago, shared bikes appeared on the streets of Chinese cities. Users scan a code with their phones to unlock a bike, pay by riding time, and leave it by the roadside after use. Shared bikes solved the "last kilometre" problem of urban travel and for a time became a symbol of green transport. Rapid expansion, however, brought problems: some companies flooded the streets with bikes to seize the market, pavements were blocked, and worn-out bicycles piled up like hills. The industry then went through large-scale reshuffling; small firms withdrew and the market became concentrated in a few companies. Nowadays city administrators and enterprises have established systems of total quantity control and electronic fences, so the number of bikes has returned to a reasonable level and parking is more orderly. The story of shared bikes shows that for a new technology to truly improve urban life, a good idea is not enough; it also requires scientific management and rational competition. The rise and fall also reminds people that the future of the sharing economy depends on whether innovation and rules can move forward together.

lessons.chinese: 春运是中国规模最大的周期性人口流动。每年春节前后，数十亿人次乘坐火车、飞机和汽车返乡过年，铁路单日旅客发送量多次刷新纪录。为了应对这一挑战，铁路部门不断加密班次、扩建线路，并推出网络购票系统。过去，人们要在售票窗口前排长队，甚至通宵等待；如今，大多数人只需在手机上轻轻一点。春运的背后，是中国人对家庭团聚的重视。无论路途多远、车票多紧张，回家过年始终是许多人一年中最重要的安排。与此同时，也有越来越多的人选择反向出行，把父母接到自己工作的城市过年，或者利用假期外出旅行。春运见证了中国交通的进步，也见证了家庭观念在时代中的延续与变化。
lessons.english: The Spring Festival travel rush is the largest periodic movement of people in China. Around the Spring Festival every year, billions of passenger trips are made by train, plane and car, and the number of passengers carried by rail in a single day has set new records again and again. To meet this challenge, the railway authorities have added trains, expanded lines and introduced an online ticketing system. In the past, people had to stand in long queues at ticket windows, sometimes waiting all night; nowadays, most people need only a tap on their phones. Behind the rush lies the importance that Chinese people attach to family reunion. However long the journey or tight the tickets, returning home for the festival remains the most important arrangement of the year for many. At the same time, a growing number of people choose to travel in the opposite direction, bringing their parents to the cities where they work, or spending the holiday on a journey. The travel rush has witnessed the progress of Chinese transport, as well as the continuity and change of the idea of family in a changing age.

lessons.chinese: 夜幕降临，城市的夜市开始热闹起来。烤串的香气、小摊的灯火和川流不息的人群，构成了许多城市最有烟火气的风景。近年来，不少城市把发展夜市经济作为促进消费的举措，延长地铁和公交的运营时间，划定特色夜市街区。夜市不仅满足了人们的味蕾，也创造了大量灵活就业机会。一个不起眼的小摊，可能就是一个家庭的生计。对年轻人来说，夜市还是重要的社交场所，朋友相聚、拍照分享，都是城市生活的一部分。当然，夜市的繁荣也考验着城市治理：食品卫生、垃圾处理和噪音控制都需要精细管理。一座城市的夜市如果既有烟火气又有秩序，往往说明这座城市的治理有了温度，也有了水平。灯火、声响与人流，共同讲述着一座不肯睡去的城市的故事。
lessons.english: As night falls, the night markets of Chinese cities come to life. The smell of grilled skewers, the lights of small stalls and the flowing crowds make up some of the most lively scenery of a city. In recent years, many cities have taken the night market economy as a way to promote consumption, extending the operating hours of subways and buses and designating special night market districts. Night markets not only satisfy people's appetite but also create a large number of flexible jobs; an unremarkable stall may be the livelihood of a whole family. For young people, night markets are also an important social space — meeting friends, taking photos and sharing them online are all part of city life. The prosperity of night markets, of course, tests urban governance: food safety, waste disposal and noise control all require careful management. If a city's night markets combine lively human warmth with good order, it usually means that the governance of the city has both warmth and competence. The lights, the sounds and the crowds together tell the story of a city that refuses to sleep.

lessons.chinese: 近年来，健身在中国成为一种生活方式。城市里健身房和运动公园越来越多，马拉松赛事几乎每个周末都有举行，报名人数常常远超名额。运动手环和手机应用让人们可以记录步数、监测心率，并把成绩分享到社交平台。全民健身的兴起与生活水平的提高密切相关，也与健康观念的转变有关：人们不再满足于“不生病”，而是追求更好的体能和状态。政府也把全民健身上升为国家战略，推动学校、单位和社区开放体育设施。当然，健身热中也存在一些误区，例如盲目跟风高强度训练。专业人士建议，运动应当循序渐进，选择适合自己的项目。全民健身的意义不仅在于个人的健康，更在于它让运动成为一座城市共同的生活方式。
lessons.english: In recent years, keeping fit has become a way of life in China. Gyms and sports parks are appearing in more and more cities, marathon races are held almost every weekend, and the number of applicants often far exceeds the quota. Fitness bands and phone apps allow people to record their steps, monitor their heart rates and share the results on social media. The fitness boom is closely related to the rise of living standards and to a change in the idea of health: people are no longer satisfied with "not being ill" but pursue better fitness and energy. The government has also made national fitness a national strategy, encouraging schools, workplaces and communities to open their sports facilities. There are, of course, some misunderstandings in the boom, such as blindly following high-intensity training. Professionals suggest that exercise should progress step by step and fit the person. The meaning of national fitness lies not only in personal health, but also in making sport a common way of life for a whole city.

lessons.chinese: 等公交的间隙、排队的时候、睡前的几分钟，越来越多的人用短视频来填满这些碎片时间。短视频通常只有十几秒到几分钟，节奏快、内容多，容易让人一刷就停不下来。短视频平台也为普通人提供了展示的舞台：会做饭的、会唱歌的、住在乡村的，都可能拥有百万粉丝。一些乡村博主通过镜头让城市人看到了田园生活，也带动了当地特产的销售。不过，短视频的流行也引发担忧。有研究表明，过度使用短视频与注意力下降、睡眠不足存在关联。不少学校和家庭开始引导孩子合理使用，一些平台也上线了时间管理功能。短视频本身并无好坏，关键在于使用它的人。让工具服务于生活，而不是让生活被工具填满，是这个时代每个人都面对的课题。
lessons.english: While waiting for a bus, standing in a queue, or in the few minutes before sleep, more and more people fill these fragments of time with short videos. Short videos usually last from a dozen seconds to a few minutes; their fast rhythm and rich content make it easy to keep scrolling. Short video platforms have also provided an ordinary person with a stage: those who can cook, who can sing, or who live in the countryside may all win millions of followers. Some rural bloggers have shown city people the life of the fields through the camera, and promoted the sale of local produce as well. The popularity of short videos, however, has raised concerns. Studies suggest that excessive use is related to a shorter attention span and lack of sleep. Many schools and families have begun to guide children towards reasonable use, and some platforms have introduced time-management functions. Short videos themselves are neither good nor bad; the key lies in the user. Making the tool serve life, instead of letting life be filled by the tool, is a task that everyone faces in this age.

lessons.chinese: 如今，志愿服务已经成为中国城市生活中一道常见的风景。大型活动里有引导和翻译的志愿者，社区里有陪伴老人的志愿者，交通路口有维持秩序的志愿者。据统计，全国注册志愿者人数已超过两亿。许多城市建立了志愿服务时长记录制度，志愿者可以用积累的时长兑换培训和公共服务。对年轻人来说，志愿服务不仅是奉献，也是了解社会、锻炼能力的课堂。有大学生说，在乡村支教的经历改变了他们对教师职业的看法。志愿服务的发展也推动了相关制度的完善，例如志愿者保险和服务认证。一座城市的文明程度，不仅体现在高楼和马路上，也体现在愿意为陌生人停下来帮忙的人有多少。志愿者越多，城市的温度就越高。
lessons.english: Nowadays, volunteering has become a common sight in the urban life of China. At large events there are volunteers for guidance and translation; in communities there are volunteers who keep the elderly company; at crossings there are volunteers who help keep order. According to statistics, the number of registered volunteers across the country has exceeded two hundred million. Many cities have set up systems to record the hours of voluntary service, which volunteers can exchange for training and public services. For young people, volunteering is not only contribution but also a classroom for understanding society and testing their abilities. One university student said that her experience of teaching in a village changed her view of the teaching profession. The growth of volunteering has also pushed forward the improvement of related systems, such as insurance for volunteers and the certification of service. The level of civilisation of a city is shown not only in its tall buildings and wide roads, but also in how many people are willing to stop and help a stranger. The more volunteers a city has, the warmer the city is.

lessons.chinese: 高考，即全国普通高等学校招生考试，是中国最重要的一次考试。每年六月，上千万考生走进考场，无数家庭为之牵挂。高考成绩在很大程度上决定了考生能进入哪所大学、学习什么专业。对许多出身普通家庭的学生来说，高考仍然是改变命运的重要机会。为了这场考试，学生们要准备三年，家长也常常全力陪读。近年来，高考制度也在不断改革，例如部分省份实行新的选科模式，高校录取更加多元。与此同时，社会对高考的态度也在变化：越来越多的人认识到，高考很重要，但它不是人生的唯一出路。无论结果如何，一个十八岁的年轻人为目标全力以赴的经历，本身就是一份财富。而高考更深的意义在于公平：在同一间考场里，所有考生都站在同一条起跑线上。
lessons.english: The Gaokao, the national college entrance examination, is the most important single examination in China. Every June, tens of millions of candidates walk into examination halls, and countless families think of little else. The result of the Gaokao largely decides which university a candidate can enter and what subject he or she will study. For many students from ordinary families, the Gaokao remains an important chance to change their fate. Students prepare for three years for this examination, and parents often give all their support. In recent years, the system has kept reforming: some provinces have introduced new models of subject selection, and university admission has become more diverse. At the same time, attitudes towards the Gaokao are changing: more and more people have come to see that although the Gaokao matters, it is not the only road in life. Whatever the result, the experience of a young person of eighteen giving all his or her effort for a goal is itself a kind of wealth. Yet the deeper meaning of the Gaokao lies in fairness: within one hall, all candidates stand at the same starting line.

lessons.chinese: 过去二十年，中国出国留学的人数持续增长，中国已成为世界最大的留学生生源国。留学的目的地也从传统的英美扩展到德国、日本、新加坡等许多国家。留学的吸引力在于优质的教育资源、多元的文化体验和更广阔的职业选择。与此同时，越来越多的留学生选择学成回国，国内快速发展的经济和人才政策为他们提供了广阔舞台。留学并不适合每一个人：高昂的费用、语言的障碍和文化差异都是现实挑战。一些教育专家建议，是否出国应当取决于个人的学业规划和适应能力，而不是盲从潮流。值得注意的是，中外合作办学和在线课程的兴起，让更多人不出国门也能接触国际化的教育。留学的形式在变，但它打开视野的价值没有变。无论形式如何，求学的目标始终是成长。
lessons.english: Over the past twenty years, the number of Chinese students studying abroad has kept growing, and China has become the largest source of international students in the world. The destinations have also expanded from the traditional choice of Britain and America to many other countries, such as Germany, Japan and Singapore. The attraction of studying abroad lies in high-quality educational resources, varied cultural experiences and wider career choices. Meanwhile, a growing number of overseas students choose to return after graduation, for the rapidly developing economy and talent policies at home offer them a broad stage. Studying abroad does not suit everyone: high costs, language barriers and cultural differences are all real challenges. Some education experts suggest that the decision should depend on one's academic plan and ability to adapt, not on blind fashion. It is worth noting that the rise of Chinese-foreign cooperative universities and online courses has allowed more people to reach international education without leaving the country. The form of studying abroad is changing, but its value of opening the eyes has not. Whatever the form, the goal of study remains growth.

lessons.chinese: 互联网正在改变人们接受教育的方式。借助在线平台，偏远地区的学生可以听到一线城市的名师课程，上班族可以利用碎片时间学习新技能。特别是在特殊时期，在线教学保障了亿万学生的学业不中断。在线教育的优势十分明显：成本低、资源多、不受时间和地点限制。但它也有明显的短板，例如缺乏面对面的交流，学习效果高度依赖自觉性。调查显示，缺乏监督是在线课程完成率低的主要原因。因此，混合式教学正在兴起——学校把线上资源与线下课堂结合起来，让技术支持教学，而不是替代教师。教育的本质是人与人的相互点亮，屏幕可以传递知识，但点亮人心的仍然是教师。未来的教育，很可能是线上与线下各展所长的教育。
lessons.english: The internet is changing the way people receive education. With the help of online platforms, students in remote areas can listen to excellent teachers from big cities, and office workers can learn new skills in their fragments of time. Especially during the special period, online teaching kept the studies of hundreds of millions of students from being interrupted. The advantages of online education are clear: low cost, rich resources, and freedom from the limits of time and place. But it also has an obvious weakness, such as the lack of face-to-face communication and the fact that the result depends heavily on self-discipline. Surveys show that the lack of supervision is the main reason for the low completion rate of online courses. For this reason, blended teaching is on the rise — schools combine online resources with offline classrooms, letting technology support teaching rather than replace teachers. The essence of education is one person lighting up another; a screen can carry knowledge, but it is the teacher who lights up the heart. The education of the future is likely to be one in which online and offline each play to their strengths.

lessons.chinese: “全民阅读”近年来被多次写入政府工作报告，阅读正在成为一种被鼓励的生活方式。城市的书店数量回升，一些书店变成了集图书、咖啡和文化活动于一体的空间。社区图书馆、共享书柜和流动图书车，让阅读走近普通人的生活。数字阅读也在快速增长，很多人用手机读完了一本又一本书。不过，调查显示，深度阅读的时间仍然不足，碎片化阅读难以替代系统的学习。为此，许多学校和单位组织读书会，引导人们静下心来读完一本好书。阅读的意义远不止获取信息，它锻炼思维、滋养情感，也让人在喧嚣中保持安静的能力。一个热爱阅读的民族，会拥有更丰富的精神世界和更持久的创造力。说到底，一本书给予什么，取决于读者带入什么。
lessons.english: "Reading for all" has been written into the government work report several times in recent years, and reading is becoming an encouraged way of life. The number of bookshops in cities is recovering, and some bookshops have become spaces that combine books, coffee and cultural events. Community libraries, shared bookcases and mobile book vans bring reading close to ordinary life. Digital reading is also growing fast, and many people finish one book after another on their phones. However, surveys show that the time spent on deep reading is still not enough, and fragmented reading can hardly replace systematic learning. For this reason, many schools and workplaces organise reading clubs to guide people to calm down and finish a good book. The meaning of reading goes far beyond gaining information: it trains the mind, feeds the feelings, and keeps alive the ability to stay quiet in a noisy world. A nation that loves reading will have a richer spiritual world and a more lasting power of creativity. In the end, what a book gives back depends on what the reader brings to it.

lessons.chinese: 中医药是中华文明的重要组成部分，已流传数千年。它包括中药、针灸、推拿等多种治疗方式，强调人与自然的整体平衡。随着健康观念的转变，越来越多的人开始关注中医药的养生价值。针灸已经被世界许多国家接受，成为治疗某些疾病的重要补充手段。屠呦呦从传统中药中获得灵感提取青蒿素，并因此获得诺贝尔奖，让世界看到了中医药的现代价值。当然，中医药的发展也面临挑战，例如疗效标准的建立和药材质量的控制。近年来，国家出台政策支持中医药的传承与创新，推动中西医结合。许多外国朋友第一次接触中国文化，就是从一杯凉茶或一次推拿开始的。中医药走向世界的过程，也是中国文化与世界对话的过程。
lessons.english: Traditional Chinese medicine is an important part of Chinese civilisation and has been passed down for thousands of years. It includes herbal medicine, acupuncture, massage and other forms of treatment, and stresses the overall balance between human beings and nature. With the change in ideas about health, more and more people have begun to pay attention to the value of traditional Chinese medicine in keeping well. Acupuncture has been accepted by many countries as an important supplement in treating certain diseases. Tu Youyou drew inspiration from traditional herbs to extract artemisinin and won the Nobel Prize for it, showing the world the modern value of traditional Chinese medicine. Its development, of course, faces challenges, such as setting standards of effect and controlling the quality of herbs. In recent years, the state has introduced policies to support its inheritance and innovation, promoting the combination of Chinese and Western medicine. For many foreign friends, the first contact with Chinese culture begins with a cup of herbal tea or a session of massage. The process of traditional Chinese medicine going global is also a process of dialogue between Chinese culture and the world.

lessons.title_en: A Healthy Revolution on the Table
lessons.chinese: 中国人的餐桌正在悄悄发生变化。过去人们讲究“吃得好”，如今更追求“吃得健康”。超市里，低糖、低盐、高蛋白的食品越来越多，蔬菜和粗粮重新受到青睐。外卖平台上的轻食订单逐年增长，年轻人开始关注食品的营养成分表。《健康中国行动》等文件提倡减盐、减油、减糖，并给出具体的膳食建议。健康饮食的流行也带动了相关产业，例如有机农业和食品加工业的升级。当然，改变饮食习惯并不容易，高油高糖的传统美食依然诱人。营养专家的建议是循序渐进：不必完全放弃喜爱的食物，而是学会搭配与节制。健康革命没有惊天动地的场面，它就发生在每一餐的选择里。一顿顿更合理的饭，累积起来就是更健康的人生。每一餐的小选择，经年累月，就成了整个人生的健康。
lessons.english: A quiet change is taking place on the tables of China. In the past, people aimed to "eat well"; now they pursue "eat healthily". In supermarkets, food low in sugar and salt and high in protein is increasing, and vegetables and coarse grains are regaining favour. Orders for light food on delivery platforms grow year by year, and young people have begun to study the nutrition lists on packages. Documents such as Healthy China Action advocate less salt, less oil and less sugar, and give concrete dietary advice. The fashion for healthy eating has also driven related industries, such as the upgrading of organic agriculture and food processing. Changing eating habits is not easy, of course; traditional dishes rich in oil and sugar remain attractive. Nutrition experts advise a step-by-step approach: one need not give up favourite foods completely, but should learn matching and moderation. The healthy revolution has no dramatic scenes; it happens in the choice of every meal. Meal after meal eaten more reasonably adds up to a healthier life. Small choices at every meal, repeated for years, become the health of a whole life.

lessons.chinese: 中国正在进入老龄化社会。统计显示，六十岁以上人口已超过两亿八千万，占总人口的五分之一左右。银发浪潮带来了挑战，也催生了机遇。养老服务从传统的家庭养老，逐步扩展为社区养老、机构养老等多种模式。老年大学里座无虚席，智能手机课程常常供不应求。银发经济也在快速增长，从老年旅游到康复辅具，市场需求旺盛。与此同时，年轻人的养老观念也在变化，越来越多的人提前规划养老金和健康管理。如何让老年人不仅“活着”，而且“活得好”，是全社会面对的课题。尊老爱老是中华民族的传统美德，在新的时代，这份美德正在被赋予新的形式。每一位老人都值得有尊严、有质量的晚年，这也是衡量一个社会文明程度的重要标尺。老龄化社会不是负担，而是一道设计题。
lessons.english: China is entering an ageing society. Statistics show that the population above sixty has exceeded two hundred and eighty million, about one fifth of the total. The silver wave brings challenges, but also gives birth to opportunities. Care for the elderly has expanded from the traditional family model to many forms, such as community care and institutional care. Seats in universities for the elderly are full, and courses on smartphones are often oversubscribed. The silver economy is also growing fast, from travel for the old to rehabilitation devices, with strong market demand. Meanwhile, the ideas of the young are changing too, and more and more people plan their pensions and health management early. How to let the elderly not only "live" but "live well" is a question for the whole society. Respecting the old is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation, and in the new age this virtue is being given new forms. Every old person deserves a later life of dignity and quality — this is also an important measure of how civilised a society is. An ageing society is not a burden but a question of design.

lessons.chinese: 最近几年，心理健康成为校园里的高频词。学业压力、人际交往和对未来的迷茫，都可能影响学生的情绪。许多学校开设了心理健康课程，设立心理咨询室，并培训教师识别学生的情绪变化。一些高校还开通了二十四小时心理援助热线。值得欣慰的是，越来越多的学生愿意主动寻求帮助，“看心理老师”不再是一件难以启齿的事。心理健康教育的目标，不仅是减少心理问题，更是培养学生面对挫折的能力。有心理教师说，我们无法替学生避开风雨，但可以教他们撑伞的方法。社会各界也在努力，例如推出面向青少年的心理科普读物和热线服务。关注心理健康，就是关注一个人完整的成长。当学生学会说出自己的情绪，他们就获得了一种任何考试都无法衡量的能力。
lessons.english: In recent years, mental health has become a frequent topic on campus. Pressure from study, personal relationships and uncertainty about the future can all affect the feelings of students. Many schools have opened courses on mental health, set up counselling rooms, and trained teachers to notice changes in students' moods. Some universities have also opened twenty-four-hour hotlines of psychological aid. What is encouraging is that more and more students are willing to seek help actively; "seeing the counsellor" is no longer something hard to speak about. The aim of mental health education is not only to reduce problems, but to build the ability of students to face setbacks. One counsellor said that we cannot keep the storms away from students, but we can teach them how to hold an umbrella. All parts of society are making efforts too, such as publishing books of popular science on psychology for teenagers and opening hotlines. To care for mental health is to care for the whole growth of a person. When students learn to name their feelings, they gain a tool that no examination can measure.

lessons.chinese: 垃圾分类正在改变中国城市居民的生活习惯。在上海、北京等城市，居民需要按照“可回收物、有害垃圾、厨余垃圾、其他垃圾”的分类投放垃圾。起初，不少人觉得麻烦，记不住类别；社区里出现了志愿者，站在垃圾桶旁耐心指导。学校也把垃圾分类带进课堂，孩子们回家当起了“小老师”。几年下来，效果逐渐显现：可回收物的利用率提高了，填埋的垃圾量下降了。垃圾分类背后，是城市发展理念的转变——垃圾不是无用的废物，而是放错位置的资源。当然，分类只是第一步，后续的运输和处理同样重要。只有整条链条都规范运转，分类才有意义。这件小事考验着每个人的耐心，也正在重塑一座城市的文明习惯。城市需要的不只是规则，更是一种共同的习惯——而习惯在共同践行中长得最好。
lessons.english: Waste sorting is changing the habits of city dwellers in China. In cities such as Shanghai and Beijing, residents are required to put waste into four categories: recyclable, harmful, kitchen and other waste. At the beginning many people found it troublesome and could not remember the categories; volunteers appeared in communities, standing beside the bins to give patient guidance. Schools have brought waste sorting into classrooms, and children have acted as "little teachers" at home. After several years, the effect is appearing gradually: the rate of recycling has risen, and the amount of waste buried has fallen. Behind waste sorting lies a change in the idea of urban development — waste is not useless matter but resources in the wrong place. Of course, sorting is only the first step; transport and treatment afterwards are equally important. Only when the whole chain runs properly does sorting have meaning. This small matter tests everyone's patience, and it is reshaping the habits of a civilised city. What the city needs is not only rules, but a shared habit — and habits grow best when they are practised together.

lessons.chinese: 每年春天，数以百万计的中国人会拿起铁锹参加义务植树。这项活动已经坚持了几十年，荒山披上绿装，沙漠边缘筑起绿色屏障。塞罕坝林场就是著名的例子：三代人在荒原上种下百万亩林海，如今那里已成为国家公园。城市也在变绿，口袋公园、林荫道和屋顶花园让居民推窗见绿。卫星数据显示，近二十年全球新增绿化面积中，中国贡献了约四分之一。森林带来的好处是实实在在的：防风固沙、涵养水源、吸收二氧化碳。种树也不只是政府的工程，越来越多的企业和个人通过捐款认养树苗。一棵树从种下到成荫需要许多年，这份耐心本身就是一种远见。树荫下的中国，是留给下一代的礼物。
lessons.english: Every spring, millions of Chinese people take up spades to plant trees as volunteers. This activity has been carried on for decades: barren hills have dressed themselves in green, and a green barrier has risen along the edge of the desert. The Saihanba forest farm is a famous example: three generations planted a sea of trees over a million mu on the wasteland, and today it has become a national park. Cities are turning green as well — pocket parks, avenues of shade and rooftop gardens let residents see green the moment they open a window. Satellite data show that of the new green area added to the world in the past twenty years, about one quarter came from China. The benefits of forests are real: holding back wind and sand, storing water, and taking in carbon dioxide. Tree planting is no longer only a project of the government; more and more companies and individuals adopt young trees through donations. A tree takes many years from planting to shade, and such patience is itself a kind of foresight. China under the trees is a gift left to the next generation.

lessons.chinese: 春节是中国最隆重的传统节日，标志农历新年的开始。它的历史可以追溯到两千多年前，最初与祭祀祖先和祈求丰收有关。如今，春节的核心仍然是团聚：无论身在何处，人们都会设法在除夕前赶回家中。除夕夜，全家围坐在一起吃年夜饭，北方吃饺子，南方多吃年糕和汤圆。许多人守岁到午夜，迎接新年钟声。春节期间，人们走亲访友、互赠红包，红包如今常常通过手机发送，但祝福的心意没有变。贴春联、挂灯笼、舞龙舞狮等习俗，为节日增添了喜庆的气氛。近年来，春节文化也走向世界，许多国家的人们一同庆祝这个节日。春节承载着中国人对家庭的珍视和对新年的期盼，是一年中最温暖的时刻。在节日的温情里，新的一年总会开始。
lessons.english: Spring Festival is the grandest traditional festival of China, marking the beginning of the lunar new year. Its history goes back more than two thousand years; at first it was connected with offering sacrifices to ancestors and praying for a good harvest. Today the heart of the festival is still reunion: wherever they are, people try to get home before New Year's Eve. On that evening the whole family sits together for the reunion dinner — dumplings in the north, rice cakes and glutinous rice balls in the south. Many stay up until midnight to greet the bell of the new year. During the festival, people visit relatives and friends and exchange red envelopes, which nowadays are often sent by phone, though the good wishes remain the same. Customs such as pasting spring couplets, hanging lanterns and performing dragon and lion dances add a joyous air to the festival. In recent years the culture of the festival has travelled abroad, and people in many countries celebrate it together. Spring Festival carries the Chinese love of family and hope for the new year; it is the warmest moment of the year. In the warmth of the festival, a new year always begins.

lessons.title_en: The Mid-Autumn Festival and the Moon
lessons.chinese: 农历八月十五是中国传统的中秋节。这一天，月亮圆满明亮，象征着团圆和美满。中秋节的习俗大多与月亮有关：一家人在庭院里摆上月饼、瓜果，赏月聊天，孩子们听着嫦娥奔月的故事入睡。月饼是中秋节的标志性食品，圆形的外皮里包着各种馅料，莲蓉蛋黄最为经典。近年来，人们更加重视健康，低糖月饼越来越受欢迎。中秋也是诗人偏爱的主题，“但愿人长久，千里共婵娟”的名句流传至今。对漂泊在外的人来说，天上那一轮圆月，就是家乡的方向。中秋节寄托了中国人对团圆的永恒向往，也是一年中月光最温柔的夜晚。
lessons.english: The fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month is the traditional Mid-Autumn Festival of China. On this day the moon is full and bright, a symbol of reunion and happiness. Most customs of the festival are connected with the moon: the family sets out mooncakes and fruit in the yard, enjoys the moonlight and talks, while children fall asleep listening to the story of Chang'e flying to the moon. The mooncake is the sign of the festival — a round crust wrapped with various fillings, of which lotus seed paste with egg yolk is the most classic. In recent years people have paid more attention to health, and mooncakes low in sugar have grown popular. The festival is also a favourite subject of poets; the famous line "May we all live long, and share this graceful moon though a thousand miles apart" has come down to today. For those who wander far from home, the full moon in the sky points the direction of home. The Mid-Autumn Festival carries the eternal Chinese longing for reunion, and it is the night of the year with the gentlest moonlight.

lessons.chinese: 一片小小的树叶，经过中国人的双手，变成了影响世界的饮品——这就是茶。相传早在几千年前，中国人就开始利用茶叶。按照工艺不同，茶分为绿茶、红茶、乌龙茶、白茶等多种类型。泡茶是一门学问：水温、茶具和冲泡时间都会影响茶汤的滋味。江南人品绿茶，追求的是春天的清新。茶马古道上，马帮曾把茶叶运往高原与海外。如今，茶馆仍然是人们聊天、会友、放松的地方，新式茶饮也受到年轻人喜爱。茶不仅是一种饮料，更承载着中国人“和静怡真”的生活哲学。一杯茶里，有山川的风土，也有人与人之间的情谊。要了解中国，也许第一步就是坐下来，共饮一杯茶。
lessons.english: A small leaf, through the hands of the Chinese, has become a drink that influences the world — this is tea. According to tradition, the Chinese began to use tea leaves as early as several thousand years ago. According to the craft, tea is divided into green tea, black tea, oolong tea, white tea and other types. Making tea is a study in itself: the temperature of the water, the vessels and the time of brewing all change the taste. Along the Ancient Tea Horse Road, caravans once carried tea to the plateau and overseas. Today teahouses are still places where people chat, meet friends and relax, and new styles of tea drinks have won the young. Tea is more than a drink; it carries the Chinese philosophy of life — harmony, calm, delight and truth. In a cup of tea there is the character of mountains and rivers, and the friendship between people as well. To know China, perhaps the first step is to sit down and share a cup of tea.

lessons.chinese: 京剧被誉为中国的“国粹”，形成于两百多年前的北京。它融合了歌唱、舞蹈、武术和杂技，演员在舞台上唱、念、做、打，样样讲究。京剧的角色分为生、旦、净、丑四大行当，脸谱的颜色代表人物的性格：红色象征忠义，白色暗示奸诈。表演的舞台布置极为简约，一根马鞭代表骑马，几个龙套便代表千军万马，给观众留下想象的空间。京剧的唱腔悠扬婉转，台词多为古雅的韵白。学习京剧十分艰苦，演员往往从童年起便开始练功。200多年间，京剧名家辈出，梅兰芳便是其中的代表，他曾把京剧带到世界的舞台上。如今，越来越多年轻人走进剧场，感受这门古老艺术的力量。油彩背后藏着这条舞台的法则：每一个细节都是一种语言。
lessons.english: Peking Opera is honoured as the national treasure of China, and took shape in Beijing more than two hundred years ago. It combines singing, dancing, martial arts and acrobatics; on the stage, actors must be masters of singing, speech, acting and combat. The roles fall into four main types — sheng, dan, jing and chou — and the colours of the painted faces show the character of each figure: red stands for loyalty, white suggests treachery. The stage setting is extremely simple: a single whip stands for riding a horse, and a few walk-ons for armies of thousands, leaving space for the imagination of the audience. The singing is long and winding, and the lines are mostly recited in an ancient, musical speech. Learning Peking Opera is hard work; actors usually begin their training in childhood. Over two hundred years the stage has produced master after master, among whom Mei Lanfang is the representative — he once carried Peking Opera to the stages of the world. Nowadays more and more young people walk into the theatres to feel the power of this ancient art. Behind the painted faces lies a rule of the stage: every detail is a language of its own.

lessons.chinese: 一把剪刀，一张红纸，在艺人的指尖翻飞几下，一幅栩栩如生的图案便诞生了——这就是中国剪纸。剪纸的历史可以追溯到一千五百多年前，是最受欢迎的民间艺术之一。剪纸的题材大多寄托着美好的愿望：鱼代表年年有余，喜鹊登梅寓意喜上眉梢。逢年过节，人们把剪纸贴在窗户上，红彤彤的窗花映着白雪，年味十足。北方剪纸粗犷豪放，南方剪纸细腻秀美，风格各有千秋。2009年，中国剪纸被列入人类非物质文化遗产代表作名录。如今，剪纸也走进现代生活，出现在服装设计和动画作品里。许多学校开设了剪纸课，孩子们从最基本的对称图案学起。这门指尖上的艺术证明：最朴素的材料，也能承载最丰富的想象。在机器时代，手剪的温度反而更加动人。
lessons.english: One pair of scissors, one sheet of red paper — after a few turns at the fingertips of the artist, a living picture is born. This is Chinese paper cutting. Its history goes back more than one thousand five hundred years, and it is one of the most beloved folk arts. The subjects mostly carry good wishes: a fish stands for plenty year after year, and a magpie on a plum branch means joy up to the eyebrows. At festivals people paste the cuttings on windows, where red window flowers against the snow fill the house with the air of the new year. The northern style is bold and free, the southern fine and graceful — each has its own beauty. In 2009, Chinese paper cutting was entered on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Nowadays paper cutting has entered modern life as well, appearing in fashion design and animation. Many schools offer courses in it, and children begin with the simplest symmetrical patterns. This art at the fingertips proves that the plainest material can carry the richest imagination. In the age of machines, the warmth of a hand-cut pattern speaks even louder.

lessons.chinese: 中国园林被誉为“凝固的诗，立体的画”。其中，苏州园林是最杰出的代表，已被列入世界文化遗产。园林的设计讲究“虽由人作，宛自天开”：亭台楼阁、假山池沼、花草树木，都被安排得错落有致。一道曲廊、一扇花窗，就能把景色分割成一幅幅画。造园者常用“借景”的手法，把园外的远山宝塔引入园中，使有限的空间变得深远。园中的匾额与楹联也大有讲究，文字与景物互相呼应，营造出诗的意境。漫步园中，一步一景，走过同一扇窗，看到的却已是另一幅画面。园林体现了中国人对自然的理解：人不应征服自然，而应与自然相处。在喧嚣的城市里，园林为人们保留了一方可静心的天地。园林，是一座城市学会呼吸的地方。
lessons.english: Chinese gardens are honoured as "poems that stand still, paintings that stand up". The gardens of Suzhou are the finest among them and have been entered on the World Heritage List. Their design follows the principle "made by human hands, yet looking like heaven's work": pavilions, artificial hills, ponds, flowers and trees are all arranged in pleasing disorder. A winding corridor or a latticed window cuts the scenery into picture after picture. Garden-makers often used the technique of "borrowing scenery", drawing distant hills and pagodas outside the garden into the view, so that a small space became deep and far. The tablets and couplets in the gardens are also full of thought — words and scenery echo each other and create the mood of poetry. Walking in the garden, one sees a new scene at every step; passing the same window again, one finds a different picture already waiting. The gardens show the Chinese understanding of nature: human beings should not conquer nature but live with it. In the noisy city, the gardens keep for people a small corner of the world where the heart can be still. A garden is where a city learns to breathe.

lessons.chinese: 在北京的老城区，一片片灰色屋顶的四合院静静排列。四合院由北房、南房和东西厢房围合而成，中间是宽敞的院子。这样的布局体现了中国传统的家庭观念：长辈住正房，晚辈住厢房，一家人在院子里共享阳光。四季之中，院子各有风景：春天赏海棠，夏天乘凉，秋天收葡萄，冬天看雪。胡同里，邻里之间隔着矮墙聊天，孩子们在门前追逐玩耍。随着城市改造，许多四合院消失了，人们开始意识到它们的价值。如今，一部分四合院被保护修缮，改成了博物馆和文创空间；住在院子里的居民，生活条件也得到了改善。四合院不仅是一种建筑，更是老北京生活方式的容器。推开一扇朱漆木门，就走进了这座城市的历史。
lessons.english: In the old districts of Beijing, rows of courtyard houses with grey roofs stand quietly. A courtyard house is enclosed by the northern main rooms, southern rooms and wings on the east and west, with an open yard in the middle. The layout shows the traditional Chinese idea of family: the elders live in the main rooms, the younger generation in the wings, and the whole family shares the sunlight in the yard. Each season has its own scenery in the yard — crab-apple blossoms in spring, cool air in summer, grapes in autumn and snow in winter. In the narrow lanes, neighbours chat across low walls, and children chase each other before the gates. With the redevelopment of the city, many courtyard houses disappeared, and people began to realise their value. Nowadays some of them have been protected and repaired, turned into museums and cultural spaces, and the living conditions of residents in the courtyards have improved as well. The courtyard house is not merely a building; it is the vessel of the old life of Beijing. Push open one red wooden door, and you walk into the history of the city.

lessons.chinese: 两千多年前，张骞受命出使西域，开辟了一条连接中国与西方的通道。后来，商人们沿着这条路，把丝绸、瓷器和茶叶运往远方，又带回了葡萄、核桃和汗血宝马。这条道路后来被德国学者命名为“丝绸之路”。丝绸之路不仅是一条商路，更是一条文化交流之路：佛教经它传入中国，中国的造纸术经它传向西方。驼铃声声，商队在沙漠中跋涉，绿洲城市因此繁荣，敦煌便是其中最耀眼的明珠。如今，古老的丝绸之路以新的形式延续，“一带一路”倡议让沿线国家重新紧密相连。中欧班列穿越亚欧大陆，往来货物的种类远超当年。丝绸之路的故事告诉人们：文明因交流而丰富，因互鉴而精彩。道路会改换名字，但人类相遇与通商的愿望，始终是各民族之间最古老的桥梁。
lessons.english: More than two thousand years ago, Zhang Qian was sent on a mission to the Western Regions and opened a passage joining China with the West. Later, along this road, merchants carried silk, porcelain and tea to faraway lands, and brought back grapes, walnuts and fine horses. The road was later named "the Silk Road" by a German scholar. The Silk Road was more than a trade route; it was a road of cultural exchange: Buddhism entered China along it, and Chinese paper-making travelled west along it. With the sound of camel bells, caravans trudged through the deserts, oasis cities grew rich because of them, and Dunhuang was the brightest pearl among them. Today the ancient Silk Road continues in a new form: the Belt and Road Initiative has joined the countries along the routes closely again. Freight trains between China and Europe cross the continent, carrying goods far richer in kind than those of the past. The story of the Silk Road tells people that civilisations grow rich through exchange and shine through learning from one another. Roads may change their names, but the human wish to meet and to trade remains the oldest bridge between peoples.

lessons.chinese: 长城是人类建筑史上的奇迹，全长两万多公里，横跨中国北方。它的修建历经多个朝代，现存的大部分为明代所建。长城并非一道孤立的墙，而是由城墙、关隘、烽火台组成的防御体系。发现敌情时，士兵在烽火台上点燃烟火，消息几个小时便可传到千里之外。修建长城的艰辛超出想象：无数的士兵和民夫在崇山峻岭间搬运砖石，许多人长眠于此。民间流传的孟姜女哭长城的故事，寄托着人们对和平的向往。如今，长城不再是防御工事，而成为中华民族精神的象征。“不到长城非好汉”的说法，吸引着世界各地的游客登临远眺。站在长城上极目远望，人们看到的不仅是壮丽的山河，还有跨越千年的坚韧与智慧。
lessons.english: The Great Wall is a wonder in the history of human building, with a total length of more than twenty thousand kilometres across northern China. Its construction went on through many dynasties, and most of what remains today was built in the Ming Dynasty. The Wall was never a lonely wall but a system of defence made up of walls, passes and beacon towers. When the enemy appeared, soldiers lit fires on the towers, and the news could travel a thousand kilometres within hours. The hardship of building the Wall went beyond imagination: countless soldiers and labourers carried bricks and stones over high mountains, and many of them lie there still. The folk story of Meng Jiangnu weeping at the Wall carries people's longing for peace. Today the Great Wall is no longer a fortification but a symbol of the spirit of the Chinese nation. The saying "He who has never been to the Great Wall is not a true man" draws visitors from all over the world to climb and gaze afar. Standing on the Wall and looking out, one sees not only magnificent mountains and rivers, but also toughness and wisdom that have crossed a thousand years.

lessons.chinese: 近年来，一股“汉语热”在全球范围内悄然兴起。据统计，目前全球学习中文的人数已超过三千万，一百八十多个国家开展了中文教育项目。许多国家把中文纳入国民教育体系，孔子学院和各类中文课堂遍布世界各地。学习汉语的动机多种多样：有人为了职业发展，有人热爱中国文化，有人只是被汉字的美所吸引。汉字对初学者来说并不容易，但每一个汉字背后都有故事，一旦入门便趣味无穷。除了语言，书法、太极和中华美食也成为许多学习者了解中国的窗口。语言是文化的桥梁，学汉语的外国朋友常说，学得越深，越能理解中国人看待世界的方式。随着中国与世界交流的不断深入，这股汉语热还将持续升温。每一位新的学习者，都为这场文化对话增添了一个声音。
lessons.english: In recent years, a wave of love for the Chinese language has quietly risen around the world. According to statistics, the number of people learning Chinese across the globe has exceeded thirty million, and more than one hundred and eighty countries have carried out programmes of Chinese education. Many countries have included Chinese in their national education systems, and Confucius Institutes and Chinese classrooms of all kinds are found everywhere. The motives for learning are various: some study it for their careers, some love Chinese culture, and some are simply drawn by the beauty of Chinese characters. Characters are not easy for beginners, but behind every character there is a story, and once one has entered the gate the interest is endless. Besides the language, calligraphy, taiji and Chinese food have become windows through which learners come to know China. Language is the bridge of culture; foreign friends who learn Chinese often say that the deeper they go, the better they understand the way Chinese people see the world. As China and the world keep deepening their exchange, this wave of love for Chinese will keep rising. Every new learner adds a voice to this conversation between cultures.

lessons.chinese: 人工智能的快速发展，正在引发一场关于就业的深刻讨论。有人担心，机器将取代大量岗位，从工厂流水线到客服热线都难幸免；也有人认为，历史上每一次技术革命最终都创造了新的就业。研究显示，最容易自动化的往往是重复性强、规则清晰的工作，而需要创造力、同理心和复杂判断的岗位相对安全。因此，真正的挑战或许不是“人被机器取代”，而是劳动者能否及时更新技能。为此，许多国家开始重视职业再培训，鼓励人们终身学习。人工智能不会等待任何人，但教育可以帮助人们与它同行。经济学家称之为“技能阶梯”：当最下面一级被自动化，劳动者被期待爬上更高一级。然而，攀爬的速度因人而异、因地而异。因此，培训体系才是面对智能机器的社会真正的考验。
lessons.english: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has started a deep discussion about employment. Some fear that machines will replace a large number of jobs, from factory lines to customer-service hotlines; others argue that every technological revolution in history finally created new employment. Research shows that what is easiest to automate is usually work of strong repetition and clear rules, while posts that demand creativity, empathy and complex judgement are relatively safe. What matters more is that while new technology destroys old posts, it also gives birth to new professions — data annotators and algorithm trainers, for example, hardly existed ten years ago. For this reason, many countries have begun to attach importance to vocational retraining and encourage lifelong learning. Artificial intelligence will wait for no one, but education can help people walk with it. Economists call this the "ladder of skills": as the first rung is automated, workers are expected to climb to the next. The speed of climbing, however, differs from person to person and from region to region. Training systems, therefore, become the true test of a society facing intelligent machines.

lessons.title_en: The Age of the Connected Everything
lessons.chinese: 5G网络的铺开，让“万物互联”从概念走向现实。在智慧工厂里，机器设备通过传感器相互通信，生产效率显著提升；在农田里，湿度与光照数据实时回传，农民用手机就能管理作物。智能家居让家庭生活更加便利，照明、安防和家电都可以远程控制。万物互联的前提是海量的数据传输，这正是5G的优势所在：速度快、延迟低、可连接的设备数量庞大。当然，机遇背后也有挑战，例如网络安全和标准统一的问题。专家指出，技术本身没有方向，方向取决于使用技术的人。当万物开始互联，人与人之间的理解与合作，比以往任何时候都更加重要。当然，连接让价值与风险同时放大：一台设备的漏洞可能蔓延至整个网络。因此，安全不是最后添加的功能，而是万物立足的地面。
lessons.english: The spread of 5G networks is turning "the internet of everything" from a concept into reality. In smart factories, machines and devices communicate through sensors, and production efficiency has risen markedly; in the fields, data on humidity and light are sent back in real time, and farmers manage their crops with a phone. Smart homes make family life more convenient: lighting, security and household appliances can all be controlled from afar. Connected cars promise to reduce traffic accidents, for vehicles can "talk" to one another and warn of danger in advance. Behind the opportunities, of course, there are challenges, such as network security and the unification of standards. Experts point out that technology itself has no direction; the direction depends on those who use it. When everything begins to be connected, understanding and cooperation between human beings matter more than ever. Of course, connection multiplies both value and risk: a single weakness in one device may spread through the whole network. Security, therefore, is not a feature added at the end, but the ground on which everything stands.

lessons.title_en: The New Countryside in the Live-Streaming Room
lessons.chinese: 曾经，偏远乡村的农产品愁销路；如今，一部手机、一个支架，就能把田间地头连接全国市场。农村电商的兴起，正在深刻改变乡村的面貌。果农在果园里开直播，现摘现发；地方政府官员也走进直播间，为本地特产代言。数据显示，全国农村网络零售额连年增长，电商带动了大量农民增收。更重要的是，电商为乡村留住了年轻人，返乡创业成为新风尚。当然，行业发展也面临挑战，例如产品同质化和售后服务的短板。有专家建议，乡村电商应当从“卖产品”走向“卖品牌”，把地方文化融入产品之中。当古老的乡村连接上数字时代，振兴的故事才刚刚开始。每一份订单背后都有一条更长的链条：品控、包装与品牌设计，决定乡村产品能走多远。
lessons.english: In the past, farm products from remote villages had trouble finding buyers; now a phone and a stand connect the fields with the national market. The rise of rural e-commerce is changing the face of the countryside. Fruit growers open live-streaming rooms in their orchards and ship what they pick the same day; local officials also enter the live-streaming rooms to speak for local produce. The extension of logistics networks has made "on the tree in the morning, on the road in the afternoon" a reality. More importantly, e-commerce has kept young people in the villages, and returning home to start a business has become a new fashion. The industry of course faces challenges, such as products too alike from village to village and weaknesses in after-sale service. Experts suggest that rural e-commerce should move from selling products to building brands, weaving local culture into the goods. When the ancient countryside is connected to the digital age, the story of revitalisation has only begun. Behind each order is a longer chain: quality control, packaging standards and brand design decide whether a village product can travel far.

lessons.chinese: 在新旧能源的转换中，新能源汽车成为最受关注的产业之一。得益于政策支持和技术进步，中国新能源汽车的产销量连续多年位居世界第一。电池技术的突破是关键：续航里程不断提升，充电时间大幅缩短。智能座舱和辅助驾驶系统，让汽车从交通工具变成移动的生活空间。交通领域的碳排放占比较大，汽车的电动化将显著改善城市的空气质量。当然，挑战依然存在，例如充电设施分布不均、电池回收体系尚不完善。行业专家认为，未来十年将是决定性的窗口期。当发动机的轰鸣被电机的安静取代，改变的不仅是汽车，还有人与能源、与环境的关系。充电网络、电池回收与电网容量，必须与汽车本身同步成长。
lessons.english: In the change from old energy to new, the new energy vehicle has become one of the most closely watched industries. Thanks to policy support and technical progress, the production and sales of new energy vehicles in China have ranked first in the world for years running. The breakthrough lies in battery technology: the driving range keeps rising, and charging time has been greatly cut. Smart cabins and driver-assistance systems have turned the car from a means of transport into a moving living space. Transport produces a large share of carbon emissions, and the electrification of cars will markedly improve the air of cities. Challenges remain, of course, such as the uneven distribution of charging stations and an imperfect system of battery recycling. Experts in the industry believe the coming ten years will be a decisive window. When the roar of the engine gives way to the quiet of the motor, what changes is not only the car, but also the relationship between human beings and energy, and between human beings and the environment. Charging networks, battery recycling and grid capacity must grow at the same pace as the cars themselves.

lessons.chinese: 当年轻人熟练地在数字世界里生活时，还有一群人被挡在了门外。不会扫码、不会挂号、不会线上缴费——这些困难构成了所谓“数字鸿沟”。数字鸿沟不仅存在于代际之间，也存在城乡之间和地区之间。它的本质并非设备的有无，而是使用能力的差异。缩小数字鸿沟，需要技术多一分包容，也需要家庭多一分耐心。技术进步的真正意义，不是让一部分人跑得更快，而是不让任何人掉队。一个有温度的数字社会，应当容得下慢一点的人。一些社区开设了数字门诊，让老人按自己的节奏学习；银行也为需要的人保留了纸质服务。进步的标尺，终究不是最新的用户跑得多快，而是被留在路边的人有多少。
lessons.english: While the young live with ease in the digital world, a group of people are still kept outside its gate. Unable to scan a code, book a hospital appointment, or pay a bill online — these difficulties make up the so-called "digital divide". The divide lies not only between generations, but also between town and country and between regions. Its essence is not the presence or absence of devices, but the difference in the ability to use them. To narrow the digital divide, technology needs a little more inclusiveness, and families a little more patience. The true meaning of technological progress is not that some people run faster, but that no one is left behind. A digital society with warmth should have room for those who walk more slowly. Some communities have opened digital clinics where the elderly learn at their own pace, and banks keep paper services for those who need them. The measure of progress, in the end, is not how fast the newest user moves, but how few are left at the roadside.

lessons.chinese: 曾经，人们习惯于免费获取网络信息；如今，为知识付费已被广泛接受。音频课程、专栏文章、直播讲座，用户用真金白银为内容买单。知识付费的兴起，一方面源于人们对自我提升的焦虑与渴望，另一方面也反映了优质内容的稀缺。相比传统教育，它的优势在于便捷与灵活：通勤路上听课，睡前读一篇专栏。市场因此开始洗牌，深耕专业领域的创作者留了下来。知识付费的本质，是用商业方式传播知识。真正有生命力的产品，最终依靠的仍然是内容的真诚与专业。知识没有捷径，付费买的应当是起点，而不是终点。市场也在学同一课：只有当一门课真正改变了什么——一项技能、一个习惯或一种眼光，读者才会再次付费。就此而言，知识付费不是一件商品，而是一个承诺。
lessons.english: There was a time when people expected information on the internet to be free; nowadays, paying for knowledge has been widely accepted. Audio courses, columns, live lectures — users pay real money for content. The rise of paying for knowledge springs partly from the anxiety and desire for self-improvement, and partly reflects the scarcity of good content. Compared with traditional education, its advantages are convenience and flexibility: listening to courses on the way to work, reading a column before sleep. Problems of the industry, however, have gradually appeared: the quality of content is uneven, some courses are beautifully wrapped with little inside, and the illusion that "to buy is to learn" has disappointed many. The essence of paying for knowledge is spreading knowledge by commercial means. What finally gives a product life is still the sincerity and professionalism of the content. There is no shortcut in knowledge; what one pays for should be a starting point, not a destination. The market is learning the same lesson: readers will pay again only when a course has truly changed something — a skill, a habit, or a way of seeing. In this sense, paying for knowledge is not a product but a promise.

lessons.chinese: 清晨送报、白天开车、晚上直播，一个人同时拥有几份收入来源，正在成为一种常见的工作方式。这背后是零工经济的兴起：企业按需用工，劳动者按单取酬。零工经济给劳动者带来了自由，人们可以灵活安排时间，选择喜欢的工作。它也给企业降低了成本，提高了应对市场波动的弹性。然而，硬币总有另一面。如何在灵活性与保障之间找到平衡，成为各国共同面对的课题。一些国家开始探索新的制度，例如按单缴纳社会保险。零工经济不是对传统就业的简单补充，它正在重塑人们对于“工作”的理解。未来，或许“单位人”会越来越少，“手艺人”会越来越多。问题不在于零工是否应当存在，而在于它的底线在哪里：每单最低报酬、意外保险与休息的权利。底线画在哪里，决定新经济能否站稳。
lessons.english: Delivering newspapers in the morning, driving through the day, live-streaming at night — to have several sources of income at once is becoming a common way of working. Behind it is the rise of the gig economy: enterprises hire by need, and workers are paid by the task. The gig economy offers workers freedom, for people can arrange their time flexibly and choose the work they like. It also lowers the costs of enterprises and raises their flexibility in facing the waves of the market. The coin, however, has another side. How to strike a balance between flexibility and protection has become a question for all countries. Some have begun to explore new systems, for example paying social insurance by the order. The gig economy is not a simple supplement to traditional employment; it is reshaping people's understanding of "work". In the future, perhaps there will be fewer "employees of an organisation" and more "masters of a craft". The question is not whether gig work should exist, but what floor it should have: minimum pay per order, accident insurance, and the right to rest. Where that floor is set will decide whether the new economy stands on solid ground.

lessons.chinese: 曾经，一些国产品牌是“廉价”的代名词；如今，带有中国元素的产品成为年轻人的心头好，这股潮流被称为“国潮”。从运动鞋服到美妆产品，从电子产品到博物馆文创，国货的设计越来越时尚，品质不断提升。国潮兴起的原因是多方面的：中国制造的整体升级打下了品质基础，文化自信的增强点燃了消费热情，社交媒体的传播则放大了这一趋势。许多老字号也借势翻红，把传统工艺与现代审美结合起来，产品频频卖断货。国潮的本质，是文化认同在消费领域的表达。当一件国货能让年轻人自豪地背出门，它承载的就不只是商品，还有文化的底气。设计师走进博物馆寻找纹样，老匠人作为顾问出现在工作室；遗产与商业的边界正在被重画。有人警告文化不应沦为标志，年轻人却用订单作答：他们想要的，是一件有故事可讲的产品。
lessons.english: There was a time when some domestic brands stood for "cheap"; nowadays, products with Chinese elements have become the favourites of the young, and this trend is called "Guochao", the China wave. From sports shoes and clothing to beauty products, from electronics to museum souvenirs, the design of Chinese brands grows more fashionable, and their quality keeps improving. The rise of Guochao has many causes: the overall upgrading of Chinese manufacturing laid the base of quality, the growth of cultural confidence lit the fire of consumption, and social media spread the trend. Many time-honoured brands have also ridden the wave, combining traditional craft with modern taste, and their products are often sold out. The essence of Guochao is cultural identity expressed in consumption. When a Chinese product can be carried out of the door with pride, it carries not only goods, but the confidence of a culture. Designers travel to museums for patterns, and old craftsmen appear in studios as consultants; the boundary between heritage and commerce is being redrawn. Critics warn that culture should not be reduced to a logo, yet the young answer with their orders: what they want is a product with a story they can tell.

lessons.chinese: 十年前，无人机还是军事和航模爱好者的专属；如今，它已飞入千行百业。在农业领域，无人机为大片农田喷洒农药，效率是人工的数十倍；在电力巡检中，无人机代替工人攀爬铁塔；在应急救援里，无人机为灾区投送物资、勘察地形。表演领域的无人机编队，能在夜空中变换出复杂图案，成为大型活动的常客。行业快速发展的同时，监管也在跟进：划定禁飞区、实行实名登记，以保障公共安全。无人机的普及提出一个有趣的问题：当天空属于每一个人时，规则与自由如何平衡？答案将随着技术的发展逐渐清晰。农民、电力工人、影视人与救援者如今共享同一片天空，而天空的规则正在机器不断升空中书写。目前平衡尚在：实名登记、禁飞区与静默时段保住了秩序，也没有让产业停飞。一个国家如何共享天空，也许正是它如何共享未来的小小试验。
lessons.english: Ten years ago, drones belonged to the army and to model-aircraft fans; nowadays they have flown into every trade. In agriculture, drones spray pesticide over wide fields, dozens of times more efficient than manual work; in the inspection of power lines, drones climb the towers instead of workers; in emergency rescue, drones send supplies to disaster areas and survey the land. Chinese consumer drones in particular occupy the main share of the world market, flying from the factories of Shenzhen to every corner of the earth. Formations of drones in performance can turn in the night sky into complex patterns, and have become regular guests of large events. The spread of drones raises an interesting question: when the sky belongs to everyone, how shall rules and freedom be balanced? The answer will become clear as the technology develops. Farmers, power-line workers, film-makers and rescuers now share one sky, and the rules of the sky are being written while the machines keep rising. So far the balance holds: registration, zones and quiet hours have kept the order without grounding the industry. How a country shares its sky may become a small test of how it shares its future.

lessons.chinese: 中国的水资源分布极不均衡：南方水多，北方水少。为解决这一难题，南水北调工程应运而生，东、中两条线路先后通水，把长江流域的水送往华北大地。工程之艰巨世界罕见：中线干渠全长一千四百多公里，跨越数百条河流；通水以来，累计调水超过五百亿立方米，北京城区七成以上的供水来自南水北调，数千万人口因此受益。干渠所过之处，生态也在改善，地下水位回升，河湖重现生机。南水北调不仅是一项水利工程，更是一部人与自然协商的历史。它提醒人们：水是宝贵的资源，节约每一滴水，与调来每一滴水同样重要。
lessons.english: Water resources in China are most unevenly distributed: the south has much water, the north has little. To solve this problem, the South-to-North Water Diversion Project was born. The eastern and middle routes began to supply water one after another, carrying water from the Yangtze basin to the land of North China. To protect the water quality, large numbers of polluting enterprises along the line were closed, and ecological compensation reached hundreds of thousands of people who moved. Since the water arrived, the total transferred has exceeded fifty billion cubic metres; more than seventy per cent of the water supply of urban Beijing comes from the project, and tens of millions of people have benefited. Where the canal passes, the ecology improves as well: the underground water level rises, and rivers and lakes live again. The South-to-North Water Diversion is not only a water project; it is a history of negotiation between human beings and nature. It reminds people that water is a precious resource, and saving every drop matters as much as moving every drop.

lessons.chinese: 中国已向世界郑重承诺：二氧化碳排放力争在2030年前达到峰值，努力在2060年前实现碳中和。碳中和并非停止发展，而是要完成一场能源结构的深刻变革。具体路径包括：大力发展风电和光伏，让清洁电力成为主体能源；推动工业、交通和建筑领域的电气化改造；挑战同样巨大：煤炭在能源结构中占比仍然较高，部分地区的转型需要时间和资金。值得注意的是，新能源汽车、光伏产业等新兴领域，正把减排压力转化为发展动力。碳中和是一场面向未来的长跑，它考验的不是速度，而是一代人的坚持。转型同样带来公平之问：煤炭产区需要新产业，劳动者需要在新技能过时前学会它。碳中和的承诺，只有在没有人被抛下时才可信。就此而言，路本身与目的地同样重要。
lessons.english: China has made a solemn promise to the world: carbon dioxide emissions will strive to peak before 2030, and carbon neutrality will be pursued before 2060. Carbon neutrality does not mean stopping development; it means completing a deep transformation of the structure of energy. The path includes developing wind and solar power on a large scale, so that clean electricity becomes the main source of energy; pushing the electrification of industry, transport and buildings; and planting forests to absorb the emissions that cannot be avoided. What deserves attention is that emerging fields such as new energy vehicles and the photovoltaic industry are turning the pressure of reduction into the force of development. Carbon neutrality is a long race towards the future, and what it tests is not speed but the persistence of a generation. The transition also carries questions of fairness: coal-mining regions need new industries, and workers need new skills before the old ones fade. The promise of carbon neutrality, therefore, is credible only when nobody is abandoned on the road. In this sense, the road itself is as important as the destination.

lessons.title_en: Cities, and How to Make Them Livable
lessons.chinese: 过去几十年，世界上越来越多的人搬进了城市。城市创造了财富与机会，也带来了拥堵、污染和高房价。如何让城市更宜居住，成为各国共同面对的问题。一些城市的探索值得借鉴：哥本哈根把街道还给自行车，骑行通勤的比例接近一半；中国的许多城市建起了十五分钟生活圈，居民步行可达菜场、学校和诊所。研究发现，决定城市生活质量的，往往不是地标建筑的高度，而是日常生活的便利程度。绿地的可达性、街道的安全感、公共空间的活力，这些看似细小的因素，塑造着人们对城市的感受。一座伟大的城市，最终不在于它有多少摩天大楼，而在于它如何对待其中最普通的居民。许多最好的点子都很小：更宽的人行道、遮荫的树、面向落日的长椅，以及住商混合让日常所需无需开车。宜居城市不是被一笔宏伟规划设计出来的，而是由成千上万个这样的细节拼装而成。
lessons.english: In the past few decades, more and more people in the world have moved into cities. Cities have created wealth and opportunity, but also congestion, pollution and high housing prices. How to make cities more livable has become a question shared by all countries. Research shows that what decides the quality of urban life is often not the height of landmark buildings, but the convenience of daily life. The reachability of green space, the sense of safety on streets, the life of public spaces — these small-seeming factors shape how people feel about a city. A great city, in the end, is measured not by how many towers of glass it owns, but by how it treats its most ordinary residents. Many of the best ideas are small: wider pavements, trees for shade, benches facing the sunset, shops mixed with homes so that daily needs need no car. Livable cities are not designed in one grand plan; they are assembled from thousands of such details.

lessons.chinese: 在云南北部的高山针叶林里，科研人员用红外相机记录下滇金丝猴一家觅食的画面。这种有着红色嘴唇的灵长类动物，是中国特有的濒危物种。它们的存续，依赖整片森林的健康，而森林的健康，又依赖其中的每一种生物。这就是生物多样性：物种之间、物种与环境之间，结成了一张精密的生命之网。一个物种的消失，往往引发连锁反应。研究显示，人类活动正使物种灭绝的速度大幅加快，保护生物多样性刻不容缓。中国的努力包括建立以国家公园为主体的保护地体系，实施长江十年禁渔。保护自然不是发展的对立面；守住了生命之网，就是守住了人类自己的未来。科学家估计，仍有数百万物种未被命名，许多或许在我们相遇之前就会消失。每一个物种的消逝，都是合上一本没读完的书。因此，保护生物多样性不是多愁善感，而是审慎：我们的药物、作物与气候，都系于那张网。
lessons.english: In the coniferous forests of the northern mountains of Yunnan, researchers with infrared cameras have recorded a family of black-and-white snub-nosed monkeys searching for food. This primate, with its red lips, is an endangered species found only in China. Its survival depends on the health of the whole forest, and the health of the forest depends on every living thing within it. This is biodiversity: between species, and between species and their environment, a precise web of life has been woven. The efforts of China include building a system of protected areas with national parks as the main body, and the ten-year ban on fishing in the Yangtze. Protecting nature is not the opposite of development; to keep the web of life whole is to keep the future of human beings ourselves. Scientists estimate that there are millions of species still unnamed, and many may disappear before we ever meet them. Each loss closes a book we never finished reading. Protecting biodiversity, therefore, is not sentiment but prudence: our medicine, our crops and our climate all rest on that web.

lessons.title_cn: 为什么我们买了不需要的东西
lessons.title_en: Why We Buy What We Do Not Need
lessons.chinese: 打开衣柜，你会发现许多吊牌从未剪开的衣服；打开手机，购物车里还躺着上次的冲动。为什么人们总是购买自己并不需要的东西？心理学给出了几个解释。其一是稀缺错觉：限时、限量的话术，让大脑把“怕错过”误当作“需要”。其三是社会比较：朋友圈里的新款和别人家的装修，悄悄改写了“必需品”的定义。破解之道并非拒绝消费，而是建立消费的“延迟机制”——把想买的物品先放七天，多数冲动会自行消退。看清欲望的来路，才能守住钱包，更守住内心的秩序。商店让购买变得容易、退回变得困难；广告总在工资到账前抵达。然而看清机器，就已经自由了一半：一旦明白那股引力是被设计出来的，你就能问出一个更好的问题——我想要这件东西，还是想要它许诺的感觉？
lessons.english: Open your wardrobe and you will find clothes whose tags have never been cut; open your phone and the shopping cart still holds the last impulse. Why do people keep buying what they do not need? Psychology offers several explanations. One is the illusion of scarcity: the words "limited time, limited stock" make the brain mistake the fear of missing out for a need. A third is social comparison — the new models in a friend's feed and the decoration of other people's homes quietly rewrite the definition of "necessary". The way out is not to refuse consumption, but to build a "delaying mechanism": keep the thing you want for seven days first, and most impulses will fade on their own. To see clearly where desire comes from is to protect your wallet — and, more than that, the order of your mind.
