Stores make it easy to buy and hard to return; advertising arrives before the salary does. Seeing the machinery, however, is already half of freedom: once you know the pull is designed, you can ask a better question — do I want this thing, or do I want the feeling it promises?

lessons.chinese: 你有没有过这样的经历：打开手机想查一个单词，二十分钟后却发现自己刷完了三条视频。注意力被切碎，正在成为信息时代的普遍症状。神经科学的研究表明，每一次任务切换，大脑都需要时间重新进入状态，频繁切换的代价是效率的成倍损失。更值得警惕的是，算法推送专门迎合人的好奇心，让“再看一条”变得难以抗拒。实验显示，经过几周训练，受试者的专注时长明显提升。注意力是这个时代最稀缺的资源，它决定我们成为什么样的人。夺回注意力的方法并不复杂：给重要的事留出不被打扰的时间，然后守住它。大脑不像机器，每一次切换都要付出代价：研究比较多任务者与轻任务者，发现前者过滤重要信息的能力更差。研究者给出的建议近乎老派——一次只做一件事，做完，再轮到手机。
lessons.english: Have you had this experience: you opened your phone to look up a word, and twenty minutes later you found you had finished three videos? Attention cut into pieces is becoming a common symptom of the information age. Research in neuroscience shows that at every switch of tasks the brain needs time to re-enter its state, and the cost of frequent switching is a many-fold loss of efficiency. More worthy of caution is that algorithms push content made to please human curiosity, making "one more video" almost impossible to resist. Experiments show that after weeks of training the span of attention of the subjects clearly lengthens. Attention is the scarcest resource of this age, and it decides what kind of person we become. The way to take attention back is not complicated: leave an undisturbed hour for what matters, and then guard it. The brain, unlike a machine, pays for every switch: studies compare heavy multitaskers with light users and find the heavy ones worse at filtering what matters. The advice of researchers is almost old-fashioned — do one thing at a time, finish it, and then allow the phone its turn.

lessons.chinese: 熬夜，正在成为许多人的生活常态。有人加班，有人刷手机，还有人坚信自己“天生少觉”。科学研究却给出了不同的答案：成年人每晚需要七到九小时的睡眠，长期不足会损害记忆、免疫力和情绪调节能力。睡眠并非时间的浪费，而是大脑的深度维护——在深睡阶段，大脑会清理白天积累的代谢废物，巩固白天学到的知识。改善睡眠的建议大多朴素：睡前远离屏幕，卧室保持黑暗安静，下午之后避免咖啡因。在崇尚奋斗的时代，睡眠常被视为可以牺牲的成本。事实恰恰相反：睡好觉，才是高效与健康的起点。学校与职场开始把睡眠当作基础设施：更晚的到校时间、安静的休息室，以及把休息写进日程而非视为日程之敌的勇气。一个尊重睡眠的社会，会发现清晨更明亮、错误更少、灵感恰好抵达需要它的地方。
lessons.english: Staying up late is becoming the normal life of many. Some work overtime, some scroll their phones, and some believe they are "born short sleepers". Science, however, answers differently: adults need seven to nine hours of sleep every night, and long-term lack of it harms memory, immunity and the control of feelings. Sleep is not a waste of time but the deep maintenance of the brain — in the stage of deep sleep, the brain clears the waste gathered in the day and strengthens what was learned by day. The advice for better sleep is mostly plain: keep away from screens before bed, keep the bedroom dark and quiet, and avoid caffeine after the afternoon. In an age that honours hard work, sleep is often treated as a cost that can be sacrificed. The truth is the opposite: to sleep well is where efficiency and health begin. Schools and workplaces are beginning to treat sleep as infrastructure: later start times, quiet rooms and the courage to say that rest is part of the timetable, not the enemy of it. A society that honours sleep may find mornings brighter, mistakes fewer, and ideas arriving exactly where they are needed.

lessons.chinese: 不同语言的使用者，看到的世界是否不同？语言学家发现了一个有趣的例子：某些语言中没有“左”“右”的词汇，人们习惯用东南西北来描述位置，因此无论走到哪里，始终知道北方在哪。另有研究发现，语言的时态划分，会影响人们对时间的感知。这些现象支持了一种观点：语言不只是思想的载体，它也在塑造思想。当然，这并不意味着语言决定了思维的全部——不会说“雪”这个词的人，照样能认识雪。学习一门外语，因此不仅是掌握交流工具，更是获得一种新的看待世界的方式。理解他人，常常从理解对方的语言开始。实验显示，没有将来时态的语言，其使用者储蓄更多，也许因为在那种语法里，未来显得更近；给物体分阴阳性别的语言，使用者对事物的记忆方式也不同。这些效应没有一个是魔法，但合在一起勾勒出一个惊人的想法：语法是一种注意力的习惯。学习另一门语言，我们不只是增加词汇——我们在练习另一种习惯。
lessons.english: Do speakers of different languages see the world differently? Linguists have found an interesting example: some languages have no words for "left" and "right"; their speakers describe position by north, south, east and west, and therefore know where north is wherever they go. Other research suggests that the way a language divides time can shape how its speakers feel time. These findings support one view: language is not only the carrier of thought — it also shapes thought. But vocabulary and grammar are indeed like a pair of coloured glasses, making us more sensitive to some sides of the world. To learn one more language is to have one more pair of eyes; to understand others often begins with understanding their language. Experiments suggest that speakers of languages without future tenses save more money, perhaps because tomorrow feels nearer; speakers of languages that assign genders to objects remember them differently. None of these effects is magic, but together they sketch a striking thought: grammar is a habit of attention. In learning another language, we are not only adding words — we are practising another set of habits.

lessons.chinese: 如今，预约一家热门博物馆的门票，难度不亚于抢一场演唱会。博物馆热的背后，是多重因素的叠加：文物类综艺让沉睡的藏品“活”了起来，文创产品把历史装进了日常生活，年轻一代的文化自信日益增强。博物馆也在主动求变：策展方式从“器物陈列”转向“故事讲述”，导览借助增强现实技术，观众可以在展柜旁看到文物千年前的模样。博物馆热的实质，是公众与历史关系的重构：文物不再只是玻璃柜中的研究对象，而是可以被欣赏、被讨论、被热爱的文化伙伴。当年轻人愿意为一件文物排两个小时的队，历史就有了新的讲述者。热潮也有它的考题：人气带来人流，人流带来保护与空间的老问题。那些能同时做到两件事的博物馆——既欢迎公众又守护文物——会把这波热情变成一座城市长久的习惯。
lessons.english: Nowadays, booking a ticket for a popular museum is hardly easier than grabbing a seat at a concert. Behind the museum boom, several forces have come together: television shows on relics have woken the sleeping collections, cultural and creative products have carried history into daily life, and the cultural confidence of the young generation keeps growing. Museums have been changing themselves as well: the way of curating has turned from "showing objects" to "telling stories", guides make use of augmented reality, and visitors can see, beside the case, how a relic looked a thousand years ago. The essence of the boom is the rebuilding of the relation between the public and history: relics are no longer objects of research behind glass, but cultural partners to be enjoyed, discussed and loved. When the young are willing to queue two hours for one relic, history has found its new storytellers. The boom has its tests: popularity brings crowds, and crowds bring the old questions of protection and space. The museums that manage both — welcoming the public and guarding the relics — will turn this wave of enthusiasm into a lasting habit of the city.

lessons.chinese: 山区老人足不出户就能得到城市专家的诊断，这样的场景正在通过远程医疗变为日常。借助视频连线与可穿戴设备，医生可以查看患者的实时数据，进行复诊随访和用药指导。远程医疗的价值在医疗资源分布不均的背景下尤为突出：优质医生集中于大城市，而基层与偏远地区长期缺医少药。疫情期间，互联网医院数量快速增长，医保支付也逐步覆盖线上问诊。当优质医疗资源能够跨越山海，健康这件事，才会离每个人更近一些。边界由技术与信任共同划定：影像可以传送，但亲手触诊不能省略；数据可以远行，但责任必须落在一个有名有姓的医生身上。随着实践推开，关于责任、执业与隐私的规则正在成形。远程医疗不会取代医院；它可能取代的，是那句“我家附近没有医生”。
lessons.english: An old man in the mountains can receive the diagnosis of a city expert without leaving home — such scenes are becoming daily life through telemedicine. With video links and wearable devices, doctors can read the real-time data of patients, carry out follow-up visits and give advice on medicine. The value of telemedicine stands out against the uneven spread of medical resources: good doctors gather in big cities, while grassroots and remote areas have long lacked medical care. The direction of the technology is complement rather than replacement — online services take care of common and chronic diseases, while offline hospitals focus on difficult and serious cases. When good medical resources can cross mountains and seas, health will come a little closer to everyone. The limits are drawn by technology and by trust: images can be sent, but hands still must examine; data can travel, but responsibility must remain with a named doctor. Rules on liability, licensing and privacy are being written as the practice grows. Telemedicine will not replace hospitals; what it may replace is the sentence "there is no doctor near me".

lessons.chinese: 一项针对创业者的追踪研究发现，早期经历过失败的公司，其后续成功率反而高于一路顺风的同行。类似的现象也出现在科学界：许多重大发现，诞生于一系列“失败”的实验。心理学把这种能力称为“心理韧性”——从挫折中恢复并继续前行的力量。研究指出，韧性并非天生，它可以像肌肉一样训练。这些研究共同指向一个结论：决定成就的，往往不是是否失败，而是如何解释失败。会与失败相处的人，把每一次跌倒都变成了路标。学校可以通过允许安全的失败来教它——在某些科目里，错误的答案只是信息而非羞耻。家庭在餐桌上谈论自己挫折的方式，也是一种教育。企业则用庆祝什么来教它：一次漂亮的挽回，常常比一次侥幸的胜利更值得注意。这样看来，韧性不是一种私人美德，而是人与人彼此营造的环境。
lessons.english: A follow-up study of founders found that companies which had failed early showed a higher rate of later success than those whose road had been smooth. Similar phenomena appear in science: many great discoveries were born from a series of "failed" experiments. Psychology calls this ability "resilience" — the strength to recover from setbacks and go on. Research points out that resilience is not inborn; it can be trained like a muscle. These studies point to one conclusion: what decides achievement is often not whether one fails, but how one explains failure. Those who know how to live with failure turn every fall into a signpost on the road. Schools can teach it by allowing safe failure — subjects where a wrong answer is information, not shame. Families teach it by how they speak of their own setbacks at dinner. And companies teach it by what they celebrate: a clever recovery often deserves more attention than a lucky win. Seen this way, resilience is not a private virtue but an environment that people build around one another.

lessons.chinese: 孟子在两千多年前写道：“老吾老，以及人之老。”意思是，尊敬自己的长辈，并把这份尊敬推及别人的长辈。这句古训，在今天有了新的注脚。城市化让许多子女远离父母，空巢老人数量持续增加；在一些城市，年轻人以低价入住养老院，用陪伴换取房租，代际之间因此重新连接。研究显示，频繁的代际交流，能显著缓解老年人的孤独感。孝道的形式在变化，内核却始终如一：让每一位老人感到自己没有被遗忘。当敬老从家庭美德扩展为社会共识，老龄化就不再只是挑战，更是一个社会成熟的标志。制度是新的，底下的情感却很旧：没有人愿意在自己变老的地方成为陌生人。记得这一点的城市，会建造的不只是照护，更是连接——步行可达的诊所、向阳的长椅，以及专门留给老人与年轻人说话的时间。
lessons.english: More than two thousand years ago, Mencius wrote: "Honour the aged of your own family, and extend that honour to the aged of all families. " The old teaching has a new footnote today. Urbanisation has taken many children far from their parents, and the number of empty-nest elderly keeps rising; at the same time, the social system of care for the old is growing fast. Research shows that frequent exchange between generations can greatly ease the loneliness of the old. The form of filial piety is changing, but its heart remains the same: to let every old person feel that he or she has not been forgotten. When honouring the aged grows from a family virtue into a social consensus, an ageing society is no longer only a challenge — it becomes a sign of the maturity of a society. The systems are new, but the feeling underneath is old: no one wishes to be a stranger in the place where they grew old. Cities that remember this will build not only care but connection — clinics within walking distance, benches in the sun, and time set aside for the young and the old to simply talk.

lessons.title_en: Public Space at the Street Corner
lessons.chinese: 一座城市的品质，往往藏在它的街角。一条可以坐下来的长椅，一处遮阳的连廊，一片让孩子们奔跑的空地——这些微小的公共空间，深刻影响着市民的幸福感。城市研究者发现，人们对自己城市最深的记忆，很少来自地标建筑，而多来自日常生活发生的场所：门口的菜市场、街角的早点摊、傍晚的滨河步道。近年来，中国的许多城市开始重视公共空间的更新：拆除公园围墙，改造桥下空间，把闲置地块变成口袋公园。一个空无一人的广场，无论多么气派，都是设计的失败。它是一座城市写给市民的情书。城市规划者有一个词形容宜居的反面：“无场所感”——那种街道上没有一样东西属于任何人、也没有人愿意停留的地方。药方通常并不昂贵，是关注。当一座城市开始在乎街角，它就在开始在乎人，其余往往随之而来。
lessons.english: The quality of a city often hides at its street corners. A bench one may sit on, a covered walk against the sun, an open ground where children can run — these tiny public spaces deeply shape the happiness of citizens. Researchers of cities have found that people's deepest memories of their city rarely come from landmark buildings; they come from the places of daily life — the market at the gate, the breakfast stall at the corner, the riverside path in the evening. In recent years, many Chinese cities have begun to care about the renewal of public space: the walls of parks have been taken down, the space under bridges rebuilt, and idle lots turned into pocket parks. A square with no one on it, however grand, is a failure of design. It is a love letter a city writes to its citizens. Urban planners have a word for the opposite of a livable city: "placelessness" — streets where nothing belongs to anyone and no one has a reason to stay. The cure is rarely expensive; it is attention. When a city begins to care about corners, it has begun to care about people, and the rest usually follows.

lessons.title_en: Trust on the Tip of the Tongue
lessons.chinese: 食品安全，是公众关注度极高的话题。一顿饭的背后，是一条漫长的链条：种植养殖、加工储运、餐饮制作，任何一个环节失守，风险都会传递到餐桌。近年来，中国的食品安全治理明显加严：追溯体系逐步建立，问题食品可以被快速定位与召回；“明厨亮灶”工程把后厨搬上屏幕，接受顾客监督。研究表明，监管最有效的场景，是违规成本远高于违规收益的时候。因此，重罚与重奖并行成为趋势。食品安全没有旁观者：生产者的自律、监管者的严格、消费者的较真，共同构成了一餐桌上的信任。信任一旦重建，受益的将是整个社会。链条同样延伸进自家厨房：食物如何清洗、储存与加热，其影响不亚于任何一条生产线。公共宣传开始教基础课——生熟砧板分开、及时冷藏、留意日期——因为最后一道防线，正是拿起筷子的人。
lessons.english: Food safety is a subject of the highest public concern. Behind one meal lies a long chain — planting and breeding, processing, storage and transport, cooking and serving; if any link fails, the risk travels to the table. In recent years, the governance of food safety in China has clearly hardened: tracing systems have been built step by step, so that problem food can be quickly located and recalled; the "bright kitchen" project has moved the kitchen onto screens to accept the supervision of customers. Technology is playing its part too — blockchain makes the origin and flow of food checkable and provable. Hence the trend of pairing heavy punishment with real reward. In food safety there are no bystanders: the self-discipline of producers, the strictness of regulators and the seriousness of consumers together build the trust on the tip of the tongue. Once that trust is rebuilt, the whole society is the beneficiary. The chain also runs through kitchens at home: how food is washed, stored and reheated decides as much as any factory line. Public campaigns now teach the basics — separate chopping boards, proper cooling, careful dates — because the last line of defence is the person holding the chopsticks.

lessons.title_en: A World of Cultures, and Cultures of the World
lessons.chinese: 全球化让世界前所未有地紧密，也引发了一个古老问题的现代版：不同文化将走向趋同，还是保持多样？街头随处可见的连锁品牌，让人担心地方文化的消失；而另一边，方言保护、传统节日的复兴又在世界各地发生。事实或许比二元对立更复杂：文化交流从来不是单向替代，而是相互滋养。对个人而言，文化多样性的价值在于选择：人们可以既读莎士比亚，也品唐诗宋词。文明因多样而有交流的价值，因互鉴而有前进的动力。一个自信的文化，从不害怕与别的文化相遇。对同质化的恐惧自有其答案：从来没有纯粹的文化，每一种文化都是过往交流的记录，如压进书页的叶子。重要的是接下来压进哪一片新叶，以及这本书是否继续敞开。说到底，多样性不是博物馆的政策，而是一种日常的好奇心实践。
lessons.english: Globalisation has bound the world more tightly than ever, and it has raised a modern version of an old question: will different cultures move towards sameness, or keep their diversity? The chain brands on every street make people fear the loss of local culture; on the other side, the protection of dialects and the revival of traditional festivals are happening everywhere. The truth is probably more complex than the two-way opposition: cultural exchange has never been one-way replacement, but mutual nourishment. Chopsticks and knives may lie on the same table, and Peking Opera may share a theatre with a symphony. Civilisations owe their value of exchange to diversity, and their force to move forward to learning from one another. A culture with self-confidence has never feared meeting another. The fear of sameness has its own answer: no culture has ever been pure; each is the record of past exchanges, pressed like leaves in a book. What matters is which new leaves we press next, and whether the book remains open. Diversity, in the end, is not a museum policy but a daily practice of curiosity.

lessons.chinese: 学术诚信是科学研究的地基。一篇论文的价值，建立在数据真实、引用规范的基础上；一旦造假被揭露，损害的不仅是个人的声誉，更是公众对科学整体的信任。近年来，国内外多起学术不端事件引发关注，论文撤稿数量上升，促使各研究机构收紧制度。学者们也在反思评价体系——当论文数量与职称、经费直接挂钩时，急功近利便有了土壤。对青年研究者而言，最重要的提醒或许是：科学史上被记住的，从来不是发表最多的人，而是让人类认知边界向外推进一寸的人。诚实，是这一寸的前提。一些高校开设了研究伦理课程，期刊要求作者公开结果背后的步骤。它们的讯息一致：科学的速度取决于对科学的信任，而信任的建立很慢，失去很快。
lessons.english: Academic integrity is the foundation of scientific research. The value of a paper rests on true data and proper citation; once fraud is exposed, what is harmed is not only the reputation of one person, but the trust of the public in science as a whole. In recent years, cases of academic misconduct at home and abroad have drawn attention, the number of withdrawn papers has risen, and research institutions have tightened their rules. The means of governance grow various: systems checking repetition have become standard, software for detecting false images has been put to use, and some universities require open original data. For young researchers, the most important reminder may be this: what history of science remembers has never been the person who published the most, but the person who pushed the border of human knowledge an inch farther. Honesty is the premise of that inch. Some universities now run courses in research ethics, and journals ask authors to share the steps behind their results. The message is consistent across all of them: the speed of science is set by the trust in it, and trust is slow to build and quick to lose.

lessons.chinese: 扫码点餐、人脸识别、智能推荐，技术让生活越来越便利，但每一次便利的背后，往往是一次个人信息的让渡。你的位置轨迹、消费记录、面部特征，正以数据的形态被收集、存储和分析。数据是新时代的石油，驱动着精准营销与智能服务，也埋下了滥用与泄露的风险。近年来，个人信息保护立法密集出台，明确收集数据须遵循“知情、同意、最小必要”原则，大型平台因违规处理数据被处以高额罚款。关键在于规则的设计者与技术的使用者，是否把人的权利放在中心。法律画一条线，日常选择画另一条：我们读过自己点下“同意”的协议吗？我们会问一个应用为什么需要这些信息吗？千万用户的习惯，也是一种立法。当用户开始追问为什么，便利与隐私就不再是一对敌人，而成为一个设计问题。
lessons.english: Ordering by scanning a code, paying with a face, recommendations by algorithm — technology makes life ever more convenient, but behind every convenience there is often a handing-over of personal information. Your location, your records of consumption, the features of your face are being gathered, stored and analysed in the form of data. Data is the oil of the new age: it drives precise marketing and intelligent services, and it also buries the risk of misuse and leakage. In recent years, legislation on the protection of personal information has appeared thick and fast, making clear that gathering data must follow the principles of "knowledge, consent and the least necessary", and large platforms have been fined heavily for mishandling data. What matters is whether the makers of rules and the users of technology put the rights of the person at the centre. The law draws one line, and daily choice draws another: do we read the agreements we click? Do we ask what an app needs to know before it needs it? The habits of millions are also a kind of legislation. When users start asking why, convenience and privacy stop being a pair of enemies and become a question of design.

lessons.title_en: Great Changes in the Mountain Villages
lessons.chinese: 历史上，贫困是人类社会的长期现象。而在过去八年间，中国实现了现行标准下近一亿农村贫困人口全部脱贫。这场脱贫攻坚战规模空前：数百万名干部驻村帮扶，超过十万所学校的营养餐覆盖贫困地区，易地搬迁让生活在“不适宜人类居住”地区的人们迁入新居。当然，巩固脱贫成果仍需长期努力，防止返贫的监测机制已经建立。山乡的巨变证明：消除极端贫困并非遥不可及的梦想，关键在于持续的行动与精准的方法。更深的考验在于成果能否守住：孩子仍在课堂，田地仍有人耕种，年轻人仍找得到留下的理由。监测系统盯着数字，但真正的保证是机会——家门口的工作、值得上的学校、召之即来的诊所。
lessons.english: Through history, poverty was a lasting condition of human society. Yet in the past eight years, China has lifted nearly a hundred million rural people out of poverty under the present standard. The scale of the battle was without precedent: millions of officials went to live in villages to help, nutritious meals provided by more than a hundred thousand schools reached poor areas, and people living in places "unfit for human dwelling" moved into new homes. Consolidating the gains, of course, still needs long effort, and a monitoring system to prevent a return to poverty has been set up. The great changes in the mountain villages prove that ending extreme poverty is not a distant dream; what matters is continuous action and precise methods. The deeper test is whether the gains can hold: children still in school, fields still tended, young people still finding reasons to stay. Monitoring systems watch the numbers, but the real guarantee is opportunity — work near home, schools worth attending, and clinics that answer when called.

lessons.title_en: A New Silk Road, New Stories
lessons.chinese: 两千年前，驼队载着丝绸与瓷器横穿大陆；今天，中欧班列载着电子产品与汽车配件呼啸往返。共建“一带一路”倡议提出十余年来，从理念变为行动，从蓝图变为现实。基础设施的联通最为直观：蒙内铁路让肯尼亚有了现代化铁路，雅万高铁结束了印尼没有高铁的历史。项目也带来了争议与讨论，例如债务可持续性与环境影响，中方对此的回应是不断完善的规则与标准。丝绸之路自古就是双向的奔赴。新的故事里，最主要的角色不是钢筋水泥，而是彼此的需求与信任。沿着新路线，古老的名字重新出现在时刻表与货运单上——撒马尔罕、蒙巴萨、杜伊斯堡。“倡议”一词用得贴切：倡议等待加入，每个国家都在书写属于自己的那一页。
lessons.english: Two thousand years ago, camel caravans carried silk and porcelain across the continent; today, freight trains between China and Europe race back and forth with electronics and motor parts. More than ten years have passed since the Belt and Road Initiative was proposed, and it has moved from idea to action, from blueprint to reality. The joining of infrastructure is the most visible part: the railway in Kenya gave that country a modern railway, and the high-speed railway in Indonesia ended its history of having none. The figures of trade and investment are equally bright: trade between China and the partner countries has kept growing. The Silk Road was from the beginning a road of two directions. In the new story, the leading roles are not steel and cement, but the needs and trust of one another. Along the new routes, old names are heard again — Samarkand, Mombasa, Duisburg — in timetables and shipping lists. The word "initiative" suits it well: an initiative waits to be joined, and every country writes its own part of the story.

lessons.title_en: The Legacy of Ice and Snow
lessons.chinese: 北京成为世界上首座既举办过夏季、又举办过冬季奥运会的城市。盛会落幕之后，留下了什么？场馆是最直观的遗产：“冰丝带”国家速滑馆采用二氧化碳跨临界制冰技术，既环保又高效，赛后向公众开放，成为市民滑冰的好去处。还有一份遗产属于人：数万名志愿者学会了国际交往，青少年爱上了雪道与冰场。研究表明，大型赛事的经济效益通常在赛后数年显现，关键在于赛后的规划。冬奥留下的不只是一批场馆和纪录，更是一种可能性的证明：冰雪运动并非北方与富人的专属，它可以属于每一个愿意尝试的人。其他曾举办盛会城市中的某些场馆后来陷入沉寂；北京的经验，是在第一场比赛之前，就规划好最后一场比赛之后的每一天。
lessons.english: Beijing has become the first city in the world to hold both a Summer and a Winter Olympic Games. When the event ended, what did it leave behind? The venues are the most visible legacy: the National Speed Skating Oval, known as the "Ice Ribbon", uses a technique of carbon-dioxide trans-critical ice-making that is both green and efficient; after the Games it opened to the public and became a fine place for citizens to skate. Another legacy belongs to people: tens of thousands of volunteers learned international exchange, and teenagers fell in love with the slopes and the rinks. Research shows that the economic benefit of large games usually appears in the years after them, and the key lies in the planning for the time after. What the Winter Olympics left is not only venues and records, but the proof of a possibility: winter sports are not the property of the north and the rich; they can belong to everyone willing to try. Cities that hosted the games elsewhere have sometimes watched their stadiums fall quiet; the lesson of Beijing is to plan the day after the last race from the day before the first one.

lessons.chinese: 气候、疫情、粮食安全——当今世界面临的重大挑战，没有一项可以被单个国家独自解决。“人类命运共同体”由此成为一个高频词，它的含义朴素而深刻：各国的命运紧密相连，合作不是选项，而是必需。这一理念正在诸多领域落地：全球疫苗合作让欠发达国家获得保护，多国联合科研让望远镜和探测器飞向深空，气候协定让减排成为共同承诺。当然，现实中合作常被竞争干扰，信任赤字仍然存在。仰望星空，人类共享同一片穹顶；俯瞰地球，所有边界都淡成一墨色的整体。这句理念终将接受无人能预料的检验。但只要它在实践，方向就是清晰的：共享疫苗、共享卫星、共享标准——都是“问题被分担即减半”的小小证明。在一个筑墙的世纪里，选择造桥，本身就是一种政策。
lessons.english: Climate, epidemics, food security — none of the great challenges facing the world today can be solved by any single country alone. "A community with a shared future for mankind" has thus become a phrase of high frequency, and its meaning is plain and deep: the fates of nations are joined together, and cooperation is not an option but a necessity. The idea is landing in many fields: global cooperation on vaccines has brought protection to less developed countries; joint research by many nations has sent telescopes and probes into deep space; agreements on climate have made reduction a common promise. In reality, of course, cooperation is often disturbed by competition, and the deficit of trust still exists. Looking up at the stars, human beings share one dome of sky; looking down at the earth, all borders fade into one coat of ink-dark land. The phrase will be tested by events no one can schedule. Yet its direction is clear wherever it is practised: shared vaccines, shared satellites, shared standards — small proofs that problems shared are problems halved. In a century of new walls, choosing to build bridges is itself a policy.

lessons.chinese: 曾几何时，占有更多被视为成功的标志；如今，一种被称为“极简主义”的生活方式正在世界各地的城市中兴起。它的主张十分朴素：减少物品的数量，把时间和金钱留给真正重要的事情。追随者并非苦行僧，他们也会消费，只是更看重品质与用途，而非数量与新鲜感。这种转变的背后，是多重社会因素的叠加。住房成本的上扬，使小户型成为常态，物品的堆积因此成了负担；社交媒体的展示效应，则让“拥有什么”被“经历什么”所取代。研究消费行为的学者指出，极简主义的流行，本质上是对过度消费的一次集体反思。值得注意的是，极简主义自身也可能被商业化，成为新的营销概念。但即便如此，它提出的问题依然有效：在物质极大丰富的时代，我们究竟需要多少东西？
lessons.english: There was a time when owning more was taken as the mark of success; nowadays, a way of life known as minimalism is rising in cities around the world. Its proposition is plain: reduce the number of possessions, and leave time and money to what truly matters. Its followers are not ascetics; they still consume, but they care more about quality and use than about quantity and novelty. Behind this shift lies the accumulation of several social forces. The rise of housing costs has made small apartments the norm, turning the piling up of objects into a burden; the display effect of social media has replaced "what you own" with "what you experience". Scholars of consumer behaviour point out that the popularity of minimalism is, in essence, a collective reflection on over-consumption. It is worth noting that minimalism itself may be commercialised into a new marketing concept. Yet even so, the question it raises remains valid: in an age of material abundance, how many things do we actually need?

lessons.chinese: 从流媒体、软件到健身课程，订阅制正在重塑商业的形态。企业不再追求一次性的买卖，而是与用户建立长期关系，按月或按年收取费用。对企业而言，订阅制的吸引力在于收入的可预期性：稳定的服务费让规划变得容易，也让投资者更愿意埋单。对用户而言，它的好处是低门槛与持续更新，用不高的月费换取不断升级的产品。然而，订阅经济也有它的阴影。当所有服务都改为按月收费，人们的总支出可能在不知不觉中膨胀；一些企业则刻意提高取消服务的难度，把用户留在付费名单里。监管者已经开始关注这类“暗模式”。订阅经济的未来，取决于一个朴素的判断：只有真正持续创造价值的企业，才配得上持续收到账单的用户。
lessons.english: From streaming media and software to fitness classes, the subscription model is reshaping the form of business. Instead of pursuing one-off sales, companies build long-term relationships with users and charge by month or by year. For enterprises, the attraction of subscriptions lies in the predictability of income: a stable stream of fees makes planning easier, and makes investors more willing to pay. For users, the benefit is a low threshold and continuous updating — a modest monthly fee in exchange for a product that keeps improving. The subscription economy, however, has its shadow. When all services turn to monthly charging, the total spending of a household may swell without anyone noticing; some companies deliberately raise the difficulty of cancelling, keeping users on their lists. Regulators have begun to watch such "dark patterns". The future of the subscription economy depends on a plain judgement: only enterprises that keep creating real value deserve users who keep receiving their bills.

lessons.chinese: 品牌是什么？教科书会说，它是名称、标识与设计的组合。但从消费者的角度看，品牌的本质是信任的缩写：人们购买知名品牌，很大程度上是在购买一种确定性——确定品质的下限，确定售后有着落，确定出了问题有处可诉。这种信任的建立极其缓慢，往往需要数十年如一日的品质稳定；而它的崩塌却可能只在一夜之间。近年来，多个知名品牌因质量丑闻或不当言行而市值蒸发，便是明证。有趣的是，社交媒体既加速了信任的崩塌，也为小品牌提供了建立信任的新路径：透明的生产过程、真实的用户评价、创始人的公开回应，都在重构消费者与品牌的关系。品牌之争，归根结底是信任之争。赢得信任或许没有捷径，但失去它从来不需要理由。
lessons.english: What is a brand? A textbook would say it is a combination of name, logo and design. From the point of view of the consumer, however, the essence of a brand is the abbreviation of trust: when people buy a well-known brand, they are largely buying a form of certainty — certainty about the lower limit of quality, about after-sale service, and about somewhere to turn when problems arise. Such trust is built extremely slowly, usually demanding decades of stable quality; yet its collapse may take only one night. In recent years, several famous brands have seen their market value evaporate over quality scandals or improper conduct, which is proof enough. Interestingly, social media both accelerates the collapse of trust and offers small brands a new path to building it: transparent production, honest reviews from users, and open responses from founders are re-shaping the relation between consumers and brands. The contest of brands is, in the last analysis, a contest of trust. Winning it may have no shortcut, but losing it has never needed a reason.

lessons.chinese: 远程与混合办公，曾经是少数行业的特权，如今已成为劳动力市场的常态选项。支持者列举了它的种种好处：省去通勤的时间与费用、更灵活的日程安排、更广的人才招聘范围。反对者则担心协作的稀释、新人培养的困难，以及工作与生活边界的消失。来自企业的证据呈现出一幅复杂的图景：部分岗位的生产率确有提升，而另一些依赖即时沟通的工作则受损明显。折中的混合模式因此流行，但它对管理提出了更高要求——团队需要更清晰的书面沟通、更刻意的信息同步。弹性办公的真正问题，不是“在哪里工作”，而是“如何定义工作的边界”。当办公室搬进家中，拒绝无限加班的制度保障，就成了劳动者新的必修课。
lessons.english: Remote and hybrid work, once a privilege of a few industries, has become a normal option in the labour market. Supporters list its benefits: the time and cost of commuting saved, schedules made more flexible, and the range of recruiting widened. Opponents worry about diluted cooperation, the difficulty of training newcomers, and the disappearance of the boundary between work and life. Evidence from companies paints a complicated picture: productivity in some posts has indeed risen, while work that depends on instant communication has suffered visibly. The compromise of hybrid modes has therefore become popular, but it demands more of management — teams need clearer written communication and more deliberate sharing of information. The real question of flexible work is not "where to work" but "how to define the boundary of work". When the office moves into the home, institutional protection against unlimited overtime becomes a new compulsory course for workers.

lessons.chinese: 一则成功的广告，很少是在“介绍产品”；它更常在出售一种情绪、一个身份或一段想象。广告心理学的核心发现是：人的购买决定，往往先由情感做出，再由理性补写理由。这就是为什么广告偏爱故事而非参数，偏爱画面而非说明。现代研究进一步揭示了其中的机制：重复曝光让人产生熟悉感，而熟悉感会被误读为可信；稀缺的暗示则触发损失厌恶，使人们为“怕错过”而掏钱。数字时代的广告把这些手法推向精准，算法可以根据浏览记录推测情绪状态，并在恰当的时刻投放恰当的信息。对此，监管的回应是划出红线，例如禁止向未成年人进行定向推送。对普通消费者而言，认识这些机制，就是给自己的判断力加上一层缓冲。
lessons.english: A successful advertisement seldom "introduces a product"; it more often sells a mood, an identity or an imagination. The central finding of advertising psychology is that the decision to buy is usually made first by emotion, and then justified by reason. This is why advertisements prefer stories to specifications, and pictures to explanations. Modern research has revealed the mechanism further: repeated exposure produces a sense of familiarity, which is then misread as trustworthiness; hints of scarcity trigger the aversion to loss, and people pay for the fear of missing out. Advertising in the digital age has pushed these methods towards precision — algorithms may infer the state of a person's mood from browsing records, and deliver the right message at the right moment. The response of regulators has been to draw red lines, such as banning targeted advertising aimed at minors. For ordinary consumers, knowing these mechanisms is adding a buffer to one's own judgement.

lessons.chinese: 通勤是大多数人一天的开始与结束，却很少被当作经济问题来计算。研究给出了惊人的数字：通勤时间的边际痛苦远高于工作与家务，长时间的通勤与幸福感下降、健康恶化显著相关。按小时折算，漫长通勤的隐性成本可能超过工资差距，这正是“为低薪而远距离奔波”不划算的原因。城市层面的账本同样庞大：道路拥堵吞噬生产力，尾气排放增加医疗支出。对策因此集中在两点：缩短距离与优化时间。前者涉及职住平衡的规划与远程办公的推广；后者则包括更准时的公交、可用于工作的通勤方式，例如安静、有座位的市郊铁路。当一座城市开始认真核算通勤的成本，它的交通政策才算真正面向了人。
lessons.english: Commuting opens and closes the day of most people, yet it is rarely counted as an economic question. Research has produced striking figures: the marginal pain of commuting time is far higher than that of work or housework, and long commutes are significantly related to lower happiness and worse health. Converted by the hour, the hidden cost of a long commute may exceed the difference in wages — which is exactly why rushing across the city for a slightly higher salary often does not pay. The account at the level of the city is equally large: congestion devours productivity, and emissions raise medical spending. Responses therefore concentrate on two points: shortening the distance and improving the use of time. The former involves planning for a balance of jobs and housing and the spread of remote work; the latter includes punctual buses and forms of commuting that allow work — a quiet suburban train with seats, for example. Only when a city begins to count the cost of commuting seriously does its transport policy truly face the people.

lessons.chinese: 现代消费社会中，个体消费者面对的常常是高度组织化的企业：专业的法务、庞大的数据与成熟的营销。力量的不对等，使消费者权益保护成为必需的制度安排。知情权、选择权、公平交易权与求偿权，是公认的基本框架。近年来，权利的边界随技术而扩展：个人信息被列为新型权益，自动续费须经二次确认，大数据“杀熟”被明令禁止。制度之外，市场自身也在生成保护机制，例如评价体系与第三方检测。但制度的有效性取决于执行，执行的力度又取决于投诉的成本。一些国家和地区推行小额纠纷的便捷处理程序，正是为了降低普通人维权的门槛。当维权变得容易，企业自律才会变成理性选择。保护消费者，最终保护的是市场本身。
lessons.english: In the modern consumer society, the individual buyer usually faces a highly organised enterprise: professional lawyers, enormous data and mature marketing. This imbalance of power makes the protection of consumer rights a necessary arrangement of institutions. The rights to know, to choose, to fair trade and to seek compensation form the recognised basic framework. In recent years, the boundary of rights has expanded with technology: personal information has been listed as a new form of right, automatic renewal requires a second confirmation, and charging loyal customers higher prices by big data has been explicitly banned. Outside institutions, the market itself is generating mechanisms of protection, such as systems of reviews and third-party testing. The effectiveness of institutions, however, depends on enforcement, and enforcement depends on the cost of complaint. Some countries and regions have introduced convenient procedures for small disputes, precisely to lower the threshold for ordinary people. When defending rights becomes easy, self-discipline of enterprises turns into a rational choice. To protect consumers is, in the end, to protect the market itself.

lessons.chinese: 经济学常被误解为一门关于钱的学问，它的真正内核其实是一种思维方式：任何选择都有成本，而成本是你为此放弃的最优选项。理解这一点，许多日常决策便会清晰起来。例如，是否读研不该只比较学费，还应计入放弃的两年收入与工作经验；是否排队抢购，则应计入时间的机会成本。经济学的第二个工具是边际思维：决定是否继续的，不是已经投入多少，而是再多投入一点能带来多少。这也解释了为何“来都来了”是一种常见的逻辑陷阱。第三个工具是对激励的敏感：制度改变激励，激励改变行为。当看到一项新政策时，与其争论好坏，不如先问：它会改变谁的什么行为？学会这三件工具，未必让人致富，却能让人少交一些“糊涂税”。
lessons.english: Economics is often mistaken for a study of money, but its real core is a way of thinking: every choice has a cost, and the cost is the best alternative you give up. With this understood, many daily decisions become clearer. Whether to pursue a postgraduate degree, for example, should not be compared by tuition alone; the two years of income and experience given up must also be counted. Whether to queue for a bargain should include the opportunity cost of time. A second tool of economics is marginal thinking: what decides whether to continue is not how much has already been invested, but how much an extra unit of investment will bring. This also explains why "since I am here anyway" is a common logical trap. A third tool is sensitivity to incentives: institutions change incentives, and incentives change behaviour. When facing a new policy, it is better to ask first whose behaviour it will change, and how, than to argue whether it is good. These three tools may not make anyone rich, but they save people from paying some very foolish taxes.

lessons.chinese: 连锁品牌扩张的浪潮中，街角小店的生存常被预言为时日无多。但多年过去，小店的韧性超出了预期。研究给出了几点解释。小店提供的是“关系”这种稀缺商品：店主记得你的口味，可以赊账，会在你加班晚归时多留一份热食。小店也是社区的毛细血管， 它们分散在街巷深处，提供着大商场无法覆盖的便利。此外，小店往往是低技能劳动者的创业阶梯，门槛虽低，却承载着家庭的希望。政策层面，许多城市开始为小店保留租金稳定的街铺，并简化证照办理。当然，小店自身的转型同样重要：接入外卖平台、支持线上下单、开发特色商品，都延长了它们的生命线。一个只有连锁品牌的城市是乏味的，一家有人情味的小店则是城市留给居民的温柔。
lessons.english: In the wave of expanding chain brands, the survival of corner shops was often predicted to be numbered. Yet years later, the resilience of small shops has exceeded expectations. Research offers several explanations. What a small shop provides is "relation", a scarce commodity: the owner remembers your taste, allows a bill to be paid later, and keeps a hot meal for you when you come back late from overtime. Small shops are also the capillaries of a community, scattered deep in the streets, providing conveniences that large shopping malls cannot cover. Moreover, small shops are often the ladder of enterprise for workers with few skills: the threshold is low, but they carry the hope of a family. At the level of policy, many cities have begun to reserve stable-rent street premises for small shops and to simplify licences. The transformation of the shops themselves matters as well: joining delivery platforms, supporting online orders, and developing special products have all extended their lifeline. A city with nothing but chain brands is dull; a small shop with human warmth is the tenderness a city leaves to its residents.

lessons.chinese: 价格与价值是经济学中最古老的一对概念，也是日常生活中最常见的错位。价格由供需决定，随行就市，波动不停；价值则关乎物品对人的实际用处，相对稳定。两者通常同向而行，但在特定情境下会剧烈背离。演唱会门票被黄牛炒到十倍，是价格背离价值的典型；而空气免费却维系生命，则是价值远超价格的极端。理解这种背离，有助于做出更清醒的决策。免费的东西可能代价高昂，昂贵的东西也可能一文不值；判断的依据不应是标价，而应是它对自己生活的真实贡献。经济学家提醒我们，价格是信号而非裁判：它告诉我们稀缺的程度，却不该定义事物的意义。学会区分两者，是消费时代的一门必修课。
lessons.english: Price and value are the oldest pair of concepts in economics, and also the most common mismatch in daily life. Price is decided by supply and demand, moves with the market, and never stops changing; value concerns the real use of a thing to a person, and is relatively stable. The two usually move in the same direction, but in certain situations they diverge sharply. A concert ticket driven to ten times its face value by resellers is a typical case of price departing from value; while air, free of charge but essential to life, is the extreme of value far beyond price. Understanding such divergence helps people decide more soberly. Free things may cost dearly, and expensive things may be worth nothing; the basis of judgement should not be the label, but the real contribution of a thing to one's own life. Economists remind us that price is a signal, not a judge: it tells us the degree of scarcity, but it should not define the meaning of things. Learning to separate the two is a compulsory course in the age of consumption.

lessons.chinese: 人是理性的吗？行为经济学的答案是否定的：人们的决定常受情境的细微影响。这为公共政策提供了一种温和的工具——“助推”。它不禁止任何选项，也不施加惩罚，只是改变选项的呈现方式。经典的例子是食堂的排列：把水果放在视线平齐的位置，把甜点移到角落，健康饮食的比例便明显上升。器官捐献采用“默认同意”的国家，捐献率也远高于需要主动登记的国家。助推的低成本与高有效性，使它在各国公共治理中迅速流行。但它的边界同样引发讨论：当政府开始设计选择环境，如何保证这种设计服务于公众而非操纵公众？多数研究者同意两条底线：助推必须透明，且必须让人们能够轻易退出。温和的推手，也应该接受被推者的检验。
lessons.english: Is the human being rational? The answer of behavioural economics is no: decisions are often swayed by small features of the situation. This offers public policy a gentle tool — the "nudge". It forbids no option and imposes no punishment; it only changes the way options are presented. The classic example is the arrangement of a canteen: when fruit is placed at eye level and desserts moved to a corner, the share of healthy eating rises markedly. Countries where organ donation is the default also show far higher rates of donation than countries that require active registration. The low cost and high effectiveness of nudges have made them popular in public governance around the world. Yet their boundary is equally debated: when a government begins to design the environment of choice, how can such design be guaranteed to serve the public rather than manipulate it? Most researchers agree on two bottom lines: a nudge must be transparent, and people must be able to step out of it easily. The gentle pusher should also accept the test of those who are pushed.

lessons.chinese: 治理的最后一百米，往往在社区。与政府部门的科层体系不同，社区治理面对的是具体的楼栋、具体的人与具体的矛盾：楼道堆物、停车纠纷、遛狗不牵绳。有效的社区治理很少依赖自上而下的命令，更多依靠精细的协商机制。一些社区的做法值得记录：由退休教师、律师和热心居民组成议事会，把矛盾摆到桌面上；设立“居民提案”通道，让楼道灯的修理与绿地改造由投票决定；把物业费的使用明细逐月公示。这些做法的共同点，是把“要我做”变成“我们要做”。研究基层治理的学者发现，成功的社区几乎都有一个特征：居民之间存在着多条日常互动的纽带。治理不是管理者的独角戏，而是一个社区重新学会彼此相处的过程。
lessons.english: The last hundred metres of governance usually lie in the community. Unlike the hierarchical system of government departments, community governance faces specific buildings, specific people and specific conflicts: objects piled in corridors, disputes over parking, dogs walked without leads. Effective community governance rarely relies on top-down orders; it depends more on fine mechanisms of negotiation. The practice of some communities is worth recording: a council formed by retired teachers, lawyers and devoted residents puts conflicts on the table; a channel of "residents' proposals" lets the repair of corridor lights and the rebuilding of a lawn be decided by vote; the itemised use of property fees is published every month. The common point of these practices is turning "they make me do it" into "we choose to do it". Scholars of grassroots governance have found that successful communities share one feature: many threads of daily interaction exist among the residents. Governance is not a solo performance of managers, but a process in which a community learns again how to live with itself.

lessons.chinese: 每一座老城都面临同一道难题：既留住历史的肌理，又满足现代生活的需求。推倒重建曾经是标准答案，其代价是城市记忆的成片消失。如今的共识逐渐转向“更新”：不改变街道的格局，而是在旧建筑中注入新功能。具体的做法多种多样。厂房被改造为美术馆与设计工作室，老住宅加装了电梯与适老设施，废弃的铁路线变成了市民步道。更新的资金也走向多元，政府、企业与居民共同分担。研究表明，成功的更新有一个共同前提：原住民不被大规模驱离。街市的烟火、邻里网络的密度，恰恰是老城最珍贵的资产。城市学家提醒我们，城市是活着的有机体，更新不是一次手术，而是一场持续的照料。老城更新的目标，不是让它看起来崭新，而是让它继续有生命力。
lessons.english: Every old city faces the same hard question: how to keep the texture of history while meeting the needs of modern life. Demolition and rebuilding were once the standard answer, and their price was the loss of urban memory by whole districts. The consensus has gradually turned to "renewal": the pattern of streets is kept, while new functions are poured into old buildings. The practices vary. Factories become museums and design studios; old residences are fitted with lifts and facilities for the aged; an abandoned railway line turns into a promenade for citizens. The funding of renewal has also diversified, shared by government, enterprises and residents. Studies show that successful renewal has one common premise: the original residents are not driven away on a large scale. The liveliness of street markets and the density of neighbourhood networks are precisely the most precious assets of an old city. Urbanists remind us that a city is a living organism; renewal is not one operation but a continuing act of care. The goal of renewal is not to make the old city look new, but to keep it alive.

lessons.chinese: 当一个社会的老年人口比例持续攀升，照护就不再只是家庭内部的事务，而成为一项系统工程。日本与北欧的探索提供了参照：长期护理保险分担家庭的经济压力，日间照料中心让老人不必整日独居，专业照护者成为受尊重的职业。中国的实践也在快速展开：社区嵌入式养老让老人离家不远就能获得照护，“时间银行”鼓励低龄老人服务高龄老人并把时长储蓄下来。挑战依然清晰：照护人手的缺口巨大，职业的薪酬与社会认同有待提升；失能失智老人的专业照护更是一片蓝海与难点。研究提示了一个容易被忽视的事实：绝大多数照护时间，仍然由家庭成员无偿承担。因此，支持家庭照护者——提供喘息服务、技能培训与心理支持——应当成为政策的优先项。
lessons.english: When the share of elderly people in a society keeps climbing, care is no longer an affair inside the family; it becomes a systematic project. The explorations of Japan and the Nordic countries offer references: long-term care insurance shares the economic pressure of families, day-care centres spare the old from spending whole days alone, and professional care work has become a respected occupation. Practice in China is unfolding quickly: community-based care allows the elderly to receive help not far from home, and a "time bank" encourages younger seniors to serve the older ones, banking the hours for their own future. The challenges are clear: the gap of care workers is huge, and the pay and social recognition of the profession need to rise; the professional care of the disabled and cognitively impaired is both a blue sea and a hard rock. Research points to a fact easily overlooked: the greater part of care hours is still borne unpaid by family members. Supporting family carers — with respite services, skill training and psychological support — should therefore be a priority of policy.

lessons.chinese: 医患关系的研究中，有一个反复被验证的发现：沟通的质量，与治疗的依从性和效果显著相关。患者希望被倾听、被解释、被当作完整的人，而非一纸化验单。然而现实的诊室里，医生平均只有几分钟处理一位患者，完整的叙事常常被打断。改善的尝试正在多层面展开。医学院把医患沟通列为必修课程，训练学生如何告知坏消息、如何回应愤怒与恐惧；医院推行“共同决策”，让患者参与治疗方案的选择；电子病历系统则试图把医生的目光从屏幕还给患者。研究还发现了一个朴素的变量：坐下来的医生，比站着的医生获得更多信任。医学的进步延长了生命的长度，而诊室里的对话，决定着这段延长的生命有多少温度。
lessons.english: In studies of the relation between doctors and patients, one finding has been verified again and again: the quality of communication is significantly related to how well patients follow treatment and how well the treatment works. Patients wish to be heard, to be given explanations, and to be treated as whole persons rather than as a sheet of laboratory results. In real consulting rooms, however, a doctor has only a few minutes for one patient, and the complete story is often interrupted. Attempts at improvement are unfolding on several levels. Medical schools have made communication a required course, training students to deliver bad news and to respond to anger and fear; hospitals practise "shared decision-making", letting patients join in the choice of treatment; and electronic record systems are trying to return the doctor's eyes from the screen to the patient. Research has also found a plain variable: a doctor who sits down wins more trust than one who stands. The progress of medicine has lengthened life; the conversation in the consulting room decides how much warmth that longer life contains.

lessons.chinese: 教育公平常被简化为“分数面前人人平等”，但真正的公平远比这复杂。起点的差异在入学之前就已形成：家庭的藏书、假期的旅行、父母的视野，都在悄悄塑造孩子的认知底色。研究表明，寒暑假期间不同家庭背景学生之间的成绩差距会明显扩大，这一现象被称为“暑期滑坡”。因此，公平的路径需要超出考场的努力：把优质资源送往薄弱学校的教师轮岗，为低收入家庭提供早期养育支持的入户项目，以及向所有孩子开放的图书馆、博物馆与体育设施。技术的普及带来新的可能，在线课程让名师课堂跨越了地理的边界，但设备与引导的差距又构成新的鸿沟。教育公平不是消灭差异，而是确保差异不成为命运的判决。
lessons.english: Educational equity is often simplified into "equal scores before the examination", but true equity is far more complex. Differences at the starting line are formed before enrolment: the books at home, the holidays a family can afford, and the breadth of the parents' world all quietly shape the cognitive base of a child. Studies show that during summer holidays the gap in achievement between students of different family backgrounds widens visibly — a phenomenon known as "summer slide". The road to equity therefore needs efforts beyond the examination hall: rotation of good teachers towards weaker schools, home-visit programmes of early parenting support for low-income families, and libraries, museums and sports facilities open to all children. The spread of technology brings new possibility — online courses carry the classrooms of excellent teachers across geography — yet the gap in devices and guidance forms a new divide. Educational equity does not mean erasing differences; it means making sure that differences do not become the verdict of fate.

lessons.chinese: 新闻曾以“天”为单位更新，如今以“分”为单位滚动。速度的红利显而易见：世界的变化即时呈现，信息的门槛前所未有地降低。但速度也带来了保质期的问题：一条新闻的热度往往不超过四十八小时，复杂议题的讨论常被新的热点冲散。更深的问题在于核实的过程被压缩。传统编辑部里，事实核查是新闻发表的必要环节；而在人人可发的时代，转发常快于求证，错误与谣言便获得了与事实相同的传播速度。一些媒体的应对是重建“慢新闻”栏目，用更长的篇幅解释来龙去脉；核查机构则专门追踪流传最广的错误信息。对读者而言，一个简单的习惯尤为重要：在转发之前，先等一等，看一看消息的源头。新闻可以有保质期，但事实没有。
lessons.english: News was once updated by the day; now it rolls by the minute. The benefit of speed is clear: the changes of the world appear at once, and the threshold of information has never been lower. But speed has also brought the problem of shelf life: the heat of a story seldom lasts beyond forty-eight hours, and the discussion of complex issues is often scattered by the next trending topic. The deeper problem is that the process of verification has been squeezed. In the traditional newsroom, fact-checking was a necessary step before publication; in the age when everyone can publish, forwarding often runs faster than checking, and errors and rumours gain the same speed as facts. The response of some media is to rebuild columns of "slow news", explaining the whole story in longer texts, while fact-checking bodies specialise in tracking the most widely spread falsehoods. For readers, one simple habit matters most: before forwarding, wait a moment and look at the source of the message. News may have a shelf life, but facts do not.

lessons.chinese: 信任很少出现在经济报表里，它的成本与收益却无处不在。研究显示，一个社会中人际信任水平越高，交易成本越低：合同可以更简单，监督可以更省略，合作可以更快达成。共享经济本质上就是一场信任的大规模实验——把家门钥匙交给陌生人，把车停进陌生人的院子。支持这一实验的基础设施，是评价系统与信用记录。但信任的账本同样记录损失：一次广泛传播的欺诈事件，可能让整个行业付出多年的代价。恢复信任远比建立信任昂贵，这是社会心理学反复验证的结论。因此，值得投资的不仅是防伪的技术，更是守信的回报：让诚实的人被看见、被优先选择。当守信成为一种有利可图的策略，信任才会从稀缺品变成公共财富。
lessons.english: Trust seldom appears in the financial reports, yet its costs and returns are everywhere. Research shows that in a society with a higher level of interpersonal trust, the cost of transaction is lower: contracts can be simpler, supervision can be spared, and cooperation can be reached faster. The sharing economy is in essence a large-scale experiment of trust — handing the key of one's home to a stranger, parking one's car in a stranger's yard. The infrastructure supporting this experiment is the system of reviews and credit records. But the ledger of trust also records losses: one widely spread case of fraud may cost a whole industry many years. Restoring trust is far more expensive than building it — a conclusion verified repeatedly by social psychology. What deserves investment, therefore, is not only technology against fraud, but also the return of good faith: letting honest people be seen and preferred. When keeping one's word becomes a profitable strategy, trust will turn from a scarce good into a public wealth.

lessons.title_cn: 政务大厅搬进手机之后
lessons.title_en: After the Government Hall Moved into the Phone
lessons.chinese: 过去，办一份证明可能要跑三个部门、盖五枚公章；如今，许多政务事项已经可以全程在线办理。数字政务的推广，压缩的是时间与路途，改变的是政府与公民的相处方式。数据在部门之间流转，公民不再需要重复提交材料；“一网通办”的背后，是流程的再造与责任的重新划分。便利之外，数字政务还带来了一种更深层的变化：可追溯性。每一个审批环节都有记录，自由裁量的空间被压缩，权力运行更加透明。当然，转型也有其盲区：不会使用智能手机的老年人、缺乏网络覆盖的偏远地区，都可能被数字化的车轮落下。因此，保留线下窗口与人工服务，不是效率的倒退，而是公共服务的底线伦理。技术应当扩大服务的半径，而不是重新划定谁能被服务的边界。
lessons.english: There was a time when obtaining a certificate meant visiting three departments and collecting five stamps; nowadays, many government services can be completed entirely online. The spread of digital government has compressed time and travel, and has changed the way the state and its citizens meet. As data flow between departments, citizens no longer need to submit the same papers again and again; behind "one website for all" lies the re-engineering of processes and the re-division of responsibility. Beyond convenience, digital government has brought a deeper change: traceability. Every step of approval leaves a record, the space of discretion is compressed, and the running of power becomes more transparent. The transformation has its blind spots, of course: elderly people who cannot use smartphones, and remote areas without network coverage, may be left behind by the wheels of digitalisation. Keeping offline windows and human service is therefore not a retreat from efficiency, but the bottom-line ethics of public service. Technology should widen the radius of service, not redraw the border of who can be served.

lessons.chinese: 洪水、热浪、地震——极端事件的频率正在上升，城市被迫思考同一个问题：当灾难来临时，我们准备好了吗？城市韧性的概念由此进入规划者的词汇表。它指的不是坚不可摧，而是受挫后快速恢复的能力。韧性的建设分布在城市的每一处细节：排水系统能否应对百年一遇的暴雨，电网在台风中能否快速分区恢复，医院的应急供电能支撑多久，社区是否有训练有素的志愿网络。研究韧性的学者强调“冗余”的价值：看似浪费的备用发电机组与多余的水源，正是灾难中的生命线。韧性的另一个维度是社会性的：邻里之间的熟悉程度，决定了危机中互助的速度。一座有韧性的城市，不仅在工程上达标，更在人与人之间建立了看不见的连接。
lessons.english: Floods, heatwaves, earthquakes — the frequency of extreme events is rising, and cities are forced to consider the same question: when disaster comes, are we ready? The concept of urban resilience has thus entered the vocabulary of planners. It does not mean being indestructible, but the ability to recover quickly after being struck. The building of resilience is distributed in every detail of a city: whether the drainage can cope with a storm that comes once in a century, whether the power grid can restore districts quickly in a typhoon, how long the emergency power of hospitals can last, and whether communities have a trained network of volunteers. Scholars of resilience stress the value of "redundancy": the apparently wasteful backup generators and extra sources of water are the lifelines in a disaster. Another dimension of resilience is social: the degree to which neighbours know one another decides the speed of mutual help in a crisis. A resilient city is one that not only meets the standards of engineering, but has also built the invisible connections between its people.

lessons.chinese: 每天早晨，推荐算法已经在替你完成上百次选择：该看哪条新闻、听哪首歌、关注哪个话题。选择本应是自由的表现，如今却常被外包给系统。算法推荐的价值不可否认：它在信息的海洋里为用户打捞相关内容，也帮助小众创作者找到知音。但研究者提醒我们注意它的工作原理——算法优化的是停留时长，而不是用户的真实福祉。让人生气的内容往往让人停留更久，于是被推送得更多；这便是情绪被算法放大的回路。更深的担忧在于“过滤气泡”：人们越来越少接触到与己不同的观点。一些平台开始提供关闭个性化推荐的选项，欧盟的立法也要求算法保持透明。把选择权收回手中，需要的不是拒绝技术，而是知道何时应当自己按下“换一换”。
lessons.english: Every morning, recommendation algorithms have already made hundreds of choices for you: which news to read, which song to play, which topic to follow. Choice ought to be the sign of freedom, yet it is often outsourced to systems. The value of recommendation is undeniable: it fishes relevant content out of the ocean of information for users, and helps niche creators find their audience. But researchers remind us of its working principle — what the algorithm optimises is the length of stay, not the real wellbeing of the user. Content that makes people angry often keeps them longer, and is therefore pushed more; this is the loop in which emotion is amplified by algorithms. The deeper worry is the "filter bubble": people are exposed less and less to views unlike their own. Some platforms now offer the option of turning off personalised recommendation, and legislation in the European Union demands that algorithms remain transparent. Taking the right of choice back into one's own hands requires not the refusal of technology, but the knowledge of when to press "refresh" oneself.

lessons.chinese: 手腕上的设备记录着步数、心率与睡眠，我们正进入一个自我量化的时代。量化的好处显而易见：数据让模糊的感受变得具体，锻炼的效果、睡眠的质量都有了刻度。对慢性病患者而言，连续的监测甚至可能挽救生命。然而，量化也改变着人与自身的关系。当睡眠被评分，许多人开始为“睡眠成绩”焦虑，反而更难入睡，研究者称之为“完美睡眠主义”。数字还可能取代体验：跑步的快乐被配速的焦虑覆盖，散步被步数目标绑架。有学者提出，自我量化应当服务于健康，而非定义健康。他们的建议是：定期摘下设备，用不带刻度的几天提醒自己，身体的感觉先于任何数据。被量化的自我仍需留出一部分，交给无法被测量的生活。
lessons.english: The device on the wrist records steps, heart rate and sleep; we are entering an age in which the self is quantified. The benefits of quantifying are plain: data turn vague feelings into specifics, and both the effect of exercise and the quality of sleep acquire a scale. For patients with chronic diseases, continuous monitoring may even save lives. Quantifying, however, is also changing the relation between people and themselves. When sleep is scored, many begin to worry about their "sleep grade", which makes falling asleep harder — a condition researchers call "orthosomnia", the pursuit of perfect sleep. Numbers may also replace experience: the joy of running is covered by the anxiety of pace, and a walk is hijacked by the step target. Some scholars suggest that self-quantifying should serve health, not define it. Their advice is to take the device off regularly, and spend a few days without scales, reminding oneself that the feeling of the body comes before any data. The quantified self still needs to leave a part of life to what cannot be measured.

lessons.chinese: 网约车进入中国城市已超过十年，它带来的变化远不止打车方式的更新。出行效率的提升是公认的：算法匹配取代了路边扬招，等车时间大幅缩短，偏僻路段叫车难的问题也得到缓解。就业层面，平台吸纳了数百万灵活就业者，其中许多人曾是工厂工人或失业人员。但这场变革的争议从未停歇。传统出租车行业经历了剧烈的阵痛；司机的收入与劳动强度成为公共议题；安全问题也促使平台加装录音录像、推行行程分享。回顾这十年，网约车更像是一面镜子，映照出技术与规则相互追赶的过程：每一次技术创新，都迫使监管回答新的问题。未来的出行图景中，网约车将只是一环，自动驾驶的加入还会提出更多问题。监管与创新的赛跑，不会有终点。
lessons.english: Ride-hailing has been in Chinese cities for more than a decade, and what it has changed goes far beyond the way taxis are taken. The improvement of efficiency is universally acknowledged: algorithmic matching has replaced waving by the roadside, waiting time has fallen sharply, and finding a car in remote streets is no longer a problem. On the side of employment, platforms have absorbed millions of flexible workers, many of whom were once factory workers or jobless. The controversy of this change, however, has never stopped. The traditional taxi trade suffered sharp pain; the income and labour intensity of drivers became public issues; and accidents of safety pushed platforms to install audio and video recording and to introduce journey sharing. Looking back at the decade, ride-hailing is more like a mirror, reflecting the process of technology and rules chasing each other: every technical innovation forces regulation to answer new questions. In the picture of future travel, ride-hailing will be only one link, and the joining of autonomous driving will raise more questions. The race between regulation and innovation will have no finishing line.

lessons.chinese: 会使用智能手机，不等于拥有数字素养。数字素养的内涵远超操作技能：它包括辨别信息真伪的能力、理解算法如何呈现内容的意识，以及对个人数据的珍视。研究显示，数字技能的分布并不均衡，年龄、教育与收入都在其中起着作用；即便是年轻的“数字原住民”，也可能在信息甄别上表现薄弱。数字素养的教育因此应当覆盖全生命周期：学校开设媒介素养课程，帮助学生在转发之前先求证；图书馆和社区为老年人提供耐心的培训；企业则被要求用清晰的语言告知数据用途。有学者把数字素养称为“数字时代的新识字”：一百多年前，不识字的人难以参与社会；今天，缺乏数字素养的人同样会被边缘化。让技术普及的红利不被素养的鸿沟吞噬，是教育的新使命。
lessons.english: Being able to use a smartphone does not equal digital literacy. The meaning of digital literacy goes far beyond skills of operation: it includes the ability to tell true information from false, the awareness of how algorithms present content, and the care for one's own data. Research shows that digital skills are unevenly spread — age, education and income all play their part — and even the young "digital natives" may be weak in telling information apart. The education of digital literacy should therefore cover the whole of life: schools open courses of media literacy to teach students to check before forwarding; libraries and communities offer patient training for the elderly; and enterprises are required to state the use of data in plain language. Some scholars call digital literacy "the new reading and writing of the digital age": more than a century ago, those who could not read could hardly join society; today, those who lack digital literacy are equally marginalised. Letting the benefit of technology not be swallowed by the gap of literacy is a new mission of education.

lessons.chinese: 环境监测正在经历一场技术革命。卫星在数百公里高空扫描海面的浮游藻类，传感器网络沉入河流持续记录水质，声学设备在雨林深处辨别物种的声音。监测能力的跃升，正在改变环境治理的方式：污染不再依赖举报才发现，数据可以实时定位排放源；承诺是否兑现，也有了客观的标尺。例如，甲烷泄漏曾难以察觉，如今卫星可以捕捉到信号，企业再无法以“不知情”推脱。开源的数据平台还让公众参与成为可能，研究者与普通市民可以共同审视身边的环境质量。当然，技术不能替代制度，数据只有连接到执法与问责才会产生力量。当哨兵越来越多，剩下的问题是：我们是否愿意倾听它们带回的消息。
lessons.english: Environmental monitoring is passing through a technical revolution. Satellites scan the floating algae of the sea from hundreds of kilometres above; networks of sensors sink into rivers and record the quality of water continuously; acoustic devices tell the species of a rainforest by their voices. The leap of monitoring is changing the way the environment is governed: pollution is no longer discovered by complaint alone, for data can locate the source of discharge in real time, and whether promises are kept now has an objective measure. Methane leaks, once hard to notice, can be caught by satellites, and enterprises can no longer hide behind the claim of ignorance. Open data platforms have made public participation possible: researchers and ordinary citizens can examine together the quality of the environment around them. Technology, of course, cannot replace institutions — data gain force only when connected to enforcement and accountability. As the sentinels grow in number, the remaining question is whether we are willing to hear the messages they bring back.

lessons.chinese: 一件网购商品的旅程，从工厂仓库开始，经过干线运输、分拣中心与末端站点，最终抵达家门口的快递柜。这条链条的高效令人惊叹，其环境成本同样惊人。统计显示，中国快递业务量每年超过一千亿件，由此产生的包装废弃物数量庞大。循环经济的理念因此被引入物流行业：可折叠的循环箱替代一次性纸箱，电子面单取代纸质单据，充电循环袋在网点之间流转。一些平台还推出“回箱计划”，把快递柜变成回收点。这些措施的推广仍面临障碍：循环箱的成本高于纸箱，回收需要用户配合，行业标准也不统一。研究显示，包装减量的空间依然可观，过度包装的案例比比皆是。每一件包裹的旅行都可以更轻盈，前提是链条上的各方都愿意为绿色多付一点成本。
lessons.english: The journey of a parcel bought online begins in the warehouse of a factory, passes through trunk transport, sorting centres and terminal stations, and ends at the locker by one's door. The efficiency of this chain is astonishing; so is its cost to the environment. Statistics show that the volume of parcels in China exceeds one hundred billion every year, and the waste of packaging is enormous. The idea of the circular economy has therefore been introduced into logistics: foldable and reusable boxes replace one-off cartons, electronic labels replace paper ones, and rechargeable bags circulate between stations. Some platforms have also started "box return" programmes, turning lockers into collection points. The spread of these measures still meets obstacles: reusable boxes cost more than cartons, recycling needs the cooperation of users, and industry standards remain ununified. Research shows that the room for reducing packaging is considerable, and cases of excessive packaging can be found everywhere. The journey of every parcel could be lighter — provided that all sides of the chain are willing to pay a little more for greenness.

lessons.chinese: 自动驾驶常被描述为“即将到来的现实”，但行业的进展揭示了一个更复杂的图景：在受限场景中，技术已经可用；在开放道路的全域自动驾驶，仍需时日。港口内的无人集卡、矿区的高速作业、固定线路的无人公交，都是技术落地的成功案例，因为这些场景的变量可控。城市道路则是另一回事：暴雨中的视线、突然横穿的行人、人类驾驶的不可预测，都远超当前算法的处理边界。行业由此分化出两条路线：渐进派主张辅助驾驶先行，用数据积累换取技术成熟；跨越派则押注完全无人驾驶的突破。伦理问题同样无法回避：事故的责任如何在车主、制造商与算法设计者之间划分？自动驾驶的黎明必将到来，但黎明前的这段路，需要技术、法规与公众信任的同步成熟。
lessons.english: Autonomous driving is often described as a reality "just around the corner", but the progress of the industry reveals a more complicated picture: in limited scenes the technology is already usable; full autonomy on open roads still needs time. Driverless container trucks inside ports, high-speed operation in mining areas and driverless buses on fixed lines are all successful cases of landing, because the variables of these scenes are controllable. City roads are another matter: the sight in heavy rain, pedestrians crossing suddenly, and the unpredictability of human drivers all go beyond the processing limits of present algorithms. The industry has therefore divided into two routes. The gradualist camp argues for assisted driving first, exchanging data for maturity; the leap camp stakes everything on the breakthrough of full autonomy. The ethical question cannot be avoided either: how shall the responsibility for an accident be divided among the owner, the manufacturer and the designers of the algorithm? The dawn of autonomous driving will surely come, but the road before dawn demands the synchronous maturity of technology, regulation and public trust.

lessons.chinese: 政府的抽屉里存放着海量的数据：公交卡刷卡记录、空气质量读数、企业注册信息、医院就诊统计。这些数据在完成行政使命之后，是否还有第二生命？数据开放的实践给出了肯定回答。交通部门的到离站数据被开发者做成出行应用；气象与环境数据成为农业保险定价的依据；研究者利用公开数据发表了大量论文，评估政策、发现规律。数据开放的价值不仅在应用，更在监督：预算、招投标与行政处罚数据的公开，让公共资源的使用经得起检视。当然，开放也有边界，个人隐私与国家安全的红线必须清晰。经验表明，“以开放为默认、以不开放为例外”的原则最能释放数据的价值。打开数据的抽屉，就是邀请整个社会与政府一起思考。
lessons.english: The drawers of the government hold enormous data: records of public transport cards, readings of air quality, registrations of enterprises, statistics of hospital visits. After finishing their administrative missions, do these data have a second life? The practice of open data answers yes. Arrival and departure data of transport have been made into travel applications by developers; weather and environment data serve as the basis of pricing agricultural insurance; researchers, using open data, have published large numbers of papers, evaluating policies and finding patterns. The value of open data lies not only in application but in supervision: the opening of budgets, bidding and administrative penalties allows the use of public money to bear examination. Openness has its boundary, of course — the red lines of personal privacy and national security must be clear. Experience shows that the principle of "open by default, closed by exception" releases the value of data best. To open the drawers of data is to invite the whole society to think together with the government.

lessons.chinese: 科技的默认用户常常是年轻人：字体偏小、操作层级繁多、更新频繁。当老年用户面对这样的产品，挫败感是设计使然，而非能力使然。科技适老的运动由此兴起，它的理念是把老年人的需求当作设计起点，而非事后补丁。好的适老设计有其原则：字体与按钮足够大，操作路径足够短，关键功能可以一键直达；重要提示用声音与震动双重传达；误操作的挽回机制清晰可见。更进一步的设计，则把技术织入生活而不露痕迹：跌倒监测默默运行，燃气报警自动联网，用药提醒与药盒联动。研究和实践都证明，老年人的学习能力被长期低估。当产品愿意俯下身来，暮年与数字世界之间，其实并没有想象中那么深的鸿沟。设计的选择，决定鸿沟的深度。
lessons.english: The default user of technology is usually young: fonts too small, layers of menus too many, updates too frequent. When elderly users face such products, the frustration comes from design, not from their ability. The movement of designing technology for the aged has thus arisen, on the principle that the needs of the elderly should be the starting point of design, not a patch added afterwards. Good design for the aged has its principles: fonts and buttons large enough, paths of operation short enough, key functions reachable by one touch; important notices delivered by both sound and vibration; and a clear way to undo wrong operations. Designs that go further weave technology into life without leaving traces — fall detection running quietly, gas alarms linked to the network automatically, and medicine reminders working together with the pill box. Research and practice both prove that the learning ability of the elderly has long been underestimated. When products are willing to bend down, the gulf between old age and the digital world is not as deep as imagined. The choice of design decides the depth of that gulf.

lessons.title_en: Smart Cities, and Who Gets Smarter
lessons.chinese: 智慧城市的图景令人向往：交通信号根据车流实时调整，垃圾桶满溢自动报警，路灯按人影明灭。世界各地的城市竞相投入巨资，传感器与数据中心成为新的市政标配。然而，一些昂贵的项目建成后却未能兑现承诺，原因值得深思。有的城市采购了顶尖的设备，却没有对应的治理流程，数据躺在服务器里无人问津；有的项目以技术为中心，而非以市民为中心，解决的其实是工程师的问题，而非居民的问题。成功的案例往往朴素得多：一个准确的公交到站预测，比华丽的指挥大屏更能改变生活。智慧城市的关键，不在于安装了多少传感器，而在于智慧由谁定义、为谁服务。当市民参与到定义需求的环节，技术才真正开始让城市聪明起来。
lessons.english: The picture of a smart city is attractive: traffic signals adjusted in real time by the flow of cars, waste bins calling for collection when full, street lamps dimming and brightening with the presence of people. Cities around the world have poured money into the race, and sensors with data centres have become the new standard fittings of a municipality. Yet some expensive projects, once built, have failed to keep their promises, and the reasons deserve thought. Some cities bought top equipment without building corresponding processes of governance, so the data lie untouched in servers; other projects were centred on technology rather than on citizens, solving the problems of engineers instead of the problems of residents. Successful cases are often much plainer: an accurate prediction of bus arrival changes life more than a splendid control room. The key of a smart city lies not in how many sensors are installed, but in who defines the smartness and for whom it works. When citizens join in defining the needs, technology truly begins to make a city smart.

lessons.chinese: 公众常常期待科学提供确定的答案，而科学家自己却对不确定性有着更深的敬意。一项精心设计的实验，给出的从来不是“真理”，而是在当前证据下最合理的解释，以及该解释的适用边界。这种不确定性不是科学的弱点，而是它的力量所在：正因为承认可能出错，科学才建立了纠错的机制。可重复实验、同行评议、公开数据，都是围绕不确定性设计的制度。核物理学家费曼曾说，科学是“相信专家也会无知”的文化。公众对科学的失望，多数发生在把科学理解为教条的时刻：当某个结论被修订，人们便指责“科学家自相矛盾”。事实恰恰相反——结论的修订正是科学运转正常的证据。理解不确定性，就是理解科学作为一种方法的谦卑与诚实。
lessons.english: The public often expects science to provide certain answers, while scientists themselves hold a deeper respect for uncertainty. A well-designed experiment never gives "truth"; it gives the most reasonable explanation under present evidence, together with the boundary of that explanation. This uncertainty is not the weakness of science but the very source of its strength: precisely because it admits the possibility of being wrong, science has built its mechanism of correction. Repeatable experiments, peer review and open data are all institutions designed around uncertainty. The physicist Richard Feynman once said that science is the culture of "doubting the experts". The disappointment of the public in science mostly happens at the moment when science is understood as dogma: when a conclusion is revised, people blame the scientists for contradicting themselves. The truth is quite the opposite — the revision of conclusions is the very evidence that science is working normally. To understand uncertainty is to understand the humility and honesty of science as a method.

lessons.chinese: 同行评议被视为学术出版的守门人：一篇论文能否发表，由同领域的专家匿名审定。这一制度的设计逻辑是显而易见的：最懂一项研究的人，最有资格评判它。然而，运行数百年的同行评议也暴露出人性的弱点。审稿人是无偿的志愿者，负担沉重；匿名制度偶被滥用，成为压制竞争者的工具；知名机构与知名学者的论文，往往获得更宽容的对待。近年来的改革尝试包括开放评议，让审稿意见与论文一同发表；发表后评议，把评判权交给更广泛的学术共同体；以及以研究本身的质量为中心的新的评价实验。没有任何制度是完美的，同行评议的价值不在于杜绝错误——错误时有发生——而在于它是目前已知的最不坏的过滤器。制度的演进，本质上是与人性弱点的一场持久谈判。
lessons.english: Peer review is regarded as the gatekeeper of academic publishing: whether a paper is published is judged anonymously by experts of the same field. The logic of the system is evident — those who understand a study best are the most qualified to judge it. Yet peer review, running for centuries, has also exposed the weakness of human nature. Reviewers are unpaid volunteers under heavy burdens; anonymity is occasionally abused as a tool to suppress competitors; and papers from famous institutions and famous scholars often receive more tolerant judgement. Recent reforms include open review, in which the comments of reviewers are published together with the paper; post-publication review, handing judgement to the wider academic community; and new experiments of evaluation centred on the quality of the research itself. No institution is perfect. The value of peer review does not lie in eliminating mistakes — mistakes happen all the time — but in being the least bad filter known so far. The evolution of the system is, in essence, a long negotiation with the weakness of human nature.

lessons.chinese: 1859年，《物种起源》出版，首印一千二百五十册当日售罄。达尔文在这部书中几乎没有使用“进化”一词，他用的是“带有变化的传衍”。这个措辞的谨慎反映了当时的处境：物种可变的观念，直接冲击着流行的信仰体系。批评接踵而至，最著名的一场论战发生在牛津，主教讥讽赫胥黎“祖上是猴子”，而后者平静地回应，他宁愿认一只猿做祖先，也不愿浪费才华去掩饰真理。观念的胜利从来不是一场辩论的胜负，而是证据的持续积累：遗传学、化石记录与分子生物学的每一次进展，都在为达尔文的框架添砖加瓦。今天，“带有变化的传衍”已成为生物学的基石。这个想法的旅程告诉我们：真理可能迟到，但它从不缺席于耐心的证据。
lessons.english: In 1859, On the Origin of Species was published, and the first printing of one thousand two hundred and fifty copies sold out on the same day. In this book Darwin hardly used the word "evolution"; what he used was "descent with modification". The caution of the wording reflected his situation: the idea that species could change struck directly at the popular system of belief. Criticism followed at once, and the most famous debate took place at Oxford, where the bishop mocked Huxley about having "an ape for a grandfather", and the latter replied calmly that he would rather claim an ape as an ancestor than waste his gifts in hiding the truth. The victory of an idea is never won in a single debate, but in the steady accumulation of evidence: every advance of genetics, of the fossil record and of molecular biology has added bricks to Darwin's frame. Today, "descent with modification" is the foundation stone of biology. The journey of this idea tells us that truth may be late, but it is never absent from patient evidence.

lessons.chinese: 语言学家估计，目前全球约七千种语言中，将近一半正面临消亡的危险。平均每两周，世界上就有一种语言失去最后一位使用者。语言的消逝往往悄无声息：一位老人离世，一种独特的世界观便随之合卷。每一种语言都携带独特的信息——关于植物药用的知识、关于航海的智慧、关于亲属关系的精细分类——这些信息大多没有文字记录，只存在于口口相传之中。语言消亡的原因并非语言本身：强势语言的挤压、教育政策的历史偏差、城市化带来的人口流动，共同切断了代际传递的链条。保护的努力在世界各地展开：新西兰的毛利语通过“语言巢”幼儿园重获生机，威尔士语借助媒体与法律稳住了阵脚。每一种语言的存续，都是人类想象力的一次保全。
lessons.english: Linguists estimate that of the roughly seven thousand languages in the world today, nearly half are in danger of dying. On average, once every two weeks a language loses its last speaker. A language usually dies in silence: an old person passes away, and a unique view of the world closes with them. Every language carries information of its own — knowledge of the medicinal use of plants, wisdom of navigation, fine classifications of kinship — and most of it has never been written down, existing only in the passing from mouth to mouth. The causes of a language's death are not the language itself: the pressure of dominant languages, the historical bias of education policies, and the movement of people brought by urbanisation have together cut the chain of transmission between generations. Efforts of protection are unfolding around the world: the Maori language of New Zealand has regained life through "language nest" kindergartens, and Welsh has held its ground with the help of media and law. The survival of every language is the preservation of one branch of human imagination.

lessons.chinese: 记忆常被比作录像机，忠实记录发生过的一切。神经科学的研究早已证明这一比喻的谬误：记忆不是回放，而是重建。每次回忆，大脑都会依据当下的情绪与环境，把记忆的碎片重新拼装一遍，细节在此过程中被悄悄改写。这解释了为什么目击者的证词可能出错，为什么童年的记忆往往模糊而不完整。更惊人的是，研究者成功地在实验室中为受试者植入了一段从未发生的童年记忆——在商场走失的细节，被四分之一的参与者“回忆”得绘声绘色。这些发现对司法系统意义重大：目击证人的自信与证词的准确并无必然联系。记忆的重建性并不可怕，它是大脑高效运转的代价。理解记忆如何工作，就是理解我们讲述的过去，有多少是事实，有多少是建筑。
lessons.english: Memory is often compared to a video recorder that faithfully stores everything that has happened. Research in neuroscience has long proved the metaphor wrong: memory is not replay but reconstruction. At every act of remembering, the brain assembles the fragments again according to the mood and environment of the present moment, and details are quietly rewritten in the process. This explains why the testimony of an eyewitness may be wrong, and why memories of childhood are often blurred and incomplete. More astonishing still, researchers have succeeded in implanting, in the laboratory, a childhood memory that never happened — the details of being lost in a shopping mall were "recalled" vividly by a quarter of the participants. These findings weigh heavily on the judicial system: the confidence of an eyewitness has no necessary connection with the accuracy of the testimony. The reconstructive nature of memory is not to be feared; it is the price the brain pays for working efficiently. To understand how memory works is to understand how much of the past we tell is fact, and how much is architecture.

lessons.chinese: 十六世纪，哥白尼把地球移出了宇宙的中心；二十世纪，哈勃发现银河系只是亿万星系中的一员；1990年，旅行者一号在六十亿公里外回望地球，拍下了那帧著名的“暗淡蓝点”。天文学的历史，几乎就是一部人类自我中心不断退潮的历史。萨根在那帧照片的启发下写道，所有人类的历史都发生在悬浮于阳光中的一粒微尘之上。这种视角带来的并非虚无，而是双重的清醒：一方面，我们的纷争在宇宙尺度上确实微不足道；另一方面，能够理解宇宙的器官，恰恰诞生在宇宙的尘埃里。每当天文望远镜把更深的星空带回人间，人类收获的与其说是知识，不如说是一种能力——在不被宇宙在乎的情况下，依然认真地在乎彼此。
lessons.english: In the sixteenth century, Copernicus moved the earth out of the centre of the universe; in the twentieth, Hubble discovered that the Milky Way is only one of billions of galaxies; and in 1990, Voyager 1, from six billion kilometres away, looked back and took the famous photograph of the "Pale Blue Dot". The history of astronomy is almost a history of the receding self-centredness of human beings. Inspired by that photograph, Carl Sagan wrote that all the history of the human race has taken place on a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam. The perspective brings not emptiness but a double sobriety: on one hand, our quarrels are truly trivial on the scale of the universe; on the other, the very organ that can understand the universe was born of its dust. Whenever a telescope brings a deeper sky back to the earth, what the human race gains is less knowledge than an ability — to care seriously about one another while not being cared about by the universe.

lessons.chinese: 疫苗是人类最伟大的公共卫生成就之一，天花因此被彻底消灭。然而，公众对疫苗的信任却始终脆弱。1998年，一篇将疫苗与自闭症相关联的论文引发恐慌，尽管该研究后来因数据造假被彻底撤稿，作者也被吊销行医执照，其造成的犹豫却延续至今。这一事件成为公共卫生领域的经典案例：错误信息的伤害远超其存在的时间。疫苗犹豫的成因是复杂的，对副作用的担忧、对医药企业的不信任、社交媒体的回音壁效应都在其中。应对之道不在于指责犹豫者愚昧，而在于理解犹豫的逻辑：风险是眼前的、具体的，而收益是延迟的、抽象的。重建信任需要的是透明的数据、耐心的对话，以及承认副作用存在的诚实。信任无法被命令，只能被赢得。
lessons.english: Vaccines are among the greatest achievements of public health — smallpox was wiped out because of them. Yet public trust in vaccines remains fragile. In 1998, a paper linking the vaccine to autism caused panic; though the study was later fully withdrawn for falsified data and its author struck off the medical register, the hesitation it caused continues to this day. This case has become a classic lesson of public health: the harm of false information lasts far longer than the life of the information itself. The causes of vaccine hesitation are complex — the worry over side effects, the distrust of pharmaceutical companies, and the echo-chamber effect of social media all play their parts. The response does not lie in calling the hesitant foolish, but in understanding the logic of hesitation: the risk is present and concrete, while the benefit is delayed and abstract. To rebuild trust, what is needed is transparent data, patient dialogue, and the honesty of admitting that side effects exist. Trust cannot be commanded; it can only be earned.

lessons.chinese: 基因编辑技术让人类第一次拥有了“改写生命之书”的精确工具。它的医学前景令人振奋：镰状细胞贫血等遗传病患者在接受治疗后病情显著缓解，农业领域的抗病作物也已进入试验田。但这项技术最尖锐的争议在于生殖细胞的编辑——这样的改动将遗传给后代，永久地写入人类基因库。2018年的一起事件把争论推向顶点：一位研究者宣布两名编辑过基因的婴儿诞生，全球科学界同声谴责，他本人也被判刑。科学界的共识是清晰的：基础研究应当继续，临床应用必须止步于体细胞。争论的本质是哲学性的：父母是否有权决定孩子的基因？消除疾病与“增强”的界线在哪里？生命之书可以被编辑，但执笔的资格与边界，必须由全人类共同书写。
lessons.english: Gene editing has given human beings, for the first time, a precise tool to "edit the book of life". Its medical prospects are exciting: patients of sickle-cell anaemia have been greatly relieved after treatment, and crops resistant to disease have entered trial fields. The sharpest controversy of the technology, however, lies in the editing of reproductive cells — such changes would be inherited by descendants and written permanently into the gene pool of mankind. An event in 2018 pushed the debate to its height: a researcher announced the birth of two gene-edited babies, the scientific world condemned it with one voice, and he himself was sentenced. The consensus of science is clear: basic research should continue, while clinical use must stop at somatic cells. The essence of the debate is philosophical: do parents have the right to decide the genes of their children? And where is the line between removing a disease and "enhancing" a life? The book of life may be edited, but the qualification to hold the pen, and the boundary of what may be written, must be composed by all mankind together.

lessons.chinese: 十九世纪的数学家研究数论时，常被问及“这有什么用”。他们中的硬汉派回应道：“一个理论的价值，恰恰在于没人能说出它的用处。”一百多年后，正是这些“无用”的理论成了现代世界的地基：数论支撑着网络加密，非欧几何铺垫了广义相对论，群论藏在粒子物理的深处。科学史学家把这一现象称为“无用的回报”：基础研究的价值，往往在数十年后才显现，且几乎从不出现在当初的研究计划里。这一规律对今天的科研管理构成挑战：当经费越来越倾向于“可转化的成果”，谁来为看似无用的好奇心买单？历史给出的答案令人不安又充满希望：无法预知哪个无用想法会改变世界，所以唯一安全的策略，是让许多无用想法活着。
lessons.english: In the nineteenth century, mathematicians studying the theory of numbers were often asked, "What is the use of it?" The tougher ones would answer: "The value of a theory lies exactly in the fact that no one can tell its use." More than a century later, it is precisely these "useless" theories that have become the foundation of the modern world: the theory of numbers supports the encryption of networks, non-Euclidean geometry prepared the ground for general relativity, and group theory lies hidden in the depths of particle physics. Historians of science call this phenomenon "the return of the useless": the value of basic research usually appears only after decades, and almost never within the original plan of the research. This law challenges the management of research today: when funding leans more and more towards "transformable results", who will pay for curiosity that seems useless? The answer of history is unsettling and hopeful at once: since no one can tell which useless idea will change the world, the only safe strategy is to let many useless ideas stay alive.

lessons.chinese: 时间是最公平的资源，也是最难定义的对象。人类测量时间的历史，是一部精度不断打败想象的历史：从日晷的影子到原子钟的振荡，精度的提升跨越了十几个数量级。今天的原子钟数十亿年才差一秒，全球定位系统正依赖这种精度运转。但测量的进步也带来了哲学的追问：时间究竟是宇宙的属性，还是人类为理解变化而发明的概念？物理学的回答耐人寻味：在相对论中，时间的快慢取决于速度与引力——卫星上的时钟与地面确实不同步。爱因斯坦的同事曾说，我们无法定义时间，但我们知道那是什么。测量时间的努力最终揭示的，或许不是时间的本质，而是人类心智面对永恒时的不甘：既然无法停留，那就把流逝刻画到极限。
lessons.english: Time is the fairest of all resources and the hardest object to define. The history of measuring time is a history of precision defeating imagination: from the shadow of a sundial to the oscillation of an atomic clock, the rise of accuracy spans more than a dozen orders of magnitude. An atomic clock today errs by one second in billions of years, and the global positioning system depends on exactly this accuracy. But the progress of measuring also brings a philosophical question: is time a property of the universe, or a concept invented by human beings to understand change? The answer of physics is thought-provoking: in the theory of relativity, the pace of time depends on speed and gravity — the clock on a satellite truly differs from a clock on the ground. A colleague of Einstein once said that we cannot define time, but we know what it is.
