lessons.chinese: 节前三天，艾草整车的进了集市，全镇开始隐隐闻见药香。外婆买了两大抱，比我们家一扇门需要的多得多，我们拖着一道绿色的影子穿过巷子回家。艾草上了街上每一扇门楣，用红线捆着，梢头朝下。问她为什么，她给的是那句老话：熏走五毒，也让门变得诚实。“挂了艾的门，”她说，“是告诉病气，门后有一户还醒着的人家。”艾的气味在我们手上留了好几天，苦，干净，对什么都不害怕。晌午大人们把同一种草煮了喝，孩子们得到一句许诺，说秋天会有胆气。我记住的不是故事，而是它给的许可：一年一度，我们把野草挂上门楣，房子为此赞许我们。如今镇上买的是塑料的把束，存得住年头，却没有意思；风从它们旁边过，找不到可以带走的气味。
lessons.english: Three days before the festival, the mugwort appeared in the market in whole carts, and the town began to smell faintly of medicine. Grandmother bought two great armfuls, more than our door needed, and we walked home through the lanes trailing a green shadow. The stalks went up over every door on the street, bound with red thread, tips turned down. Asked why, she gave the old answer: to wave off the five poisons, and to make the door honest. "A door with mugwort," she said, "tells the sickness there is a household still awake behind it." The smell stayed on our hands for days afterward, bitter, clean, and entirely unafraid of anything. At noon the adults drank the same plant boiled, and the children were promised courage in the fall. What I remember is not the story but the permission it gave: once a year we hung wild weeds over the door, and the house approved of us for it. Towns now buy plastic bundles that keep for years and mean nothing; the wind, passing them, finds no smell to carry inside.

lessons.chinese: 月饼到我们家，像亲戚上门：一盒一盒，多得远过我们的胃口，对我们来说还略微贵重。它们流转几个星期，从父亲的单位到伯父家，从伯父家到邻居，从邻居又回到我们家，每转一圈老一点。地道的月饼皮薄，皮在掌心里碎成褐色的一小片一小片，非用手接住不可。里面有一颗像被捉住的小月亮的蛋黄，还有莲蓉，甜得不容争辩。父亲把每一只精确地切成四块，不管有没有人分这一块。妹妹出生那年他切成五块，第五块给了祖父的照片。没有人觉得这奇怪；饭桌照它一贯的样子让出位置。如今这滋味在任何城市都能复制，分毫不差，吃它也不再费一季的等待；这是一种所得，也是一种所失。我终于明白，不缺的月饼只是一块点心；月亮从来不在馅里。
lessons.english: Mooncakes arrived at our house the way visiting relatives do: in boxes, in numbers far beyond our appetite, and slightly expensive for us. They circulated for weeks, from my father's office to my uncle's, from my uncle's to the neighbors, from the neighbors back to us, older with every round. The proper ones were thin-skinned, and the skin broke in brown flakes that had to be caught with the palm. Inside there was a yolk like a small caught moon, and lotus paste, sweet past all arguing. My father cut each one precisely into quarters, whether or not anyone shared the quarter. The year my sister was born he cut one into five, and the fifth piece went to the photograph of the grandfather. Nobody thought this strange; the table made room the way it did. The taste is reproducible now in any city, and exact, and the eating of it no longer costs a season of waiting, which is a gain, and a loss. A mooncake without scarcity, I finally understood, is only a pastry; the moon was never in the filling.

lessons.chinese: 庙会一夜之间就搭了起来，像天气一样，散后留下的是踩烂的薄荷气味和一只不知谁丢的鞋。它跟着春天的香火来，香火给它发了许可：庙会是一场学会了变戏法的祈祷。头一天早上起，几条巷子就织成一匹声音的布：锣、抻糖、猴子脖子上的链子、一顶戏帽的竞价。外婆为香而去，回来时带着一支哨子、一把木梳，和一个议论某人香灰厚薄的故事。孩子们是冲捏糖人的去的，他四十秒抻出一条龙，你要是吃了，他便像受了人身侮辱。那里有理发师的椅子，有斗蛐蛐的赌棚，大殿背后的阴凉里还有一位算命先生，他的长队从来不见变短。钱一小枚一小枚地离开我们，没有留下配得上名字的懊悔。傍晚灯笼在铁丝上歪歪地亮起来，庙会用散落的稻草和收场的锣鼓道晚安。之后庙里静了一天，像待客之后的人家，自己打扫自己，并且饶恕了我们。
lessons.english: The fair set up overnight, the way weather does, and left behind trampled mint smell and one lost shoe. It came with the spring incense, and the incense gave it permission: a fair is a prayer that has learned to juggle. From the first morning the lanes were a single fabric of sounds: gongs, sugar being stretched, a monkey's chain, the auction of an opera hat. My grandmother went for the incense and came back with a whistle, a comb and a story about the thickness of someone's incense ash. We children went for the sugar-figure man, who spun a dragon in forty seconds and looked personally insulted if you ate it. There was a barber's chair, a gambling den for crickets and, in the shade behind the hall, a fortune teller whose queue never shortened. Money left us in coins of small denomination and left no regret worth the name. In the evening the lanterns came up crooked on their wires, and the fair said its goodnights in falling straw and beaten drums. The temple kept one day of silence after, like a house after guests, sweeping itself and forgiving us.

lessons.chinese: 腊月初八，厨房自己宣布了一次小小的济世，家里每一只罐子都交了税。大米、小米、红豆、桂圆、红枣、花生、莲子，还有顶架上一纸包的果脯，天亮前全进了锅。外婆主持下料的次序，次序就是教义：硬的先下，甜的后下，搅动不许着急。粥用一早晨的时间变成它自己。邻里整天隔着巷子换碗，还回来的碗从不空着，到傍晚，整条巷子都靠着粥的经济学运转。我们被告知，穷人当年吃它是出于无奈，如今我们吃它是出于记性，记性也是一种敬意。按她的吩咐，头一碗先端到门口，给鸟雀，给开饭前经过的每一个人。我喜欢勺子在里面立住一秒的那一刻，直得像一根小小的柱子，然后慢慢躺倒。一年里其余的日子，锅煮汤，罐子各过各的日子；只有那个早晨，食品柜和自己讲和。
lessons.english: On the eighth of the twelfth month, the kitchen declared a small economy of its own, and every jar in the house paid its tax. Rice, millet, red beans, longan, dates, peanuts, lotus seeds and, from the top shelf, a twist of candied fruit went into the pot before dawn. My grandmother presided over the ordering, and the ordering was doctrine: hard things first, sweet things last, and the stir never hurried. The porridge took the morning to become itself. Neighbors exchanged bowls across the lane all day, and a returned bowl never came back empty; by evening the lane ran on porridge economics. We were told the poor once ate this out of necessity, and now we ate it out of memory, which is a kind of respect. By her instruction the first bowl went to the door, to the birds and to whoever passed before we ate. I liked the moment when the spoon stood up in it for a second, straight as a little pillar, and slowly lay down. The rest of the year the pot held soup and the jars held their separate lives; only that morning did the pantry agree with itself.

lessons.chinese: 年前的纸市是一片红，全镇从当中走过，呼吸着墨香。春联买得到现成的，我们家却守着老分工：祖父写，父亲选词，我拿着纸条的那一头。词要新、要吉利、要对得纹丝不差；两扇门像市场上的货那样互相掂量。祖父半开玩笑地说，一个字写坏了能压一年；他每一笔都写得像纸在听。浆糊用笤帚刷上门框；纸条贴歪了，站到街当中看一眼，再重贴。门楣上的横批用四个字总结这一家的指望，为这四个字我们站了很久。邻居们像读文章一样读彼此的门，关于书法的恭维是当年的头一笔进项。初八那天风掀起左联的上角，外婆说，它听见了。词随浆糊年年揭下来，可是我发觉，给两扇门掂量的那点心思，留下了。
lessons.english: The paper market before the New Year was a field of red, and the town walked through it breathing ink. Couplets could be bought ready-written, but our family kept the old division of labor: grandfather wrote, father chose the words, and I held the far end of the strip. The words had to be new, hopeful and exactly balanced; the two doors were weighed against each other like market goods. A badly written character could sink the year, grandfather said, half joking, and he wrote every stroke as if the paper were listening. Paste went on with a broom; the strips went up crooked, were judged from the middle of the street, and went up again. The horizontal scroll above carried the household's hopes in four characters, and we stood a long time choosing it. Neighbors read one another's doors like pages, and compliments about calligraphy were the year's first currency. On the eighth day the wind took the top corner of the left strip, and grandmother said it had heard us. The words come off with the paste each year, but the weighing of the two doors, I find, stayed with me.

lessons.chinese: 戏台在村口，隔着晒谷场与庙对望，这两个物件互相看了四百年。一年两回唱戏，播种一回，收成一回，老榆树上一张红纸就是告示。头天夜里，长凳用绳子写上名字占了地方，那是一整张由孩子们谈判出来的地图。锣在黄昏敲响，声音顺着每条巷子淌下去，像水找平。唱我们一概不懂，情节却全懂：绕场一周便是赶路，水袖遮脸便是伤心。奸臣挨嘘，蒙冤的老臣有人在台下高声护着，到第三本，满场都比皇帝明白。祖父说，这就是戏的妙处：这一晚上，台下的个个都比台上的人高明。雨让戏停在半句上，长凳往檐下跑，嘴里还争着情节。戏台如今是文物了，修过，围起来；还满座的日子仍是播种和收成，唱的仍是老戏文，这么说，这故事到底留住了它的观众。
lessons.english: The stage stood at the village mouth, facing the temple across the grain yard, and the two had watched each other for four hundred years. Plays came twice a year, at sowing and harvest, announced by a red paper on the old elm. The night before, benches claimed places with ropes and names, an entire geography negotiated by children. The gong started at dusk, and the sound went down every lane like water finding its level. We understood nothing of the singing and everything of the plot: a walk in a circle meant a journey, a sleeve across the face meant grief. The villain was booed, the wronged minister defended in loud whispers, and by act three the whole audience knew more than the emperor. That is the pleasure of opera, grandfather said: for one night everyone on the ground is wiser than the man on the stage. Rain stopped the plays mid-line, and the benches ran for the eaves still arguing about the plot. The stage is a heritage site now, restored and roped off; the nights it fills are still sowing and harvest, the old plots, which means the story kept its audience after all.

lessons.chinese: 到我母亲出嫁，花轿已经是一件借来的东西，归公家保管办喜事用，八个抬轿的男人是为一顿饭抬的。红漆让太阳晒成了玫色，描着金牡丹，嵌着小镜子，一路朝巷子里撒火星。她的鞋由婚姻美满的妇人们缝成，好让运气能说是在针脚里住着。她在天亮前离开娘家，按着分寸哭，分寸不够时，姑母们替她补上。巷子成了一条脸的走廊；孩子们跑在轿夫前头，像引水的小鱼。母亲多年后告诉我们，轿里有一只脚凳、一把木梳、一篮栗子和枣，取词里的音，谐着“早”和“起”。轿夫一路唱歌，词没有定本，现编出来，为的是羞一羞婆家那条街，让他们把饭做好些。到了婆家门口，鞭炮炸响，轿帘掀起，一个五岁的男孩递给她一双新筷子。那顶轿后来又抬过三位新娘；然后卡车来了，运气去了运气去的地方。
lessons.english: By my mother's wedding the sedan was already a borrowed thing, kept by the commune for occasions, carried by eight men for the sake of the meal. It was red lacquer gone rose in the sun, with gilt peonies and small mirrors that threw sparks along the lane. Her shoes were made by women who were happily married, so the luck could be said to live in the stitching. She left her mother's house before light, crying in the correct amounts, and the aunts corrected the amounts when they fell short. The lane was a corridor of faces; children ran ahead of the carriers like pilot fish. Inside, my mother told us later, there was a stool, a comb and a basket of chestnuts and dates, their words rhyming with early and rise. The carriers sang the whole way, songs with no fixed words, invented to shame the groom's street into cooking better. At the groom's door the firecrackers cracked, the curtain lifted, and a boy of five handed her a pair of new chopsticks. That chair carried three brides after her; then the trucks came, and the luck went wherever luck goes.

lessons.chinese: 立春，历书上写着春天开始的那一天，在我童年从不曾像过春天，而这恰恰是它的本意。它落在二月初，落在一个灰茬子和风的世界里，风从田野上带着棱角刮过来。可这一天照过不误：历书那一页画了圈，每人跟前卷一张春饼，萝卜要嚼出声来吃。这风俗叫咬春，是个讲道理的仪式：趁季节还不存在就把它吃下去，用嘴逼它兑现。老人们照样去看柳树，一个个报着芽的消息，庄重得像边境上的查验官。什么也没变；这就是结论，而结论年年当作新闻记上一笔。我后来懂了，希望先是一门功课，然后才是一种心情，历书是它的操场。立春之后的某个星期里，不经任何仪式，光变稠了，泥有了光，空气不再扎人。没有人宣布；年是守了我们二月里替它订下的约。
lessons.english: Lichun, the day the calendar says spring begins, never once looked like spring in my childhood, and that is exactly the point of it. It fell in early February, on a world of gray stubble and wind that came off the fields with an edge. But the day was kept: the calendar page was circled, a spring pancake was rolled at each place, and radish was eaten to the sound of it crunching. Biting the spring, the custom is called, and it is a sensible ceremony: to eat the season before it exists, to force the issue by the mouth. The old men checked the willows anyway, and reported each bud with the gravity of inspectors at a border crossing. Nothing had changed; that was the finding, and it was entered every year as if new. Hope, I understood later, is a discipline before it is a mood, and the calendar is its gymnasium. Somewhere in the weeks after Lichun, without ceremony, the light thickened, the mud acquired a shine, and the air stopped stinging. No one announced it; the year had simply kept the appointment we made for it in February.

lessons.chinese: 那顿饭要做三天，而按设计，吃它要用四个钟头。厨房像一个战时的小国在运转：顶火蒸笼，后火煨汤，我父亲守着那条鱼。必须有鱼，还必须剩下不吃，好让来年知道富余是什么滋味。必须有一只鸡，整鸡，带头端上来，带着一种关于晚饭从哪里来的老式诚实。饺子挨近午夜才包；其中一只藏了硬币，找到它的事被讨论得像一场查账。席上要把账结清：几斤米的账、人情账，一样样点出来，一笔笔饶过，好让新年不带行李。孩子们获准一杯，掺了水；大人在老位置讲同样三个故事。午夜街上礼貌地炸开了，我们出去看别人家的花火；看别人的，永远是更好的一场。然后最后一道凉菜端进来；多年后我认出它就是时间本身，端给满桌，无论饿不饿，都得吃。
lessons.english: The cooking of that dinner took three days, and the eating of it, by design, took four hours. The kitchen ran like a small state at war: steamer on the top ring, soup at the back, my father guarding the fish. There had to be a fish, and it had to be left unfinished, so the year ahead would know what abundance felt like. There had to be a chicken, whole, presented with its head, an old-fashioned honesty about where dinner comes from. Dumplings were folded as midnight drew near; one hid a coin, and the finding of it was discussed with the gravity of an audit. At the table, accounts were settled: every debt of rice or favor was named and forgiven, so the new year would carry no luggage. The children were permitted one cup, watered, and the adults told the same three stories at the same places. At midnight the streets exploded politely, and we went out to watch other people's fireworks; other people's are always the better show. Then the last dish came in cold; years later I know it for time itself, served to the whole table, eaten hungry or not.

lessons.chinese: 正月十五夜里，全镇一起造光，各家拿各自的手艺交同一份作业。兔子、莲花船、公鸡，偶尔还有一架有雄心的飞机：灯笼被孩子们举在棍子上走过街，大人反复嘱咐走慢些。我们家是莲花，十二片铁丝的花瓣，一截蜡烛，花瓣的影子落在地上，随我们走动而走动。全镇敲着鼓，点心铺子当街卖元宵，面粉在灯光里飞，像当年的头一场雪。每一盏灯都是一家人的耐心在公开场合亮相，晌午还嘴硬的父亲们跟在后头，手里牵着线。谜语贴在南门大灯笼上；猜中一条，得一块肥皂或一支铅笔，这是整个晚上的经济。风是一天里唯一的敌人；输给风的灯，哀悼的时间恰好等于走回家的路。最后蜡烛一起矮下去，街一户一户地黑，像一座城分段睡去。长辈说，要举自己的灯，别光看别人的；可我们个个都看了，而街因此更好。
lessons.english: On the fifteenth night the whole town made light, every family answering one assignment with a different hand. Rabbits, lotus boats, roosters, an occasional airplane: the lanterns walked the streets held by children ordered to walk slowly. Ours was a lotus, twelve wire petals and a candle stub, throwing petal shadows that moved as we moved. The town drummed, the shops sold yuanxiao out of doors, and the flour flew in the lamplight like the first snow of the year. Every lantern was the family's patience shown in public, and fathers who had sneered at noon walked behind, holding the string. Riddles were pasted on the big lantern at the south gate; a solve earned a soap or a pencil, the whole evening's economy. The wind was the day's only enemy; a lantern lost to it was mourned exactly as long as the walk home. At the end the candles guttered together, and the streets went out one family at a time, a town going to sleep in sections. Carry your light, the elders said, do not look at other people's; and yet we all looked, and the streets were better for it.

lessons.title_en: A Letter to My Younger Brother
lessons.chinese:
弟弟：拆信见字如晤，只是见到的这张脸，恐怕比站台上的瘦了。
你写道，考试临近，一想到它手就发冷；听一个坐在你那个位置上的人说几句。我落榜过一回，就是你学走路那年，天没有塌；它只是让我再试一次，天要的从来只有这个。考前一晚不要用功；去走一走，慢慢地吃点东西，像世上没有仇人那样睡觉。考场上脑子空了的时候，记住，监考的也不是你的仇人；不过是个抱着一摞卷子、腰疼着的人。字一个一个写，像父亲教我们的那样；让第一个丑，第二个会出于羞愧写得好些。考完坐慢车回家；厨房嫌自己不够挤，果酱也在等你。考上也好，考不上也好，你还是那个叫得出河堤上每一棵树名字的男孩；要紧的东西没有一样是在一个考场里决定的。
兄　明远
灯下
lessons.english: Dear brother, I open your letter and see your face, thinner, I am afraid, than it was at the station.

lessons.chinese:
儿：你寄的柿子完好到了，整条街都吃了。
我说整条街，因为你父亲没等我开封，先提着盒子走了四户人家，男人夸耀儿子，向来这个方式。我们都好。你父亲的咳到第二杯茶为止；他走到磨坊再走回来，为的是向磨坊证明什么。这个季节不要寄钱；柿树付了窗纸钱，窗纸是冬天要的账。你要我写的小消息如下：井又深了一拃，李家姑娘十月嫁了，稻草人身上那件褂子是我的，我要讨回来。关于你的考试，我只说一句：你父亲头一回也没考上；我一直告诉他你不知道；现在你知道了。围巾戴上；南方暖身子，冷性子。饭要按钟点吃；志向自己不开火。灯矮了，我的字越来越大；在母亲的信里，这就是说，能回来就回来。
母亲
初霜那日
lessons.english: My son, the persimmons you sent arrived whole, and the whole street has eaten of them.

lessons.title_en: Three Entries from a Travel Diary
lessons.chinese:
四月初四，小雨。搭货船下行，甲板上与猪、煤，和一家去送葬的人同行。晌午丧家请我们喝酒，比酒席还好，一位船工说，说得满船人笑完又静。雨点打篷是最好想事的声音，而我想了一下午，什么也没想。
四月初七，晴。上午攀上崖顶的庙，大钟无声，僧人已去，一扇门靠一根草绳把守。看庙的乡人用手掌根替我们撞了一记钟，钟声铺到河面上，像一段被记起的事。他不肯收钱，我便扫了院子；我们站了一会儿，都说这是一口好钟。
四月十二，风。走山路回家；岭上松涛让风声传了几里，一根不断的长音。我如今明白旅人从前为何要靠钟引路：一国用声音告诉你它的边界，比眼睛承认得早。
lessons.english: The fourth of April, light rain. Down the river by cargo boat, sharing the deck with pigs, coal and a family going to a funeral. At noon the funeral family shared their wine with us, better than the feast, a boatman said, which made everyone laugh and then go quiet. Rain on the canvas is the best sound for thinking, and I thought of nothing the whole afternoon.

lessons.chinese: 岁末最后一晚，雪将停。晚饭后誊完家用账，像读一部陌生人的传记那样读它，每一页转折都吃惊。茶十一笔；药四笔；三月里一笔，照了一张相，我全不记得，可见有人笑过，而我把那个笑弄丢了。钱写的传记比我写的真，只是它什么都不懂。黄昏父亲来电话，说塘冻得能传声，他走到塘心，试了试这一年。我问那可安全；他说今年的冰是诚实的。窗外黑了，灯老了一岁；街对面一扇和我一样的窗里点着和我一样的灯，我竟觉得安慰。新的一年带什么来都好，它带来的会是一个扫净了门阶、研满了墨的人，人能预备的也就这些。放猫出门，封好炉火，睡得像块石头，让正月去和雪开始它那场长久的辩论。
lessons.english: The last evening of the year, snow ending. After supper I copied the household accounts and read them the way one reads a biography of strangers, surprised at each turn. Eleven entries for tea; four for medicine; one, in March, for a photograph I do not remember taking, which means someone smiled and I have lost the smile. Money writes a truer diary than I do, and understands nothing. At dusk father called to say the pond had frozen hard enough for his voice to carry across it, and he walked out to the middle to test the year. I asked whether that was safe; he said the ice this year was honest. The window is dark, the lamp is a year older, and across the street a window like mine holds a lamp like mine, and I find that comforting. Whatever the new year brings, it will bring it to a man with a swept doorstep and a full inkstone, which is all one can prepare. Put out the cat, bank the fire, sleep like a stone, and let January begin its long argument with the snow.

lessons.chinese: 编辑说，序应当解释这本书；我把志向放低些，只解释它的写作。这些文字写在十一个冬天里，写在别种工作的缝隙中，也就是写作生涯真正的国土上。它们起初没有被计划成一本书；它们自己排好了队，像家具安排一间屋子，某个早晨，屋子开始接待生人。读者在这里会找到一些小东西：一本词典，一条渡船，燕子，一件布衫，一场烧。我为小东西作的辩护用的是老理由：大题目要么走到小题目门口，要么根本不来。从来没有人靠一篇论战争的文章被劝出战争；可是一个把渡船读得好的人，可以被托付一座桥。忍心删的句子我都删了，这花了十一个冬天，也教会了我这本书是什么。如果有一篇挣得重读，那是题目扣住了它；题目在我之前许多年就被选好，在我之后许多年还会被选。余下的错误，照惯例该怪灯；我高兴地报告，我那盏灯是无辜的。
lessons.english: A preface, my editor says, should explain the book; I lower the ambition and explain the writing of it. These pieces were written over eleven winters, in the gaps of other work, in the true country of a writing life. They were not planned as a book; they arranged themselves, the way furniture arranges a room, and one morning the room admitted strangers. The reader will find small things here: a dictionary, a ferry, swallows, a blouse, a fever. I defend the small things on the old grounds: the large subjects arrive at the door of the small ones or not at all. No one was ever argued out of a war by an essay on war; but a man who reads well about a ferry may be trusted with a bridge. I cut every sentence I could bear to cut, which took eleven winters and taught me what the book was. If a piece earns a second reading, the subject held it; the subjects were chosen long before me and will be chosen long after. For the errors that remain, the custom is to blame the lamp; my lamp, I am glad to say, is innocent.

lessons.title_en: Old Photographs of a Small Town
lessons.chinese: 这本序所介绍的影集，像它的同类一样，是在抽屉的夹层里发现的，外面包着防了几十年蠹虫的纸。里面收九十一张照片，拍的是一座已经不再以那个形状存在、却又全然以那个形状存在着的城；这就是照片平常的奇迹。最早的底片照的是雪中的晒谷场，从拍照人的影子看，摄于一个冬日午后三点半。里面有婚礼，有丧事，还有一个人被照了两次：一次在铺子门口，一次在棺材旁边。无名者与有名者的比例是四比一，因此这本影集恰好也是历史收留我们的方式的写真。我按原样付印，污渍、指印，一并在内；污渍是城的天气，指印是我们大家的。照片证明有东西在光里站过；它证明不了有人还记得。在这两件事之间，曾经住着一整座城；这本书合不上这道缝，至少量了量它。我以档案员的身份请求：看慢些；死者已经被催赶得够多了。
lessons.english: The album this preface introduces was found, like most of its kind, in the double bottom of a drawer, wrapped against the moths of decades. It holds ninety-one photographs of a town that no longer exists in that form and exists entirely in that form, which is the ordinary miracle of photographs. The earliest plate shows the grain yard under snow, taken, by the shadow of the photographer, at half past three on a winter afternoon. There are weddings in it, there are funerals, and there is one man photographed twice, once outside his shop and once outside his coffin. The unnamed outnumber the named by four to one, and the album is thus a fair portrait of how history actually keeps us. I have printed them as they are, stains, thumb marks and all; the stains are the town's weather, and the thumb marks are ours. A photograph proves that something stood in the light; it cannot prove that anyone remembers. Between those two facts a whole town used to live, and this book, which cannot close the gap, can at least measure it. Look slowly, the archivist in me asks; the dead were hurried enough.

lessons.title_en: A Few Words before the Translation
lessons.chinese: 翻译常被比作在两个村子之间挑水；这个比方错得让人高兴。水到的时候还是水；语言从来不是。译者真正挑的不是水，是渴，是当初有人朝井边走过去的那个原因。本书各篇入选，因为它们在两种语言里都渴得体面：它们在中文里想说，到了英文里还想再说一遍。原文素净处我拒绝添彩；原文拥挤处我由它拥挤，因为忠实是一种待客之道，不是一种算术。读者会遇上不肯翻译的门：认输的韵，出了国又不来信的双关。在这样的门前，我做了主人所做的事：添一把椅子，继续谈话；意思通常总能另外找到座位。我的守则是一句老话：先译句子，再译那个人；两者不一致时，问那个人。如果这里的英文还有一点活气，功劳属于早已过世的作者们；毛病是最近才搬进来的，都签了名。
lessons.english: Translation is often compared to carrying water between two villages; the comparison is wrong in a flattering way. Water arrives the same; language never does. What the translator actually carries is not the water but the thirst, the reason someone reached for the well in the first place. The pieces in this book were chosen because they thirst well in both languages: they want, in Chinese, to be said, and they want, in English, to be said again. Where the original is spare I have refused to decorate; where it is crowded I have let it crowd, for fidelity is a manner of hospitality, not of arithmetic. The reader will meet doors that will not translate: the rhyme that resigned, the pun that emigrated and sent no letters. At such doors I have done what hosts do, set another chair and gone on talking; meaning can usually be seated elsewhere. My rule has been an old one: translate the sentence, then translate the man, and when the two disagree, ask the man. If the English here lives at all, the credit belongs to writers long dead; the faults moved in recently and signed their names.

lessons.title_en: A Reply to a Young Reader
lessons.chinese:
青年朋友：你三月十日的信辗转了三个地址到我手里，我读了两遍，第二遍慢些。
你问，会写文章是天生还是学来；这问题比我们两个人都老，而诚实的回答是：像学走路，一点指点，大量跌倒，外加一块不计较的地面。你还寄来三页文字，问它们有没有苗头。有的：耳朵不坏，习惯不好，那习惯就是伸手去够漂亮词，总是先于够准确的词。漂亮尽管漂亮，但要付账；用错地方的漂亮词，花的是读者的信任，而我们这一行只此一家银行。读的要多于写的，写的要多于寄的；邮件等得起。至于鼓励，我的鼓励只有这一句：你注意到了鹭的肩。大多数人看见一只鸟；你看见的是一只正在干活的鸟。把这只眼睛留住，慢慢喂它；十年后再给我写信，还托那三个地址。到那时我会更慢，也更高兴。
你的
一个老人
lessons.english: Dear young friend, yours of the tenth of March reached me by way of three addresses, and I read it twice, the second time slower.

lessons.title_en: A Letter to Myself in Ten Years
lessons.chinese:
致这张桌子十年后的主人：我是那个想不出标题、正要封火的人；只汇报这一年。
这是个平常的年份，我认定这是最高的夸奖：没进医院，没有越过晚饭还不停的架，李树头一回结果。我记得你担心：房子，那本书，还有是不是太迟。汇报吧，不管你是谁：屋顶修了没有，书写完了没有、还是体面地死了，还有太迟是不是照例只是一句谣言。屋子要是还漏，你要知道，漏比房子早，形状是一个停不下在心里翻修房间的人。那本书要是既没写完也没死，替我转告它：未完成是合法的住址；有人一住多年，有些还住得不坏。至于太迟，你会注意到，它是一扇只从你站的这一侧才打得开的门。火低了，纸用完了。无论你成了什么人，善待我这个人；李树是他替你浇的。
同一双手
仍在这扇窗下
lessons.english: To the owner of this desk, ten years on, I am the one who cannot think of a title and is about to bank the fire; I report the year.

lessons.chinese: 书成了，成了的书做的第一件事，就是带着一点惊讶回头看造它的人。六十课，六十扇小门；木匠数着它们，有点不敢信这条街。我欠读者一笔账：这几百页是为什么写的。它们是给手的，不是给眼的：给那个把中文译回去、又在语言的缝隙里认出自己尚未拥有的东西之确切形状的读者。那道缝隙是我所知唯一诚实的老师；它从不夸奖，只负责展示，而它展示得最好的地方，是渡船和燕子那些句子，那里赌注小，道理大。如果练习起了作用，读者从此会对自己的流利略起疑心，而这正是精确的开始。我写这些文字，像给一位敬重的人出考题：难到对得起他，好到留得住他。六十扇门关上了；这条街，但愿还在走。而若在前方某处，有个读者停在某句中文面前，不带任何书，就看见英文在它背后，像一扇窗里的灯，那么这个木匠就可以放下工具，等到明天。
lessons.english: The book is done, and the first thing done books do is look back at their makers with mild surprise. Sixty lessons, sixty little doors; the carpenter counts them and cannot quite believe the street. I owe the reader an accounting of what these pages were for. They were for the hand, not the eye: for the reader who translates back and finds, in the gap between languages, the exact shape of what he does not yet own. That gap is the only honest teacher I know; it never praises, it only shows, and it shows best in sentences about ferrymen and swallows, where stakes are low and truth is high. If the exercises have done their work, the reader will now distrust his fluency slightly, which is the beginning of precision. I wrote them the way one sets examination papers for a person one respects: hard enough to honor him, kind enough to keep him. Sixty doors close; the street, I hope, goes on. And if somewhere ahead a reader pauses over a Chinese sentence and, without any book, sees the English behind it like a lamp in a window, this carpenter may put down his tools until morning.
